questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which statement about Cisco TrustSec Security Group Tags (SGTs) is correct?

options.A: SGTs are assigned based on the destination IP address only, never based on user or device identity information
options.B: SGTs are only usable with MACsec encryption enabled
options.C: SGTs replace the need for VLANs entirely
options.D: SGTs classify traffic and enable policy enforcement independent of IP addressing or topology

questions.explanation_es: Las SGT (Security Group Tags) de TrustSec clasifican el tráfico según el rol/identidad del usuario o dispositivo, permitiendo aplicar políticas de segmentación independientemente de la IP o la topología física. No dependen de VLANs ni requieren MACsec.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: At which layer does MACsec (802.1AE) provide encryption?

options.A: Layer 2, encrypting Ethernet frames hop-by-hop between adjacent devices
options.B: Layer 4, encrypting TCP/UDP segments
options.C: Layer 3, encrypting the IP header and payload
options.D: Layer 7, encrypting application data end-to-end regardless of how many Layer 2 hops the traffic crosses

questions.explanation_es: MACsec opera en Capa 2 y cifra los frames Ethernet salto por salto (hop-by-hop) entre dispositivos adyacentes directamente conectados. Cada enlace tiene su propia asociación de seguridad; NO es cifrado end-to-end como IPsec.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: A network has MACsec enabled between Switch A and Switch B, and separately between Switch B and Switch C. If a frame travels from A to C through B, what happens to the encryption?

options.A: The frame is encrypted only once at the source and decrypted only at the final destination, exactly like end-to-end IPsec would behave
options.B: The frame remains encrypted with the same key throughout the path
options.C: MACsec cannot be used across more than one hop
options.D: The frame is decrypted at B, processed, and re-encrypted with a different session key before forwarding to C

questions.explanation_es: Como MACsec es hop-by-hop, en cada salto el frame se descifra, se procesa/conmuta en texto claro dentro del dispositivo, y se vuelve a cifrar con una asociación de seguridad distinta antes del siguiente salto. No hay una sola sesión cifrada de extremo a extremo.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What is the role of the Security Association Protocol (SAP) or MKA (MACsec Key Agreement) in a MACsec deployment?

options.A: It performs deep packet inspection on encrypted traffic without ever needing to decrypt it first at any point
options.B: It assigns SGTs to endpoints
options.C: It negotiates and manages the encryption keys used to secure the point-to-point link
options.D: It routes traffic between TrustSec domains

questions.explanation_es: MKA (MACsec Key Agreement, definido en 802.1X-2010) es el protocolo que negocia y renueva las claves de cifrado usadas por MACsec en el enlace punto a punto. La asignación de SGT es una función distinta, propia de TrustSec/ISE.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: In a TrustSec architecture, what device typically performs SGT propagation over links that do not support inline tagging?

options.A: SGT is dropped and traffic is untagged
options.B: SGT is converted into a VLAN ID automatically by the switch, with no need for SXP or any additional propagation protocol
options.C: SGT is carried using SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) to propagate IP-to-SGT bindings to devices without hardware support
options.D: SGT is embedded in the DSCP field

questions.explanation_es: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) permite propagar los bindings IP-a-SGT hacia dispositivos que no soportan el etiquetado inline (in-line tagging) en hardware, típicamente entre switches de acceso más antiguos y el enforcement point.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which component enforces TrustSec policy based on SGT-to-SGT communication rules?

options.A: The VTP server
options.B: The Security Group ACL (SGACL), applied at the enforcement point
options.C: The STP root bridge, which centrally enforces every SGACL policy for the entire Layer 2 domain
options.D: The DHCP relay agent

questions.explanation_es: Las SGACL (Security Group ACLs) son las que definen y aplican qué comunicación está permitida entre grupos (SGT origen -> SGT destino), y se aplican en el punto de enforcement (generalmente el switch de egreso o el firewall).

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares MACsec and IPsec?

options.A: MACsec requires a VPN gateway, while IPsec does not
options.B: IPsec only works on wireless links, while MACsec only works on wired links
options.C: Both provide identical end-to-end encryption across multiple routed hops, making the two technologies fully interchangeable
options.D: MACsec secures Layer 2 links hop-by-hop; IPsec can secure traffic end-to-end across Layer 3 routed paths

questions.explanation_es: MACsec cifra tráfico de Capa 2 en cada enlace físico directo (hop-by-hop), mientras que IPsec puede establecer túneles end-to-end sobre Capa 3, atravesando múltiples saltos enrutados sin descifrarse en cada uno.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which is a primary benefit of TrustSec's SGT-based segmentation compared to traditional VLAN-based segmentation?

options.A: It decouples policy from IP addressing/topology, simplifying segmentation across the network without redesigning VLANs/subnets
options.B: It eliminates the need for any access control policy at all, since SGT-based segmentation enforces itself automatically without configuration
options.C: It requires re-IPing the entire network
options.D: It only works within a single VLAN

questions.explanation_es: El valor de TrustSec es que la política de segmentación se basa en la identidad/rol (SGT), no en la IP o VLAN, por lo que se puede segmentar sin rediseñar el esquema de direccionamiento o de VLANs.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What happens to MACsec-protected traffic if it needs to traverse an untrusted, non-MACsec-capable Layer 2 device in the middle of the path?

options.A: Nothing changes, IPsec takes over automatically
options.B: The device automatically upgrades to support MACsec
options.C: MACsec automatically tunnels through the device transparently, re-establishing hop-by-hop protection on the other side without any support needed
options.D: The chain of hop-by-hop protection is broken at that device, since MACsec requires MACsec-capable devices at every hop

questions.explanation_es: Como MACsec depende de asociaciones de seguridad por enlace entre dispositivos adyacentes que lo soportan, un salto intermedio sin capacidad MACsec rompe la cadena de protección hop-by-hop en ese punto.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Which Cisco platform typically acts as the policy administration point (PAP) in a TrustSec deployment, defining SGTs and SGACL policies?

options.A: Cisco Catalyst Center only
options.B: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE)
options.C: Cisco IOS XR route processor
options.D: Cisco WLC, since wireless controllers are solely responsible for defining every SGT and SGACL policy

questions.explanation_es: Cisco ISE (Identity Services Engine) es típicamente el punto de administración de políticas (PAP) en TrustSec: define SGTs, políticas SGACL y las distribuye a los enforcement points.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: In YANG, what is the primary distinction between a 'list' and a 'leaf-list'?

options.A: A 'list' can only hold strings; a 'leaf-list' can hold any type
options.B: A 'list' contains multiple instances of complex data with one or more child nodes (potentially with keys); a 'leaf-list' contains multiple instances of a single simple leaf value
options.C: A 'leaf-list' requires a key statement, while a 'list' never does
options.D: A 'leaf-list' can contain nested container or list nodes as children, while a 'list' is restricted to holding only a single scalar leaf value and therefore never requires a key statement

questions.explanation_es: Un 'list' agrupa múltiples instancias de una estructura de datos compleja (con uno o más nodos hijos, normalmente identificadas por una 'key'); un 'leaf-list' es simplemente una colección de valores simples de un único leaf, sin estructura interna adicional.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a YANG data model in network automation?

options.A: To compress configuration files for storage
options.B: To replace the CLI as the only way to configure a device, since YANG models make the command line interface completely obsolete on modern platforms, since YANG-capable platforms must disable CLI access entirely
options.C: To act as a routing protocol
options.D: To provide a standardized, structured, and vendor-neutral (or vendor-specific) definition of configuration and operational data for programmatic access

questions.explanation_es: YANG es un lenguaje de modelado de datos que define de forma estructurada y estandarizada cómo se representan los datos de configuración y estado operativo de un dispositivo, permitiendo el acceso programático consistente vía NETCONF/RESTCONF.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which statement about YANG 'container' is correct?

options.A: A container groups related nodes together but does not itself hold a value; it's an organizational structure
options.B: A container is equivalent to a leaf with multiple values, functioning as a single scalar field with a list built into it
options.C: A container is always mandatory and cannot be nested
options.D: A container can only contain leaf-list elements

questions.explanation_es: Un 'container' en YANG agrupa nodos relacionados (leafs, lists, otros containers) de forma jerárquica y organizativa; en sí mismo no almacena un valor, solo estructura los datos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What are the two main types of YANG modules used with NETCONF/RESTCONF for network devices?

options.A: Only vendor-native models exist
options.B: Only OpenConfig models are valid for Cisco devices, since native YANG models were deprecated entirely by Cisco
options.C: Native (vendor-specific) models and Open/Standard models (such as those from IETF or OpenConfig)
options.D: XML models and JSON models

questions.explanation_es: Existen modelos YANG nativos (específicos del fabricante, ej. Cisco-IOS-XE-native) y modelos abiertos/estándar (IETF, OpenConfig), que buscan ofrecer una representación común entre distintos fabricantes.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of using YANG models compared to screen-scraping CLI output for automation?

options.A: YANG eliminates the need for any authentication
options.B: YANG only works with SNMP
options.C: YANG provides a structured, machine-readable schema with defined data types, reducing parsing errors compared to unstructured CLI text
options.D: YANG requires more bandwidth than CLI scraping in all cases, since every YANG-encoded message carries a full schema definition inline, since every leaf must resend its full type definition

questions.explanation_es: El beneficio central de YANG es que define un esquema estructurado con tipos de datos definidos, lo cual es mucho más confiable de procesar de forma programática que hacer 'screen-scraping' de salidas de CLI que pueden cambiar de formato entre versiones.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: In a YANG list definition, what is the purpose of the 'key' statement?

options.A: It defines the default value for the entire list, applied automatically whenever a new instance is created without explicit values
options.B: It is only used for leaf-lists, not lists
options.C: It defines which leaf(s) uniquely identify each entry/instance within the list
options.D: It encrypts the list data

questions.explanation_es: El statement 'key' en un 'list' de YANG especifica qué leaf o combinación de leafs identifica de forma única cada instancia/entrada dentro de esa lista, similar a una clave primaria.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which protocol(s) commonly use YANG models to exchange configuration and operational data?

options.A: NETCONF and RESTCONF
options.B: Only BGP
options.C: Only SNMP
options.D: Only Telnet, since YANG was originally designed for that legacy CLI transport protocol

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF y RESTCONF son los protocolos de gestión que utilizan modelos YANG como esquema de datos para representar la configuración y el estado operativo intercambiado con el dispositivo.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: What does the YANG 'rpc' statement define?

options.A: A routing protocol configuration, defining how routes are advertised and received between two YANG-modeled network devices
options.B: A remote procedure call operation with defined input and output parameters, such as a reboot or clear-counters action
options.C: A container used only for statistics
options.D: A read-only leaf value

questions.explanation_es: El statement 'rpc' en YANG define una operación de tipo llamada a procedimiento remoto, con parámetros de entrada y salida definidos (por ejemplo, una acción de reinicio o de limpieza de contadores), distinta de la simple configuración de datos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which statement about YANG data modeling and vendor interoperability is accurate?

options.A: Native YANG models guarantee full interoperability across all vendors
options.B: OpenConfig/IETF models aim to provide a common, vendor-neutral schema, while native models are vendor-specific and may differ significantly between platforms
options.C: YANG models are identical regardless of whether they are native or open, since all vendors are required to converge on one single unified schema, a claim repeated because both reuse one canonical XPath syntax
options.D: Only IETF models can be used with NETCONF

questions.explanation_es: Los modelos abiertos (OpenConfig/IETF) buscan ofrecer un esquema común entre fabricantes, mientras que los modelos nativos son específicos de cada plataforma y pueden variar bastante entre sí, lo que reduce la portabilidad de la automatización basada en ellos.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: A YANG leaf-list named 'dns-server' contains the values '8.8.8.8' and '1.1.1.1'. If you needed to instead model each DNS server with both an IP address and a description, which construct would be more appropriate?

options.A: Use a container with no children
options.B: Use a 'list' with a key (e.g., the IP) and child leafs for the IP and description, since leaf-list only supports single simple values
options.C: Keep using leaf-list, since it already supports multiple attributes per entry including nested key-value pairs and descriptions
options.D: Use a single leaf with a comma-separated string

questions.explanation_es: Cuando cada entrada necesita más de un atributo (IP + descripción), se requiere un 'list' con una key y leafs hijos, ya que un 'leaf-list' solo puede almacenar valores simples de un único tipo, uno por entrada.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What type of API does Cisco Catalyst Center primarily expose for northbound programmatic access?

options.A: A proprietary binary protocol that only Cisco's own internal tools are able to parse and decode
options.B: RESTful APIs using HTTPS with JSON payloads
options.C: Only CLI-based scripting
options.D: SOAP-based APIs

questions.explanation_es: Cisco Catalyst Center expone principalmente APIs RESTful sobre HTTPS con payloads en JSON, permitiendo integraciones northbound con sistemas de terceros y automatización.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which category of Catalyst Center APIs would you use to retrieve inventory information about devices managed by the platform?

options.A: Intent APIs / Discovery and Inventory APIs
options.B: SNMP trap APIs
options.C: Only northbound SSH APIs
options.D: Only SD-WAN Manager APIs, since Catalyst Center has no inventory API category of its own

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center ofrece Intent APIs, entre ellas las de Discovery e Inventory, que permiten consultar la lista de dispositivos descubiertos y gestionados, su estado, y detalles asociados.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What authentication mechanism is typically used first when interacting with Cisco Catalyst Center's REST API?

options.A: Obtaining an authentication token via a POST request with credentials, then using that token in subsequent API calls
options.B: Kerberos
options.C: No authentication is required for any API call
options.D: Only client-side certificates, with no username/password support offered under any configuration or licensing tier available

questions.explanation_es: El flujo típico es enviar credenciales (usuario/contraseña) en una solicitud POST para obtener un token de autenticación (X-Auth-Token), que luego se incluye en el header de las llamadas API subsecuentes.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: How do Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) APIs differ in purpose from Catalyst Center APIs, at a high level?

options.A: SD-WAN Manager APIs focus on managing and monitoring the SD-WAN fabric (templates, policies, device onboarding), while Catalyst Center APIs focus on the campus/branch enterprise network (intent-based provisioning, assurance)
options.B: They are functionally identical and interchangeable
options.C: Catalyst Center has no APIs related to network provisioning at all, focusing on read-only reporting and dashboards for administrators who need historical data for compliance audits across the entire enterprise campus and branch network
options.D: SD-WAN Manager APIs are SOAP-only

questions.explanation_es: Ambos son controladores con APIs RESTful, pero SD-WAN Manager gestiona específicamente el fabric SD-WAN (plantillas, políticas, onboarding de dispositivos SD-WAN), mientras que Catalyst Center gestiona la red empresarial de campus/sucursal con un enfoque de intención (intent-based) y aseguramiento (assurance).

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Catalyst Center API capability allows you to trigger provisioning of a network intent, such as applying a template to a device?

options.A: Only export APIs for reporting, with no ability to trigger any configuration change on a managed device, since the REST gateway is claimed to reject every POST and PUT verb
options.B: Assurance-only read APIs
options.C: Only APIs for user management
options.D: Intent APIs that support both GET (read) and POST/PUT (create/update) operations for network configuration and provisioning

questions.explanation_es: Las Intent APIs de Catalyst Center soportan tanto operaciones de lectura (GET) como de escritura (POST/PUT) para desencadenar acciones de provisioning e intención sobre la red, no solo consultas.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of these is an advantage of using Catalyst Center APIs over configuring devices individually via CLI?

options.A: APIs require more manual steps per device than CLI
options.B: APIs allow centralized, intent-based, and repeatable automation across many devices at once, reducing manual per-device configuration
options.C: APIs typically require a persistent TLS session to be re-established for each individual configuration call, which can make small one-off changes on a single device slower than an equivalent CLI session already logged in
options.D: APIs cannot scale beyond a single device

questions.explanation_es: El principal beneficio es la automatización centralizada y basada en intención, aplicable de forma repetible a muchos dispositivos a la vez, reduciendo la configuración manual dispositivo por dispositivo.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: When calling Catalyst Center's Intent API to get the list of network devices, what is the typical HTTP method used?

options.A: PATCH only
options.B: GET
options.C: DELETE
options.D: OPTIONS only

questions.explanation_es: Para consultar información (como la lista de dispositivos de red), el método HTTP típico es GET, que se usa para operaciones de lectura sin modificar datos.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What format does Catalyst Center typically use for API request and response bodies?

options.A: YAML
options.B: JSON
options.C: Plain text only
options.D: CSV

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center utiliza JSON como formato estándar para los cuerpos de las solicitudes y respuestas de su API REST.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: According to RFC 8040, what is the well-known base URI path used to discover the RESTCONF API entry point on a device?

options.A: /restconf
options.B: /netconf/rest
options.C: /api/v1/restconf
options.D: /.well-known/host-meta

questions.explanation_es: Según RFC 8040, el punto de entrada base de RESTCONF es '/restconf' (el dispositivo puede anunciar la ruta exacta vía /.well-known/host-meta, pero '/restconf' es la ruta convencional y comúnmente usada por defecto).

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which HTTP status code does RESTCONF typically return when a new resource is successfully created via a POST request?

options.A: 404 Not Found
options.B: 200 OK
options.C: 204 No Content
options.D: 201 Created

questions.explanation_es: Cuando un POST crea exitosamente un nuevo recurso, el código correcto es 201 Created. 200 OK se usa típicamente para respuestas exitosas a GET/PUT donde no se crea un recurso nuevo con Location, y 204 No Content para operaciones exitosas sin cuerpo de respuesta.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which HTTP method does RESTCONF use to completely replace an existing configuration resource?

options.A: GET
options.B: PUT
options.C: HEAD
options.D: OPTIONS

questions.explanation_es: PUT se usa en RESTCONF para reemplazar completamente un recurso de configuración existente (o crearlo si no existe, retornando 201 en ese caso). PATCH se usaría para una modificación parcial.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: RESTCONF and NETCONF both use YANG data models, but what is a key architectural difference between them?

options.A: RESTCONF cannot use YANG models, only NETCONF can
options.B: They are exactly the same protocol with different names
options.C: NETCONF is limited to editing the candidate datastore and cannot commit changes to the running configuration directly, while RESTCONF operates only against the running datastore and offers no commit-based workflow
options.D: RESTCONF uses HTTP(S) with a stateless request/response model, while NETCONF uses a session-based protocol typically over SSH with an RPC-based XML exchange

questions.explanation_es: RESTCONF opera sobre HTTP(S) de forma stateless (sin sesión persistente), usando verbos HTTP estándar; NETCONF establece una sesión persistente (típicamente sobre SSH) e intercambia mensajes RPC en XML. Ambos pueden usar los mismos modelos YANG subyacentes.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which media types are commonly supported in the Accept/Content-Type headers of a RESTCONF request?

options.A: Only multipart/form-data
options.B: Only text/plain
options.C: Only application/octet-stream, since RESTCONF never encodes YANG data using either JSON or XML media types
options.D: application/yang-data+json and application/yang-data+xml

questions.explanation_es: RESTCONF soporta representaciones en JSON y XML mediante los media types específicos application/yang-data+json y application/yang-data+xml, indicados en los headers Accept y Content-Type.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What HTTP status code indicates a successful DELETE operation in RESTCONF, with no content returned?

options.A: 200 OK
options.B: 301 Moved Permanently
options.C: 204 No Content
options.D: 201 Created

questions.explanation_es: Una operación DELETE exitosa que no retorna cuerpo de respuesta se indica típicamente con el código 204 No Content.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: In RESTCONF, which HTTP method is used to perform a partial modification (merge) of an existing configuration resource rather than replacing it entirely?

options.A: PUT
options.B: DELETE
options.C: HEAD
options.D: PATCH

questions.explanation_es: PATCH se utiliza para aplicar una modificación parcial (merge) sobre un recurso existente, a diferencia de PUT que reemplaza el recurso completo.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which datastore does RESTCONF operate against, in contrast to NETCONF's separate running/candidate/startup datastores?

options.A: RESTCONF only supports the startup datastore
options.B: RESTCONF operates directly against a single conceptual 'running' datastore, without a separate candidate datastore commit model
options.C: RESTCONF requires a candidate datastore for every operation, exactly the same way NETCONF's commit-based workflow always does, the same commit-based workflow NETCONF itself always uses
options.D: RESTCONF has no concept of a datastore

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de NETCONF, que puede trabajar con datastores separados (running, candidate, startup) y requiere un commit explícito, RESTCONF opera directamente sobre un datastore conceptual único (equivalente a 'running'), aplicando cambios de forma inmediata.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: If a RESTCONF client sends a malformed JSON body that doesn't validate against the YANG schema, what type of HTTP status code range would you expect in the response?

options.A: 2xx (Success)
options.B: 1xx (Informational)
options.C: 4xx (Client Error), such as 400 Bad Request
options.D: 3xx (Redirection) always, since RESTCONF redirects every malformed request to a documentation page describing the correct schema

questions.explanation_es: Un error del cliente, como un JSON malformado o que no valida contra el esquema YANG, típicamente resulta en un código 4xx, como 400 Bad Request, indicando que el problema está en la solicitud enviada.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of the following correctly reflects the RESTCONF URI structure for accessing configuration data under the base path?

options.A: /restconf/data/{...} is used to access data resources (config and state), and /restconf/operations/{rpc-name} is used to invoke RPC operations
options.B: Data and operations both use /restconf/yang-library/
options.C: /restconf/data/{...} is reserved exclusively for invoking YANG RPC operations, while /restconf/operations/{rpc-name} is used to read and write configuration and operational state data resources under the base path
options.D: There is no distinction; everything uses /restconf/rpc/

questions.explanation_es: En RESTCONF, '/restconf/data/{...}' se usa para acceder a recursos de datos (configuración y estado), mientras que '/restconf/operations/{rpc-name}' se usa para invocar operaciones RPC definidas en el modelo YANG.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What is the primary function of a virtual switch (vSwitch)?

options.A: Switches Ethernet frames between VMs on the same host, and between VMs and the physical network via NICs
options.B: Performs Layer 3 routing between subnets, with no Layer 2 switching
options.C: Provides storage replication between hosts, syncing VM disk files
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical switches, handling all WAN and internet edge connectivity too

questions.explanation_es: Un vSwitch conmuta tramas Ethernet entre las VMs del mismo host, y entre esas VMs y la red física a través de las NICs físicas, funcionando principalmente en Capa 2.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What does Open vSwitch (OVS) support that a very basic vSwitch doesn't?

options.A: It only works with a single hypervisor vendor and can't be programmed at all by any external tool
options.B: Advanced features like OpenFlow programmability, VXLAN/GRE tunneling, and flow-based forwarding
options.C: Proprietary Cisco hardware, unlike a standard software vSwitch
options.D: No VLAN tagging at all, limiting it to one flat broadcast domain

questions.explanation_es: Open vSwitch soporta características avanzadas como programabilidad vía OpenFlow, tunneling VXLAN/GRE, y reenvío basado en flujos, yendo más allá de un vSwitch básico.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: In VMware vSphere, what's the difference between a Standard and a Distributed vSwitch (vDS)?

options.A: A vDS can't support port groups; VLANs must be set manually per host instead
options.B: They're functionally identical, differing only in licensing cost
options.C: A Standard vSwitch is per-host; a vDS gives centralized config across a cluster
options.D: A Standard vSwitch automatically syncs its config across every host in the cluster

questions.explanation_es: El Standard vSwitch se configura por host; el Distributed vSwitch (vDS) ofrece configuración centralizada y consistente a través de múltiples hosts de un clúster.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What is a 'port group' on a VMware vSwitch?

options.A: A routing table entry forwarding traffic between two port groups
options.B: A physical NIC port reserved for management, vMotion, and storage traffic between hosts across the entire cluster
options.C: A group of physical switches stacked into one logical switch
options.D: A logical grouping of virtual ports sharing the same network policy (VLAN, security)

questions.explanation_es: Un port group es una agrupación lógica de puertos virtuales que comparten la misma política de red (VLAN, seguridad), a la cual se conectan las vNICs.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Which security feature, when disabled, lets a VM send frames claiming a different MAC than its vNIC?

options.A: NIC teaming load balancing policy
options.B: Forged Transmits protection
options.C: VLAN tagging in VST mode
options.D: Jumbo frame support on the uplink

questions.explanation_es: 'Forged Transmits' bloquea que una VM envíe tramas con una MAC de origen distinta a la de su vNIC configurada; si se deshabilita, permite ese comportamiento potencialmente malicioso.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What's correct about VLAN tagging on a vSwitch port group (VST mode)?

options.A: The VM's guest OS must add/remove its own VLAN tag on every frame
options.B: VLAN tagging is impossible without a Distributed vSwitch
options.C: The physical switch removes the VLAN tag before it reaches the vSwitch, which never sees any tagging
options.D: The vSwitch tags/untags frames per port group; the guest OS never sees VLAN tagging

questions.explanation_es: En VST, el propio vSwitch añade/quita la etiqueta VLAN del port group; el sistema operativo invitado no necesita saber nada sobre VLANs.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What's the primary purpose of teaming multiple physical NICs as a vSwitch uplink?

options.A: To convert the vSwitch into a full Layer 3 router
options.B: To provide redundancy and/or load balancing for outbound traffic
options.C: To eliminate MAC learning on the vSwitch entirely
options.D: To disable all outbound VM traffic until manually re-enabled

questions.explanation_es: Agrupar NICs físicas como uplinks en team provee redundancia (failover) y/o balanceo de carga del tráfico saliente hacia la red física, similar a un EtherChannel.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Why can't a physical firewall inspect traffic between two VMs on the same vSwitch/port group without extra config?

options.A: The vSwitch always performs a full Layer 3 routing lookup for every single frame, even within the same subnet
options.B: vSwitches encrypt all intra-host traffic by default
options.C: VMs on the same port group can't communicate with each other at all
options.D: That traffic switches locally inside the vSwitch and never reaches the physical network

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico entre dos VMs del mismo port group se conmuta localmente dentro del vSwitch, sin salir hacia la red física, por lo que un firewall tradicional no lo ve sin forzar el tráfico a salir.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: In a VXLAN EVPN fabric, what distributes MAC-to-VTEP mapping, replacing flood-and-learn?

options.A: BGP EVPN control plane, advertising MAC and MAC/IP routes between VTEPs
options.B: Spanning Tree Protocol running across the overlay
options.C: ARP flooding sent to every VTEP in the flood-and-learn domain for that VNI, regardless of any BGP control plane
options.D: OSPF acting as the overlay's MAC learning mechanism

questions.explanation_es: El plano de control BGP EVPN distribuye las asociaciones MAC-a-VTEP (y MAC/IP) mediante rutas Tipo 2, eliminando la necesidad de flood-and-learn tradicional.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What does 'BUM' traffic stand for in VXLAN, and why is it a design challenge?

options.A: Bidirectional Unicast Messaging; it refers only to control-plane BGP sessions between VTEPs, unrelated to any flooding or replication behavior
options.B: Backup Unicast Mode — a failover mechanism used only when a VTEP goes down
options.C: Bandwidth Usage Monitoring — relevant only to QoS marking, not flooding
options.D: Broadcast, Unknown-unicast, and Multicast — needs replication via multicast underlay or ingress replication

questions.explanation_es: BUM es Broadcast, Unknown-unicast y Multicast traffic; sin un dominio de broadcast L2 nativo entre VTEPs remotos, debe replicarse vía multicast en el underlay o ingress replication.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: With ingress replication instead of a multicast underlay, how is BUM traffic handled?

options.A: It's simply dropped, since multicast is unavailable
options.B: The underlay auto-enables PIM regardless of configuration
options.C: BUM traffic is converted to unicast ARP requests only, with absolutely no other flooding
options.D: The ingress VTEP makes a separate unicast copy for each remote VTEP that needs it

questions.explanation_es: Con ingress replication, el VTEP de ingreso genera copias unicast individuales de la trama BUM, una por cada VTEP remoto que la necesita, evitando multicast en el underlay.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What's the function of a VTEP (VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint)?

options.A: Encapsulates/decapsulates Ethernet frames into/from VXLAN, bridging overlay to underlay
options.B: It replaces the need for an IP underlay entirely, using only Layer 2 flooding and MAC learning
options.C: A pure L3 routing protocol with no encapsulation role at all
options.D: Performs only Layer 1 signal regeneration between two links

questions.explanation_es: El VTEP encapsula tramas Ethernet en paquetes VXLAN sobre UDP (y las desencapsula en destino), permitiendo que un dominio L2 overlay viaje sobre un underlay L3 enrutado.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: How does EVPN Type-2 route advertisement reduce unknown-unicast flooding?

options.A: It advertises MAC/IP plus originating VTEP via BGP, so remotes learn reachability without flood-and-learn
options.B: It only advertises IP prefixes, not MAC addresses
options.C: It disables all flooding permanently across the entire fabric, even for brand-new hosts never seen before
options.D: It's used for multicast group membership announcements

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas Tipo 2 anuncian MAC (y opcionalmente IP) junto al VTEP de origen vía BGP, permitiendo que los VTEPs remotos aprendan la ubicación por el plano de control en vez de flood-and-learn.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What's the purpose of the VNI field in a VXLAN header?

options.A: Identifies the L2 overlay segment, like a VLAN ID but with a 24-bit space
options.B: Identifies the underlay routing protocol used between VTEPs
options.C: Used only for QoS marking of VXLAN-encapsulated frames
options.D: It specifies the destination VTEP's physical MAC address for the outer header, recomputed at every hop

questions.explanation_es: El VNI identifica el segmento de overlay Capa 2, similar a una VLAN ID pero con un espacio de 24 bits (hasta ~16 millones de segmentos).

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: In a multicast-based VXLAN underlay, how is BUM traffic delivered to interested VTEPs?

options.A: It's dropped, since VXLAN can't use multicast in the underlay
options.B: It's always sent unicast to every VTEP, even with multicast configured
options.C: It uses OSPF flooding instead of multicast
options.D: Each VNI maps to a multicast group; PIM replicates to VTEPs that joined it

questions.explanation_es: Cada VNI se asocia a un grupo multicast en el underlay; el tráfico BUM se envía a ese grupo, y PIM lo replica hacia los VTEPs que se unieron a él.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: Which EVPN route type advertises IP prefix reachability for inter-subnet routing?

options.A: Type 5 (IP Prefix route)
options.B: Type 1 (Ethernet Auto-Discovery)
options.C: Type 2 (MAC/IP Advertisement)
options.D: Type 3 (Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag)

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas Tipo 5 (IP Prefix) se usan para anunciar alcanzabilidad de prefijos IP, típicamente para enrutamiento inter-subred (symmetric IRB).

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: What advantage does BGP EVPN give for ARP suppression in a VXLAN fabric?

options.A: ARP suppression only works with IPv6, never IPv4
options.B: Local VTEPs answer ARP for known remote hosts using Type-2 routes, avoiding flooding
options.C: It requires disabling EVPN entirely before configuring it
options.D: EVPN uses Type-5 routes to build static ARP entries needing manual refresh whenever any host happens to roam or move

questions.explanation_es: Gracias a los bindings MAC/IP aprendidos vía rutas Tipo 2, un VTEP local puede responder directamente a solicitudes ARP por hosts remotos conocidos, evitando inundar el fabric.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: Why does VXLAN encapsulate frames over UDP rather than another transport?

options.A: UDP's source port (hashed from the inner frame) enables good ECMP load balancing in the underlay
options.B: UDP is required since VXLAN can't run over IP any other way
options.C: UDP encrypts the payload automatically by default
options.D: It provides connection-oriented, guaranteed delivery that VXLAN fundamentally requires for reliable overlay transport

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN usa UDP porque permite variar el puerto de origen (hash de la trama interna), habilitando buen balanceo de carga/ECMP en el underlay; UDP no es garantizado ni orientado a conexión.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a 3-tier campus design, what's the primary role of the distribution layer?

options.A: Connects end-user devices and APs directly, providing edge port density
options.B: Acts as a pure Layer 1 repeater, with no L2 or L3 capability
options.C: Aggregates access uplinks, applies policy/QoS, and routes between access blocks
options.D: Serves as the backbone linking distribution blocks, with almost no policy applied

questions.explanation_es: La capa de distribución agrega los enlaces de acceso, aplica políticas (QoS, ACLs) y suele ser el límite entre Capa 2 y Capa 3, enrutando entre bloques de acceso.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What characterizes a 'collapsed core' (2-tier) design versus a 3-tier design?

options.A: Distribution and core functions merge into one layer, suited to smaller networks
options.B: It's a pattern exclusive to SD-Access fabric, unusable in traditional campuses
options.C: It adds a dedicated core on top of distribution, increasing device count
options.D: It removes the access layer, wiring end devices straight into the core

questions.explanation_es: En un diseño de 2 capas, las funciones de distribución y núcleo se combinan en una sola, reduciendo dispositivos y siendo apropiado para redes más pequeñas.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What's the primary purpose of Stateful Switchover (SSO) between redundant supervisors?

options.A: To load-balance traffic dynamically across redundant links between two devices
options.B: To provide default-gateway redundancy for end hosts via a backup router
options.C: To encrypt control-plane traffic between active and standby supervisors
options.D: To sync control-plane state between supervisors, so switchover skips a full reboot

questions.explanation_es: SSO sincroniza el estado del plano de control entre un supervisor activo y uno standby, de forma que un failover no requiera un reinicio completo ni reconvergencia total.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What problem do FHRPs like HSRP and VRRP primarily solve?

options.A: Redundancy for the default gateway seen by hosts, so one router failing doesn't break connectivity
options.B: Redundant paths across WAN links between remote sites
options.C: Replacing STP by eliminating Layer 2 loops at the gateway
options.D: Redundancy for DNS servers, so clients resolve names if one server fails

questions.explanation_es: Los FHRP resuelven que los hosts apuntan a un único gateway por defecto; si ese router falla, otro asume esa IP virtual de forma transparente para el host.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: In Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, what's the primary role of the vSmart controller?

options.A: It's the data-plane element at each branch, forwarding customer traffic over IPsec tunnels
options.B: It provides only DHCP/NTP services to branches, with no routing or policy role
options.C: It stages and pushes firmware upgrades to WAN Edge routers
options.D: It's the control-plane element distributing routing/policy to edge routers via OMP

questions.explanation_es: vSmart es el elemento de plano de control en SD-WAN; distribuye enrutamiento y políticas a los edge routers mediante OMP, similar a un route reflector de BGP para el overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What's the role of the vBond orchestrator in Catalyst SD-WAN?

options.A: It stores all historical telemetry collected from every WAN Edge router
options.B: It replaces vManage as the source of configuration templates
options.C: It handles initial authentication/orchestration, helping devices discover each other and traverse NAT
options.D: It performs deep packet inspection and application-layer firewalling on all data-plane traffic before it's forwarded onward across the fabric

questions.explanation_es: vBond actúa como orquestador: autentica inicialmente a dispositivos y controladores, y facilita que se descubran entre sí, incluyendo asistencia para atravesar NAT.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Which is a commonly cited benefit of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN over traditional WAN?

options.A: Transport independence — mixing MPLS, broadband, and LTE under centrally managed policy
options.B: It eliminates the need for any dedicated WAN transport, relying solely on the LAN within one building
options.C: It guarantees zero packet loss regardless of the underlying transport's quality
options.D: It requires no controllers; policy is configured manually on each edge

questions.explanation_es: Un beneficio central de SD-WAN es la independencia de transporte: combinar MPLS, banda ancha, LTE, etc., mientras la política se gestiona de forma centralizada.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Which is a legitimate limitation to consider when adopting SD-WAN?

options.A: SD-WAN can't support any encryption between sites, unlike a traditional MPLS L3VPN
options.B: It eliminates all need for staff to understand routing, since the overlay configures, tunes, and secures itself with zero operator input
options.C: It adds architectural complexity (controllers, overlay management) that must be operated correctly
options.D: It can't be used with more than one branch site

questions.explanation_es: SD-WAN aporta flexibilidad pero también complejidad adicional: hay que diseñar, asegurar y operar controladores y el overlay, requiriendo nuevas habilidades operativas.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what's the role of the Fabric Control Plane node?

options.A: Only onboarding wireless clients, with no role for wired endpoints
options.B: Replacing the border node, handling all external connectivity itself
options.C: Forwarding all data-plane traffic, VXLAN-encapsulating every packet
options.D: Maintaining a LISP-based host-tracking database mapping endpoint identity to location

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Control Plane node mantiene una base de datos de host-tracking basada en LISP, mapeando la identidad del endpoint (EID) a su ubicación (RLOC) en el fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What's the function of a Fabric Border Node in SD-Access?

options.A: Connects the fabric to networks outside it, like the traditional network, WAN, or internet
options.B: It replaces external DHCP servers entirely, assigning IP addresses to every endpoint directly without any server
options.C: Encrypts all fabric traffic between edge nodes using MACsec
options.D: Only manages wireless SSIDs and AP radio configuration

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Border Node es el punto de conexión entre el fabric de SD-Access y redes externas (tradicional, WAN, internet), actuando como límite de entrada/salida.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When integrating a traditional segment with SD-Access, what device typically handles route leaking between fabric VRFs and the global table?

options.A: A wireless LAN controller, since it already maintains a mapping of client locations across the whole fabric
options.B: The Fabric Edge Node, since it already handles VXLAN encapsulation
options.C: The DHCP server, since it assigns addressing across every VRF
options.D: A Fusion Router, which handles route leaking between fabric VRFs and external networks

questions.explanation_es: Un Fusion Router es el dispositivo típicamente usado para route leaking entre las VRFs del fabric SD-Access y la tabla de enrutamiento global externa.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which DSCP value should mark voice bearer (RTP) traffic per Cisco best practice?

options.A: CS3
options.B: EF
options.C: CS5
options.D: AF31

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico de voz (RTP) se marca con EF, diseñado para tráfico sensible a latencia y jitter con baja tolerancia a pérdida. AF31/CS3 se usan típicamente para señalización.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the difference between traffic classification and traffic marking in QoS?

options.A: Classification identifies traffic by criteria; marking sets a field (DSCP/CoS) reflecting that classification
options.B: Marking always happens before classification, since the DSCP value written into the packet is what determines which traffic class it belongs to
options.C: They're the same operation, just given two different names by Cisco
options.D: Classification only applies to Layer 2 CoS; marking only to Layer 3

questions.explanation_es: La clasificación identifica y agrupa el tráfico según un criterio; el marcado escribe un valor (DSCP/CoS) en el paquete para que otros dispositivos apliquen tratamiento diferenciado.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What's the key architectural difference between a Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisor?

options.A: Type 2 can't run more than one VM at a time on the same host
options.B: Type 1 runs bare-metal on hardware; Type 2 runs as an app on a host OS
options.C: Type 1 requires a host OS; Type 2 does not
options.D: They're functionally identical, differing only in branding and licensing

questions.explanation_es: Un hipervisor Tipo 1 (bare-metal) corre directamente sobre el hardware; un Tipo 2 corre como aplicación encima de un sistema operativo host existente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why are Type 1 hypervisors generally preferred for production data centers?

options.A: Better performance and lower overhead, interacting directly with hardware
options.B: Type 1 can't support more than one guest OS per host
options.C: Type 1 hypervisors are always free while Type 2 always requires a paid license, even for one server
options.D: Type 2 can't support any virtual networking at all

questions.explanation_es: Al eliminar la capa de SO host intermedio, los hipervisores Tipo 1 ofrecen mejor rendimiento y menor overhead, la opción preferida en producción.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What's the primary benefit of VM encapsulation (a VM as a set of files)?

options.A: It locks the VM to always run on the host it was created on
options.B: It lets a VM be easily copied, moved, or migrated between hosts
options.C: It eliminates the need for a hypervisor to run the VM
options.D: It prevents the VM from ever being backed up or snapshotted

questions.explanation_es: Al encapsularse como un conjunto de archivos, una VM se puede copiar, mover o migrar fácilmente entre hosts, ya que todo su estado es portable.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What does live migration (e.g. vMotion) let an administrator do?

options.A: Convert a running VM into a physical server automatically
options.B: Move a running VM between hosts with minimal to no downtime
options.C: Permanently delete a VM's disk after migration completes
options.D: Disable all networking on a VM permanently during migration

questions.explanation_es: La migración en vivo permite mover una VM en ejecución entre hosts con downtime mínimo o nulo, sin apagarla.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What's the primary purpose of a VRF on a router?

options.A: Multiple independent routing tables on one device, allowing overlapping IPs and isolation
options.B: Replacing the need for VLANs on switches entirely
options.C: It encrypts all router traffic using IPsec by default, regardless of VRF or interface, needing no crypto configuration at all
options.D: Providing Layer 2 switching only, with no routing

questions.explanation_es: Una VRF crea múltiples tablas de enrutamiento independientes en un mismo dispositivo, permitiendo IPs solapadas y aislando el tráfico entre dominios lógicos distintos.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What's a key characteristic of GRE tunneling?

options.A: It encapsulates many protocols but provides no encryption or authentication itself
options.B: It requires IPsec to be fully configured before it can function at all as a tunnel of any kind whatsoever
options.C: It only works with IPv4 payloads, never IPv6
options.D: It always encrypts the payload with AES by default

questions.explanation_es: GRE encapsula una amplia variedad de protocolos dentro de un túnel IP, pero por sí mismo no ofrece cifrado ni autenticación; por eso se combina con IPsec cuando se necesita seguridad.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: How do the IPsec protocols AH and ESP differ?

options.A: AH gives authentication/integrity only; ESP gives encryption plus authentication/integrity
options.B: AH is tunnel-mode only; ESP is transport-mode only
options.C: AH provides encryption only; ESP provides authentication only
options.D: Both can encrypt, but AH also authenticates the outer IP header, preferred for NAT traversal

questions.explanation_es: AH provee autenticación e integridad pero NO cifrado. ESP provee tanto cifrado como autenticación/integridad, por lo que es la opción más usada cuando se requiere confidencialidad.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In LISP, what's the function of the ETR (Egress Tunnel Router)?

options.A: Decapsulates LISP traffic for its site and registers EID-to-RLOC mappings with the Map-Server
options.B: Replaces the Map-Resolver in the LISP control plane
options.C: It only originates encapsulated traffic, never receives any, since receiving is reserved for the Map-Resolver
options.D: Performs no role in the LISP control plane

questions.explanation_es: El ETR recibe y desencapsula el tráfico LISP destinado a su sitio local, y registra sus mapeos EID-a-RLOC ante el Map-Server.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What's the role of the Map-Resolver in a LISP architecture?

options.A: Receives map-requests from ITRs and forwards them to the right Map-Server
options.B: Performs the actual data-plane encapsulation between sites
options.C: It performs the same encapsulation as an ETR, but only for multicast traffic, never for unicast
options.D: Stores end-user application data for later retrieval

questions.explanation_es: El Map-Resolver recibe las solicitudes de mapeo de los ITRs y las reenvía al Map-Server correspondiente, funcionando como intermediario del plano de control.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'native VLAN' on an 802.1Q trunk link?

options.A: The native VLAN is where all trunk control-plane traffic like DTP and CDP is encrypted and authenticated by default on every Cisco trunk port
options.B: Frames belonging to the native VLAN are sent untagged across the trunk, while all other VLANs are tagged
options.C: The native VLAN can never be VLAN 1, since VLAN 1 is permanently reserved for management traffic only
options.D: Native VLAN only applies to RSTP domains and has no meaning at all under legacy 802.1D STP

questions.explanation_es: En un trunk 802.1Q, las tramas de la VLAN nativa se envían sin etiqueta (untagged), mientras que las demás VLANs se envían con su etiqueta 802.1Q correspondiente. Es importante que ambos extremos del trunk configuren la misma VLAN nativa para evitar problemas de seguridad/conectividad.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What does DTP (Dynamic Trunking Protocol) do on a Cisco switch link?

options.A: It is used only for routing protocol negotiation between two directly connected Layer 3 devices
options.B: It dynamically negotiates whether a link becomes a trunk or an access port between two Cisco switches
options.C: It replaces the need for 802.1Q tagging entirely, since DTP itself carries all VLAN information across the link
options.D: It assigns IP addresses to trunk interfaces automatically once negotiation completes successfully

questions.explanation_es: DTP es un protocolo propietario de Cisco que negocia dinámicamente si un enlace entre dos switches Cisco se convierte en trunk o en puerto de acceso, según los modos configurados (auto, desirable, on, nonegotiate) en cada extremo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes LACP from PAgP as EtherChannel negotiation protocols?

options.A: LACP cannot support more than 2 active links in a bundle, unlike PAgP which supports up to 8
options.B: They are functionally and operationally identical with no meaningful difference between them at all, since both were standardized by the IEEE at exactly the same time
options.C: LACP is an IEEE standard (802.3ad/802.1AX) usable in multivendor environments; PAgP is a Cisco-proprietary protocol usable only between Cisco devices
options.D: PAgP is the IEEE standard, and LACP is Cisco-proprietary, usable only between two Cisco devices

questions.explanation_es: LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) es un estándar IEEE (802.3ad/802.1AX), por lo que se puede usar entre dispositivos de distintos fabricantes; PAgP (Port Aggregation Protocol) es propietario de Cisco y solo funciona entre dispositivos Cisco.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What determines how traffic is distributed across the links of an EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: A load-balancing hashing algorithm (e.g., based on source/destination MAC, IP, or port) selects which physical link a given flow uses
options.B: EtherChannel does not support load balancing at all, since traffic always uses only the first link in the bundle while every other link remains completely idle as a pure backup
options.C: Only the first configured link in the bundle is ever used, with the rest sitting idle as pure backups
options.D: Traffic is always sent round-robin, one frame per link regardless of flow, requiring no hashing algorithm

questions.explanation_es: El reparto de tráfico entre los enlaces físicos de un EtherChannel se determina mediante un algoritmo de hashing configurable (basado en MAC origen/destino, IP origen/destino, puerto, etc.), que asigna cada flujo a un enlace físico específico del bundle, manteniendo el orden de las tramas dentro de un mismo flujo.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the key difference in purpose between Root Guard and BPDU Guard?

options.A: BPDU Guard is used only on trunk ports carrying multiple VLANs, while Root Guard is used only on access ports connected directly to a single end-host device, never on any port facing another switch
options.B: They are functionally identical STP protection features given two different marketing names by Cisco
options.C: Root Guard blocks all traffic on a port entirely, not just BPDUs, functioning like a full port shutdown
options.D: Root Guard prevents a port from becoming the root port/root bridge by blocking superior BPDUs, while BPDU Guard disables a port entirely (typically an edge/PortFast port) upon receiving any BPDU

questions.explanation_es: Root Guard evita que un puerto se convierta en puerto raíz (y por lo tanto que un switch downstream se convierta en el root bridge) bloqueando BPDUs superiores; BPDU Guard, en cambio, deshabilita completamente el puerto (típicamente uno configurado como edge/PortFast) al recibir cualquier BPDU, asumiendo que en ese puerto no debería haber otro switch conectado.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In RSTP (802.1w), what is the purpose of the 'alternate' port role?

options.A: It refers to a port connected to an end host that never participates in the spanning tree topology at all
options.B: It provides a backup path to the root bridge via a different segment, ready to quickly transition to forwarding if the current root port fails
options.C: It is a port that is always forwarding traffic simultaneously with the root port, providing active load sharing across both paths at the same time
options.D: It only exists in legacy 802.1D STP, not RSTP, which replaced it with an entirely different mechanism

questions.explanation_es: El rol de puerto 'alternate' en RSTP representa un camino de respaldo hacia el root bridge, a través de un switch/segmento distinto, listo para pasar rápidamente a forwarding si el puerto raíz actual falla, permitiendo la convergencia rápida característica de RSTP.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In EIGRP's DUAL algorithm, what is a 'feasible successor'?

options.A: A route that always has a higher metric than the successor and can never be used
options.B: The only route that can ever be installed in the routing table, since EIGRP never keeps any backup routes in its topology table at all
options.C: A route learned via redistribution from another routing protocol into EIGRP's topology table
options.D: A backup route to a destination that is guaranteed to be loop-free, kept in the topology table as a ready alternative if the successor route fails

questions.explanation_es: Un feasible successor en EIGRP es una ruta de respaldo hacia un destino que está garantizada matemáticamente (por el criterio de factibilidad) a estar libre de loops; se mantiene en la tabla de topología como alternativa lista para usarse instantáneamente si la ruta successor (la instalada) falla, sin necesidad de recálculo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How does OSPF primarily calculate its cost metric for a link, by default on Cisco devices?

options.A: Based on a reference bandwidth divided by the interface bandwidth (cost = reference-bandwidth / interface-bandwidth)
options.B: Based purely on hop count, like RIP, regardless of the actual bandwidth of any link along the path between source and destination
options.C: Based on a random value assigned at boot time that changes every time the router reloads
options.D: Based on the interface's MTU only, with larger MTUs always resulting in a lower calculated cost

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto, OSPF calcula el costo de un enlace como el resultado de dividir un ancho de banda de referencia (reference bandwidth, 100 Mbps por defecto) entre el ancho de banda configurado en la interfaz; enlaces más rápidos obtienen un costo menor. RIP, en cambio, usa conteo de saltos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: In OSPFv3, what addressing is used to form neighbor adjacencies between routers?

options.A: Link-local IPv6 addresses, even though the topology/prefix information exchanged can include global addresses
options.B: IPv4 addresses, since OSPFv3 is backward compatible and still relies on the IPv4 stack underneath
options.C: MAC addresses, with no IP addressing involved in adjacency formation at all
options.D: Global unicast IPv6 addresses only, since link-local addresses cannot be used to form any adjacency — as OSPFv3 hellos are considered to require a global source address

questions.explanation_es: En OSPFv3, las adyacencias de vecinos se forman usando direcciones IPv6 link-local, independientemente de que la información de topología y prefijos intercambiada en los LSAs pueda incluir direcciones IPv6 globales. Esta es una diferencia clave respecto a OSPFv2.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of an OSPF 'totally stubby' area?

options.A: It blocks both external (Type 5) LSAs and inter-area (Type 3) summary LSAs, injecting only a default route into the area
options.B: It can only be used as the backbone area (Area 0), never as a regular non-backbone area
options.C: It allows all LSA types without restriction, exactly like a normal non-stub OSPF area
options.D: It is identical to a standard stub area with no differences at all in which LSA types are blocked or permitted through it

questions.explanation_es: Un área totally stubby bloquea tanto las LSA externas (Tipo 5, de redistribución) como las LSA de resumen inter-área (Tipo 3), inyectando en su lugar solo una ruta por defecto hacia esas áreas/destinos externos, reduciendo aún más el tamaño de la tabla de enrutamiento comparado con un área stub normal.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In the BGP best-path selection process, which attribute is evaluated first among these two: Weight or Local Preference?

options.A: Weight is evaluated before Local Preference
options.B: They are evaluated simultaneously and tie-broken randomly
options.C: Neither is used in the actual best-path algorithm
options.D: Local Preference is always evaluated before Weight

questions.explanation_es: En el algoritmo de selección de mejor ruta de BGP, Weight (un atributo propietario de Cisco, local al router) se evalúa antes que Local Preference. Weight nunca se anuncia a otros routers, mientras que Local Preference sí se comparte dentro del AS local.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: By default, what TTL value is used for eBGP peering between directly connected neighbors, and why does this matter?

options.A: TTL is negotiated dynamically between the two peers and cannot be fixed to any particular value
options.B: TTL of 255 always, regardless of topology, exactly like most other routing protocol control traffic sent between adjacent devices on the same segment or across a routed path
options.C: TTL has no relevance to eBGP sessions at all, since BGP operates entirely above the IP layer
options.D: TTL of 1, meaning the BGP packets are expected to arrive from a directly connected neighbor only one hop away; multihop eBGP requires explicitly enabling 'ebgp-multihop'

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto, eBGP usa un TTL de 1, asumiendo que el vecino está directamente conectado (un solo salto). Si se necesita establecer una sesión eBGP con un vecino que está a más de un salto de distancia, hay que configurar explícitamente 'ebgp-multihop' para aumentar el TTL permitido.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Policy-Based Routing (PBR)?

options.A: To provide encryption for routed traffic as it passes through the router, similar to what IPsec provides on a site-to-site VPN tunnel between two remote locations regardless of which protocol is carried inside
options.B: To replace the routing table entirely with static routes configured manually by an administrator
options.C: To perform Layer 2 switching decisions instead of Layer 3 routing decisions for a given VLAN
options.D: To forward traffic based on criteria other than just the destination IP address, such as source address, application, or packet size, overriding the normal routing table decision

questions.explanation_es: PBR permite tomar decisiones de reenvío basadas en criterios distintos a la simple dirección IP de destino (por ejemplo, dirección de origen, tipo de aplicación, tamaño de paquete), anulando la decisión normal basada en la tabla de enrutamiento cuando coincide con la política definida.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does the 'stratum' number represent in NTP (Network Time Protocol)?

options.A: The encryption strength used by the NTP session, measured in bits of key length
options.B: The distance (in hops) from the reference clock source; stratum 0 devices are the reference clocks themselves, stratum 1 servers are directly connected to them, and the number increases with each additional hop
options.C: The physical location of the NTP server, expressed as a geographic coordinate pair
options.D: The number of clients an NTP server can support simultaneously before it starts rejecting new requests due to exceeding its configured connection limit set during initial configuration

questions.explanation_es: El stratum en NTP indica la distancia jerárquica respecto a la fuente de reloj de referencia: stratum 0 son los relojes de referencia mismos (ej. GPS), stratum 1 son servidores directamente sincronizados a esos relojes, y el número aumenta a medida que se aleja de la fuente.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Why is PTP (Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588) generally preferred over NTP in environments requiring sub-microsecond time accuracy?

options.A: PTP works only over serial links, never Ethernet, which limits its use to legacy WAN connections
options.B: PTP and NTP both rely on software-based timestamping at the application layer by default, so their achievable accuracy is comparable unless PTP hardware timestamping is separately enabled on the NICs and switches involved
options.C: PTP is designed to achieve much higher time synchronization precision (sub-microsecond) than NTP, which typically achieves millisecond-level accuracy over a network
options.D: NTP typically achieves better accuracy than PTP when synchronizing over a WAN link with multiple router hops, since PTP's accuracy degrades sharply once traffic leaves a single Layer 2 segment without transparent clocks along the path

questions.explanation_es: PTP está diseñado para lograr una precisión de sincronización de tiempo mucho mayor (a nivel de sub-microsegundos) que NTP, que típicamente logra precisión a nivel de milisegundos sobre una red. Por eso PTP se usa en entornos que requieren sincronización extremadamente precisa, como telecomunicaciones o sistemas financieros.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: How does PAT (Port Address Translation) allow multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP address?

options.A: It uses source port numbers to distinguish between the different internal sessions sharing the same translated public IP address
options.B: It assigns a different public IP to each internal host dynamically from a large pool of available addresses configured by the administrator
options.C: It requires each internal host to use a different VLAN so that the router can distinguish between sessions
options.D: It encrypts each session to distinguish them, using a unique key generated per internal host

questions.explanation_es: PAT (también llamado NAT overload) traduce múltiples direcciones IP internas a una única IP pública, distinguiendo cada sesión mediante el número de puerto de origen, que se traduce a un puerto único en la tabla de traducción, permitiendo miles de sesiones simultáneas compartiendo una sola IP pública.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In HSRP, what are the two primary states a router can be in for a given HSRP group (besides transitional states)?

options.A: Master and Backup
options.B: Root and Alternate
options.C: Active and Standby
options.D: Primary and Secondary

questions.explanation_es: En HSRP, los dos estados principales de un router dentro de un grupo son Active (el que reenvía el tráfico para la IP virtual) y Standby (el que está listo para asumir el rol activo si el actual falla). Nota: VRRP usa la terminología 'Master' y 'Backup' en lugar de Active/Standby.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes VRRP from HSRP?

options.A: VRRP is an IEEE/IETF open standard (RFC 3768/5798) usable across vendors, while HSRP is Cisco-proprietary; also, VRRP can use a router's own real interface IP as the virtual IP if desired
options.B: HSRP was later documented informationally by the IETF as RFC 2281 and is now considered the vendor-neutral option of the two, while VRRP remains a Cisco enhancement layered on top of HSRP's original design
options.C: VRRP cannot support preemption, while HSRP can, making HSRP the more flexible option operationally
options.D: They are identical protocols with different names only, since Cisco simply renamed HSRP to VRRP for IETF submission

questions.explanation_es: VRRP es un estándar abierto (RFC 3768/5798) utilizable entre distintos fabricantes, mientras que HSRP es propietario de Cisco. Además, VRRP permite que la IP virtual coincida con la IP real de la interfaz de uno de los routers (el 'IP address owner'), algo que HSRP no contempla de la misma forma.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of the RPF (Reverse Path Forwarding) check in multicast routing?

options.A: It verifies that a multicast packet arrived on the interface that the unicast routing table would use to reach the source, preventing loops and duplicate delivery
options.B: It has no relation to loop prevention, serving purely as a traffic accounting mechanism
options.C: It converts multicast traffic into unicast traffic before forwarding it out any interface, eliminating the need for any replication anywhere in the multicast distribution tree
options.D: It encrypts multicast traffic using a key shared between the source and all receivers

questions.explanation_es: El chequeo RPF verifica que un paquete multicast llegó por la interfaz que, según la tabla de enrutamiento unicast, se usaría para alcanzar la fuente de ese tráfico. Si no coincide, el paquete se descarta, lo cual previene loops y entrega duplicada en árboles de distribución multicast.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the key difference between PIM Sparse Mode (PIM-SM) using shared trees and PIM Source-Specific Multicast (SSM)?

options.A: PIM-SM only works with IPv6, and SSM only works with IPv4, making the two protocols mutually exclusive
options.B: Both PIM-SM and SSM build their forwarding trees exclusively through a Rendezvous Point, differing only in how the RP address is initially discovered by the receivers
options.C: PIM-SM initially builds a shared tree through a Rendezvous Point (RP) and can later switch to a source tree; SSM requires the receiver to specify the exact source, building a source tree directly without needing an RP
options.D: SSM always requires an RP, while PIM-SM never does, which is the exact reverse of how the two protocols actually behave in a real-world deployment running either PIM-SM or SSM across the campus in every PIM deployment regardless of vendor

questions.explanation_es: PIM-SM construye inicialmente un árbol compartido a través de un Rendezvous Point (RP), pudiendo luego cambiar a un árbol de fuente (source tree, SPT) para optimizar la ruta. SSM (Source-Specific Multicast), en cambio, requiere que el receptor especifique explícitamente la fuente (S,G) y construye un árbol de fuente directamente, sin necesidad de un RP.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What's the fundamental difference between an SNMP trap and an SNMP poll?

options.A: A trap is unsolicited, sent by the device when an event occurs
options.B: A poll is unsolicited, sent by the device on a fixed interval
options.C: Traps carry only interface counters; nothing else
options.D: Polls originate from the device; traps are requested by the manager

questions.explanation_es: Un trap es enviado sin solicitud previa por el dispositivo gestionado al ocurrir un evento; un poll es una consulta que inicia el gestor SNMP para pedir información al dispositivo.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which syslog severity level corresponds to 'critical', and how does the numbering work?

options.A: Severity levels apply only to SNMP traps, not to syslog
options.B: Level 2 is critical; lower numbers mean more severe (0=emergency, 7=debugging)
options.C: All syslog messages share severity level 4 by default
options.D: Level 7 is critical; higher numbers mean more severe, the reverse of Cisco's actual severity scale

questions.explanation_es: Los niveles de syslog van de 0 a 7, donde los números más bajos son más severos: 0=emergency, 2=critical, 7=debugging.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: In Flexible NetFlow, what does a 'flow record' define?

options.A: Only the physical interface where NetFlow is enabled
options.B: Only the IP address of the export destination
options.C: The key fields that identify a flow, and the non-key fields to collect
options.D: A single fixed template, identical across every Cisco platform and IOS release

questions.explanation_es: Un flow record define los campos clave (identifican el flujo, como IP/puerto origen-destino) y los no clave (datos recolectados, como contadores) a exportar; a diferencia de NetFlow tradicional, son totalmente configurables.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: In Flexible NetFlow, how does the 'exporter' differ from the 'monitor'?

options.A: They're the same configuration object under different names
options.B: Only the monitor is required; the exporter is always optional
options.C: The exporter sets the destination; the monitor ties record, exporter, and interface
options.D: The exporter defines the record fields; the monitor only sets the destination IP

questions.explanation_es: El exporter define el destino (IP, puerto, transporte) de los datos; el monitor une el record, el exporter y la interfaz donde se recolecta el flujo.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What's the key difference between RSPAN and ERSPAN?

options.A: ERSPAN only mirrors traffic within a single local switch
options.B: RSPAN crosses Layer 3 boundaries; ERSPAN is confined to Layer 2
options.C: RSPAN mirrors within one L2 domain via a VLAN; ERSPAN uses GRE to cross Layer 3
options.D: Both use 802.1Q tags and differ only in maximum switch hop count, not encapsulation

questions.explanation_es: RSPAN refleja tráfico entre switches dentro del mismo dominio L2 usando una VLAN dedicada. ERSPAN encapsula el tráfico en GRE, permitiendo enrutarlo a través de una red L3 hacia un destino remoto.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco IP SLA (Service Level Agreement)?

options.A: To replace the need for routing protocols
options.B: To actively generate synthetic traffic and measure network performance metrics such as latency, jitter, and packet loss between two points
options.C: To provide QoS marking for all traffic on an interface, replacing the need to configure any class-maps or policy-maps manually, since IP SLA operation types can mark a DSCP value on probe packets
options.D: To perform Layer 2 loop detection

questions.explanation_es: IP SLA genera tráfico sintético de prueba de forma activa entre dos puntos de la red y mide métricas de desempeño como latencia, jitter y pérdida de paquetes, permitiendo monitorear proactivamente el estado del servicio (por ejemplo, para validar SLAs o disparar acciones como cambios de ruta ante degradación).

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the core role of Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) in an enterprise network?

options.A: It provides centralized, intent-based network configuration, monitoring (Assurance), and management, including AI-powered workflows for troubleshooting and optimization
options.B: It is a Layer 2 switch used only in the access layer
options.C: It is a wireless-only management platform
options.D: It functions only as a syslog collector with no configuration capabilities, similar to a basic logging server used purely for archival purposes with no dashboard or workflow automation

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center centraliza la configuración de red basada en intención (intent-based), el monitoreo y aseguramiento (Assurance) de la red, y añade flujos de trabajo potenciados por IA para troubleshooting y optimización proactiva, tanto para infraestructura cableada como inalámbrica.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of these are core NETCONF operations used to retrieve and modify device configuration?

options.A: <get-config> to retrieve configuration data and <edit-config> to modify configuration data within a target datastore
options.B: SELECT and UPDATE, borrowed from SQL
options.C: Only HTTP GET and POST, since NETCONF is HTTP-based
options.D: NETCONF has no defined operations; it is purely a transport mechanism with no standardized RPC calls defined in its specification

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF define operaciones RPC específicas como <get-config> para recuperar la configuración de un datastore, y <edit-config> para modificarla; estas operaciones se intercambian en mensajes XML sobre una sesión persistente, típicamente sobre SSH, a diferencia de RESTCONF que usa verbos HTTP.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the difference between configuring a simple line password on a VTY line versus configuring local username-based authentication?

options.A: Line passwords are always more secure than username-based authentication, since they cannot be individually compromised or shared between multiple different users across an entire organization's device fleet, since a shared password can't be revoked for one person alone
options.B: They provide identical security and auditability
options.C: Local username authentication cannot be combined with AAA
options.D: A line password authenticates anyone who knows the shared password with no per-user accountability; local username authentication requires individual credentials, providing per-user identification and accountability
