questions.explanation_es: Una simple contraseña de línea (line password) autentica a cualquiera que la conozca, sin distinguir quién se conectó (sin accountability individual). La autenticación con usuario local (username/password) requiere credenciales individuales por persona, lo que permite identificar y auditar quién accedió, y es la base para integrarse luego con AAA.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: How does TACACS+ differ from RADIUS regarding the AAA functions of Authentication and Authorization?

options.A: RADIUS separates Authentication and Authorization, while TACACS+ combines them into one single unified process and packet exchange every single time a user logs into a network device
options.B: Neither protocol distinguishes Authentication from Authorization
options.C: TACACS+ does not support Authorization at all
options.D: TACACS+ separates Authentication and Authorization into distinct processes/packets, offering more granular control; RADIUS combines Authentication and Authorization into a single process

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ separa la Autenticación y la Autorización en procesos/paquetes distintos, lo que permite un control más granular (por ejemplo, autorizar comandos específicos de forma independiente); RADIUS, en cambio, combina Autenticación y Autorización en un único proceso, lo que ofrece menos granularidad.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a difference in what TACACS+ and RADIUS encrypt in their protocol exchanges?

options.A: TACACS+ encrypts the entire body of the packet, while RADIUS only encrypts the password field in the access-request packet
options.B: RADIUS encrypts the entire packet, while TACACS+ only encrypts the password field in every single exchange between the client and the AAA server
options.C: Both encrypt the entire packet identically
options.D: Neither protocol encrypts anything by default

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ cifra todo el cuerpo del paquete en la comunicación entre el cliente AAA y el servidor, mientras que RADIUS por defecto solo cifra el campo de contraseña en el paquete Access-Request, dejando el resto de la información (como el nombre de usuario) sin cifrar.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What is the primary functional difference between a standard ACL and an extended ACL on a Cisco device?

options.A: A standard ACL can only match based on source IP address; an extended ACL can match based on source/destination IP, protocol, and port numbers, allowing much more granular filtering
options.B: Extended ACLs can only be applied outbound, never inbound
options.C: They are functionally identical, differing only in numbering range
options.D: A standard ACL can filter based on Layer 4 ports, while extended cannot filter on anything beyond the source IP address at all under any Cisco IOS software version currently in use on the device

questions.explanation_es: Una ACL estándar solo puede filtrar tráfico basándose en la dirección IP de origen. Una ACL extendida puede filtrar basándose en dirección IP de origen y destino, protocolo (TCP/UDP/ICMP, etc.) y números de puerto, permitiendo un filtrado mucho más granular.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Control Plane Policing (CoPP)?

options.A: To provide QoS marking for user data traffic, not control-plane traffic, since CoPP has no visibility into CPU-destined packets at all or configuration
options.B: To replace the need for any ACLs on the device
options.C: To encrypt all traffic passing through the device's data plane
options.D: To protect the device's control-plane CPU from being overwhelmed by excessive or malicious traffic destined to the route processor, by rate-limiting or filtering that traffic

questions.explanation_es: CoPP protege la CPU del plano de control del dispositivo de ser sobrecargada por tráfico excesivo o malicioso destinado al procesador de rutas (por ejemplo, tráfico de gestión, protocolos de enrutamiento, o intentos de ataque), aplicando límites de tasa (rate-limiting) o filtrado específicamente a ese tráfico dirigido al propio dispositivo.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is token-based authentication (such as OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens) generally preferred over sending a username/password on every REST API call?

options.A: Tokens can be scoped, time-limited, and revoked independently of the user's actual credentials, reducing the exposure of long-term credentials on every request
options.B: Tokens never expire, unlike passwords
options.C: Sending username/password on every call is always more secure than tokens, since credentials never leave the client's own trusted network boundary
options.D: Token-based authentication removes the need for HTTPS

questions.explanation_es: Los tokens (como los bearer tokens de OAuth 2.0) pueden tener alcance limitado (scopes), expirar después de cierto tiempo, y ser revocados de forma independiente, reduciendo la exposición de las credenciales de largo plazo del usuario en cada solicitud, a diferencia de enviar usuario/contraseña repetidamente.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What does the security principle of 'defense in depth' refer to?

options.A: A specific Cisco product name
options.B: Implementing multiple, layered security controls (e.g., firewalls, IPS, endpoint security, segmentation) so that if one layer fails, others still provide protection
options.C: Only securing the network perimeter and trusting everything inside, which is exactly what defense in depth recommends as the most efficient approach, ignoring that a breached perimeter leaves internal systems exposed
options.D: Relying on a single, very strong security control to protect the entire network

questions.explanation_es: Defense in depth (defensa en profundidad) es el principio de implementar múltiples capas de controles de seguridad (firewalls, IPS, seguridad de endpoint, segmentación, etc.) de forma que si una capa falla o es comprometida, las demás sigan brindando protección, en lugar de depender de un único control.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the purpose of posture assessment in a NAC (Network Access Control) solution like Cisco ISE?

options.A: It only assigns an IP address to the endpoint
options.B: It configures the RADIUS attributes returned in an Access-Accept message, which determine the endpoint's VLAN assignment but do not evaluate whether the endpoint's software version or patch level meets any compliance requirement
options.C: It evaluates whether an endpoint meets defined security compliance criteria (e.g., updated antivirus, patches) before or after granting network access, potentially placing non-compliant devices into a restricted/remediation network
options.D: It replaces the need for 802.1X authentication

questions.explanation_es: El posture assessment evalúa si un endpoint cumple con criterios de seguridad definidos (antivirus actualizado, parches, cifrado de disco, etc.) antes o después de otorgar acceso a la red, y puede colocar a los dispositivos no conformes en una red restringida o de remediación hasta que cumplan los requisitos.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What capability distinguishes a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) from a traditional stateful firewall?

options.A: An NGFW adds application awareness/visibility, integrated intrusion prevention (IPS), and user identity-based policy, going beyond simple port/protocol-based stateful filtering
options.B: NGFWs cannot perform stateful inspection at all
options.C: Traditional stateful firewalls already include full application-layer inspection
options.D: An NGFW can only filter based on source/destination IP, just like a traditional firewall, with no additional application-layer visibility added by any inspection engine

questions.explanation_es: Un NGFW agrega capacidades de conciencia de aplicación (identificar qué app genera el tráfico más allá del puerto), IPS integrado, y políticas basadas en identidad de usuario, yendo más allá del simple filtrado stateful basado en puerto/protocolo que ofrece un firewall tradicional.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In Python, what is the key structural difference between a 'list' and a 'dictionary' (dict)?

options.A: A list is an ordered collection of items accessed by numeric index; a dictionary is a collection of key-value pairs accessed by a unique key
options.B: A dictionary cannot store more than one value
options.C: They are functionally identical data structures with different syntax, since Python internally represents every list as a dictionary with numeric keys
options.D: A list can only store strings, while a dictionary can store any type

questions.explanation_es: Una 'list' en Python es una colección ordenada de elementos, accesibles por índice numérico (ej. lista[0]); un 'dict' es una colección de pares clave-valor, accesibles por una clave única (ej. diccionario['nombre']), similar conceptualmente a un objeto JSON.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of the following is a valid, well-formed JSON object?

options.A: {'name': 'router1', 'status': 'up'}
options.B: {name: router1, status: up}
options.C: {"name": "router1", "status": "up"}
options.D: (name=router1, status=up)

questions.explanation_es: JSON exige que las claves y los valores de tipo string usen comillas dobles (") exclusivamente; las comillas simples (') no son válidas en JSON estándar, aunque sí lo sean en Python. La opción con comillas dobles es la única realmente bien formada.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When interpreting an API response, what does an HTTP status code in the 5xx range generally indicate, as opposed to a 4xx code?

options.A: 4xx and 5xx codes mean the same thing
options.B: 5xx codes indicate the request was processed successfully but the response body could not be generated in the requested format, requiring the client to resend the request with a different Accept header
options.C: 5xx codes always mean the request succeeded
options.D: A 5xx code indicates a server-side error (the server failed to fulfill a valid request), whereas a 4xx code indicates a client-side error (the request itself was invalid or unauthorized)

questions.explanation_es: Un código en el rango 5xx indica un error del lado del servidor (el servidor no pudo cumplir una solicitud que en principio era válida, ej. 500 Internal Server Error), mientras que un código 4xx indica un error del lado del cliente (la solicitud en sí era inválida, mal formada, o no autorizada, ej. 400, 401, 404).

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When an API call to Catalyst Center returns a 202 Accepted status with a taskId in the payload, what does this typically indicate?

options.A: The request was accepted for asynchronous processing, and the client should poll the task status endpoint using the returned taskId to check completion
options.B: 202 indicates the request completed synchronously and the taskId is only included for logging purposes, so the client does not need to poll any status endpoint before assuming the operation has finished
options.C: The request failed and must be resent immediately
options.D: The taskId is used only for billing purposes

questions.explanation_es: Un código 202 Accepted en Catalyst Center indica que la solicitud fue aceptada para procesamiento asíncrono (por ejemplo, una tarea de provisioning que toma tiempo); el cliente debe usar el taskId devuelto para consultar el endpoint de estado de tareas y verificar cuándo (y cómo) se completó la operación.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM (Embedded Event Manager) event detector would you use to trigger an applet based on CPU utilization crossing a defined threshold?

options.A: event cpu, which monitors CPU utilization against a configured threshold, or the equivalent resource-based event detector for that purpose
options.B: event snmp, watching a specific OID
options.C: event none, which never triggers automatically
options.D: event cli, matching a specific command entered by a user before or after it is executed on the device by any locally or remotely connected administrator

questions.explanation_es: Para disparar un applet EEM basado en el uso de CPU superando un umbral, se utiliza un detector de eventos orientado a recursos como 'event cpu' (o el detector de recursos correspondiente), que monitorea la utilización de CPU y dispara la acción configurada cuando se cruza el umbral definido. 'event cli' se usa para disparar en base a un comando ingresado, no en base a CPU.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is the key architectural difference between agent-based orchestration tools (like Chef or Puppet) and agentless tools (like Ansible)?

options.A: They are functionally identical in terms of architecture
options.B: Agent-based tools cannot be used to manage network devices
options.C: Agentless tools always require more installed software than agent-based tools, since every managed node needs its own dedicated local automation runtime installed and continuously running in the background at all times, regardless of whether any automation task is currently executing
options.D: Agent-based tools require software installed and running on the managed node to communicate with the central server; agentless tools typically connect to managed nodes over standard protocols (like SSH) without requiring persistent installed software

questions.explanation_es: Las herramientas basadas en agente (como Chef o Puppet) requieren que un software (agente) esté instalado y corriendo en el nodo gestionado para comunicarse con el servidor central; las herramientas agentless (como Ansible) típicamente se conectan a los nodos gestionados usando protocolos estándar (como SSH) sin requerir la instalación de software persistente en el nodo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which HTTP method is most appropriate for retrieving a resource's current state without modifying anything, mapping to the 'Read' operation in CRUD?

options.A: DELETE
options.B: PUT
options.C: POST
options.D: GET

questions.explanation_es: GET se usa para recuperar (leer) el estado actual de un recurso sin modificarlo, correspondiendo a la operación 'Read' en el modelo CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete). POST se usa típicamente para Create, PUT/PATCH para Update, y DELETE para Delete.

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what's the primary purpose of the underlay network?

options.A: Provides basic routed IP reachability between fabric nodes, under the VXLAN overlay
options.B: Replaces IP addressing entirely, relying only on MAC-based forwarding
options.C: Carries only wireless client traffic between APs and the WLC
options.D: To provide the policy and segmentation function of the fabric using Scalable Group Tags alone

questions.explanation_es: El underlay en SD-Access es una red enrutada que provee conectividad IP básica entre nodos del fabric; sobre ella se construye el overlay VXLAN con segmentación (SGT).

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: What defines a cloud-managed network design (e.g. Meraki-style, Catalyst Center cloud)?

options.A: A cloud/SaaS controller centralizes management, reducing on-prem infrastructure
options.B: All switching happens in the provider's data center; no local hardware is needed
options.C: It only applies to wireless; wired switches can't use a cloud dashboard
options.D: Every forwarding decision is made in the cloud, per packet

questions.explanation_es: El diseño gestionado por la nube centraliza gestión y monitoreo vía un controlador SaaS, aunque el reenvío de tráfico sigue ocurriendo en los dispositivos locales, no en la nube.

questions.name: Diseños de red
questions.question: In a 3-tier campus design, what's the primary role of the core layer?

options.A: Connects end devices directly and enforces per-port security policy
options.B: Provides a high-speed backbone between distribution blocks, with minimal policy
options.C: Applies detailed per-user QoS and security policy between distribution blocks
options.D: Performs DHCP relay for every VLAN in the campus

questions.explanation_es: La capa de núcleo provee un backbone de alta velocidad entre bloques de distribución, aplicando el mínimo de políticas para maximizar throughput y minimizar latencia.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How does GLBP differ from HSRP/VRRP in gateway utilization?

options.A: GLBP is just Cisco's name for VRRP, with no functional difference
options.B: GLBP load-balances actively across multiple routers at once; HSRP/VRRP use one active router per group
options.C: GLBP provides no redundancy on its own at all and requires a completely separate FHRP configured alongside it to work
options.D: GLBP can only have one router forwarding, exactly like HSRP

questions.explanation_es: GLBP permite balanceo de carga activo entre múltiples routers simultáneamente, a diferencia de HSRP/VRRP donde solo un router (activo/master) reenvía tráfico por grupo.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What does 'preemption' mean for an FHRP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) group?

options.A: It permanently disables the group after a failover until manually re-enabled
options.B: It lets a higher-priority router reclaim the active role once it comes back online
options.C: It refers to encrypting the FHRP hello messages between routers
options.D: It prevents any router from ever becoming active again after a failure

questions.explanation_es: La preemption permite que un router con mayor prioridad reclame el rol activo al volver a estar disponible, aunque otro router de menor prioridad ya lo haya asumido durante la falla.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What's the difference between 'N+1' and 'active/active' redundancy?

options.A: N+1 keeps one spare standby unit ready; active/active runs multiple units handling traffic at once
options.B: N+1 always means at least two spare units per active unit
options.C: Active/active means only one unit is ever operational at a time
options.D: They're the exact same redundancy concept, just described using different vendor-specific marketing terminology for each acronym

questions.explanation_es: N+1 tiene una unidad de respaldo lista para asumir el trabajo si una activa falla; active/active significa que múltiples unidades manejan tráfico simultáneamente, dando redundancia y distribución de carga.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What's the primary function of Cisco vManage in SD-WAN?

options.A: A centralized dashboard for configuring, monitoring, and managing the whole fabric
options.B: The only device responsible for forwarding customer data-plane traffic
options.C: Performing NAT traversal and initial orchestration
options.D: Replacing vSmart as the control-plane element distributing OMP routes

questions.explanation_es: vManage es el elemento de gestión centralizada en SD-WAN: provee el dashboard para configurar, monitorear y administrar toda la solución.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What information does OMP distribute in a Cisco SD-WAN fabric?

options.A: Primarily DHCP lease information for WAN Edge LAN hosts, synchronized between vSmarts for visibility
options.B: Only NTP time-sync data to keep WAN Edge clocks aligned
options.C: Routes, TLOC info, security keys, and policy between vSmart and WAN Edge routers
options.D: Only firmware update packages staged for WAN Edge routers

questions.explanation_es: OMP distribuye rutas, información de ubicación de transporte (TLOC), claves de seguridad para IPsec, y políticas entre vSmart y los WAN Edge routers.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What's the role of a WAN Edge router in Cisco SD-WAN?

options.A: It's identical in function to vManage, providing the dashboard, and never participates in the data plane at all, merely relaying vSmart stats
options.B: The data-plane element at branch/campus/DC sites, forwarding traffic over IPsec tunnels to other edges
options.C: Only control-plane functions; it never forwards actual traffic
options.D: Tracking and reporting software licensing compliance back to Cisco

questions.explanation_es: El WAN Edge router es el elemento de plano de datos, desplegado en las sedes, que efectivamente reenvía el tráfico de usuario estableciendo túneles IPsec hacia otros WAN Edges.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does centralized policy management in SD-WAN benefit segmentation across many sites?

options.A: It removes the need for any segmentation; every site shares one flat network
options.B: It only works for a single branch at a time, needing per-site policy management
options.C: Each branch requires its own unique, manually configured policy with no central coordination, leading to inconsistent segmentation and slower rollout
options.D: Consistent policy can be defined once and pushed to all sites, instead of configuring each router manually

questions.explanation_es: Con SD-WAN, la política de segmentación se puede definir una sola vez y distribuirse automáticamente a todas las sedes, mejorando consistencia y reduciendo errores.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What's a common benefit of Direct Internet Access (DIA) at branch sites?

options.A: It's only relevant for MPLS-only deployments, since broadband circuits already provide direct access with no benefit at all for LTE branches
options.B: Internet-bound traffic goes straight out locally instead of backhauling through a data center, cutting latency
options.C: It disables all security inspection at the branch, sending traffic unfiltered
options.D: It forces all internet traffic through a single central hub, increasing latency

questions.explanation_es: DIA permite que el tráfico a internet salga directamente desde la sucursal en lugar de hacer backhaul a un data center central, reduciendo la latencia percibida.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is high-availability design for SD-WAN controllers an important consideration?

options.A: They're central to config, routing, and orchestration; their failure impairs managing the overlay
options.B: Controllers have no operational impact if they fail, since WAN Edges keep forwarding fully independently forever regardless of deployment size
options.C: SD-WAN controllers can't be made redundant regardless of deployment size
options.D: Only vManage needs redundancy; vSmart and vBond can be single points of failure

questions.explanation_es: Al centralizar configuración, plano de control y orquestación, la falla de estos controladores sin diseño de HA puede afectar significativamente la gestión de la red.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What's the role of a Fabric Edge Node in Cisco SD-Access?

options.A: It replaces the control plane node, keeping its own host-tracking database independently
options.B: It's where endpoints connect, VXLAN-encapsulating/decapsulating their traffic into the fabric
options.C: It's the exclusive point of connection to external networks
options.D: It only manages the Map-Server database tracking EID-to-RLOC mappings

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Edge Node es donde se conectan los endpoints, encapsulando/desencapsulando su tráfico en VXLAN para transportarlo dentro de la fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What data-plane encapsulation does SD-Access use between fabric nodes?

options.A: MPLS labels, requiring every node to run a label distribution protocol
options.B: VXLAN, which also carries the SGT needed for policy enforcement
options.C: GRE with no VLAN or segmentation information
options.D: Plain 802.1Q tagging only, with no overlay encapsulation

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access usa VXLAN como encapsulación del plano de datos; el encabezado VXLAN también transporta la SGT, permitiendo aplicar políticas de forma consistente.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What does a 'fabric-enabled' WLC primarily allow in SD-Access?

options.A: Wireless traffic to bypass all fabric policy entirely, since access points forward it directly to the upstream router untouched
options.B: Eliminating the need for APs, with clients associating directly to the edge switch
options.C: Wireless traffic to integrate into the fabric overlay, with the WLC registering clients in the control plane
options.D: Wired traffic to tunnel over wireless links when a wired port is unavailable

questions.explanation_es: Un WLC fabric-enabled integra el tráfico inalámbrico directamente en el overlay del fabric, registrando clientes inalámbricos en el plano de control igual que los cableados.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What's important about SD-Access's L2/L3 boundary when extending a traditional VLAN into the fabric?

options.A: VLANs can't exist in an SD-Access fabric at all; segmentation is purely SGT-based
options.B: SD-Access uses a routed access model with VXLAN overlay per VN, so VLANs must be mapped carefully into fabric VNs/IP pools
options.C: There's no need to consider Layer 2/Layer 3 boundaries in SD-Access at all, since the fabric flattens everything into one broadcast domain
options.D: SD-Access carries VLANs end-to-end via 802.1Q trunks between edge nodes

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de una red tradicional, SD-Access usa un modelo de acceso enrutado con overlay VXLAN por red virtual; extender una VLAN tradicional requiere mapearla a esa red virtual y su IP pool.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the difference between congestion management (queuing) and congestion avoidance in QoS?

options.A: They're identical, both dropping packets proactively before a queue fills
options.B: Congestion avoidance only applies to UDP traffic, since TCP already handles its own flow control and never needs a separate avoidance mechanism
options.C: Management (LLQ/CBWFQ) schedules traffic during congestion; avoidance (WRED) drops proactively to prevent worse congestion
options.D: Congestion management only works on wireless interfaces

questions.explanation_es: La gestión de congestión (colas) prioriza el tráfico cuando ya hay congestión; la prevención (WRED) descarta paquetes proactivamente antes de que la cola se llene, evitando sincronización global de TCP.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the difference between traffic policing and traffic shaping?

options.A: Policing can only be applied outbound, shaping only inbound
options.B: They're functionally identical QoS mechanisms that both buffer excess traffic to smooth bursts without ever dropping a single packet
options.C: Shaping always drops traffic immediately, while policing buffers it
options.D: Policing drops/re-marks traffic exceeding a rate immediately; shaping buffers excess to smooth it over time

questions.explanation_es: El policing descarta o re-marca de inmediato el tráfico que excede la tasa, sin buffer. El shaping almacena el excedente para suavizarlo, a costa de mayor latencia potencial.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's a 'trust boundary' in QoS design?

options.A: The point (often the access edge) where the network decides whether to trust incoming QoS markings or re-mark them
options.B: A physical firewall between two QoS domains that inspects and re-marks traffic
options.C: The maximum bandwidth an interface allows before QoS starts dropping traffic
options.D: A boundary that only exists in wireless networks, since wired switches always trust incoming markings by default with no equivalent concept

questions.explanation_es: El trust boundary es el punto de la red donde se decide si confiar en las marcas de QoS entrantes o reclasificarlas, evitando que dispositivos no confiables se marquen alta prioridad indebidamente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What does a hypervisor fundamentally do with a server's hardware resources?

options.A: Virtualizes CPU, memory, storage, and network, partitioning them into isolated VMs
options.B: It removes the need for any physical hardware at all to run VMs, replacing servers entirely
options.C: Physically duplicates the server hardware for each VM
options.D: Only virtualizes storage, never CPU or memory

questions.explanation_es: El hipervisor virtualiza los recursos físicos de un servidor, particionándolos en múltiples VMs aisladas que comparten el mismo hardware subyacente.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What does Fault Tolerance (FT) provide, as distinct from live migration (vMotion)?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any shared storage infrastructure
options.B: A live secondary VM copy running in lockstep, taking over instantly with zero downtime if the primary host fails
options.C: FT is identical to vMotion in every respect, just marketed under a completely different product name for licensing
options.D: It only protects against app crashes, not hardware failures

questions.explanation_es: FT mantiene una copia secundaria de la VM en lockstep en otro host; si el primario falla, la secundaria asume el control de inmediato, sin downtime ni pérdida de estado.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What is 'VRF-lite,' and how does it differ from a full MPLS VPN using VRFs?

options.A: There's no meaningful difference between the two
options.B: It requires MPLS labels exactly like a full VPN deployment would need across every hop, with no simpler alternative
options.C: VRF-lite only works on a single interface, never across devices
options.D: It implements VRFs without MPLS labels, using separate interfaces per VRF between hops instead

questions.explanation_es: VRF-lite implementa múltiples VRFs sin usar etiquetas MPLS entre saltos; en su lugar usa interfaces o subinterfaces separadas por VRF, más simple que una VPN MPLS completa.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What's a key benefit of VRFs for multi-tenancy on one physical router?

options.A: Each tenant still needs a completely separate physical router
options.B: VRFs eliminate the need for any IP addressing plan across tenants entirely, since every VRF gets its own space automatically
options.C: VRFs can only support a single tenant per physical device
options.D: Multiple tenants share one device with fully isolated tables, even with overlapping IPs

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs permiten que múltiples tenants compartan el mismo router físico manteniendo tablas de enrutamiento aisladas, incluso con rangos IP solapados.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What's the key difference between IPsec tunnel mode and transport mode?

options.A: Tunnel mode encrypts the whole original packet and adds a new outer IP header; transport mode only encrypts the payload
options.B: Tunnel mode can only use AH, never ESP
options.C: They're functionally identical, just named differently
options.D: Transport mode encrypts the entire packet including the header; tunnel mode only encrypts the payload, the reverse of reality

questions.explanation_es: El modo túnel cifra el paquete IP completo y agrega un nuevo encabezado IP externo. El modo transporte cifra solo el payload, preservando el encabezado original.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What's the core conceptual separation LISP introduces versus traditional IP addressing?

options.A: Identity (EID) from location (RLOC), allowing mobility without renumbering
options.B: LISP only applies to Layer 2 MAC addresses, never IP
options.C: LISP merges identity and location into one address, unlike traditional IP
options.D: LISP eliminates the need for any IP addressing scheme

questions.explanation_es: LISP separa identidad (EID) de ubicación (RLOC), permitiendo que un endpoint se mueva sin necesitar renumerar su dirección — la base también usada por SD-Access.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: How many bits does the VLAN ID field occupy in an 802.1Q tag, and what is the resulting range of usable VLAN IDs?

options.A: 8 bits, allowing only 256 VLANs, matching the size of a single IPv4 address octet
options.B: 12 bits, allowing VLAN IDs from 0-4095, with 1-4094 typically usable (0 and 4095 reserved)
options.C: 4 bits, allowing only 16 VLANs total, which matches the size of the original Ethernet priority field
options.D: 16 bits, allowing over 65,000 VLANs, matching the size of a standard Ethernet frame's length field

questions.explanation_es: El campo VLAN ID en la etiqueta 802.1Q ocupa 12 bits, lo que permite valores de 0 a 4095; en la práctica, los IDs 1 a 4094 son los usables para configuración normal (0 y 4095 están reservados para propósitos especiales).

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What happens to a frame received untagged on an 802.1Q trunk port, assuming default configuration?

options.A: It is automatically dropped as invalid, since 802.1Q trunk ports never accept untagged frames
options.B: It is treated as belonging to VLAN 0 always, regardless of how the native VLAN is configured
options.C: It causes the trunk to shut down immediately due to a native VLAN mismatch error
options.D: It is treated as belonging to the native VLAN configured on that trunk

questions.explanation_es: Por comportamiento estándar de 802.1Q, una trama recibida sin etiqueta en un puerto trunk se considera perteneciente a la VLAN nativa configurada en ese trunk. Por eso es crítico que la VLAN nativa coincida en ambos extremos del enlace.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Which mitigation is commonly recommended to reduce the risk of VLAN hopping attacks via double-tagging or DTP manipulation?

options.A: Enable DTP auto-negotiation on every port to simplify configuration and reduce the administrative overhead of managing trunk links manually — since DTP is generally considered to authenticate the far end
options.B: VLAN hopping cannot be mitigated in any way once a trunk port has been configured on a switch
options.C: Use VLAN 1 as the native VLAN on all trunks for consistency across the entire switching infrastructure
options.D: Explicitly disable DTP negotiation on trunk/access ports (set them statically) and avoid using VLAN 1 as the native VLAN or for management traffic

questions.explanation_es: Para reducir el riesgo de ataques de VLAN hopping (por doble etiquetado o manipulación de DTP), se recomienda deshabilitar la negociación dinámica de DTP (configurando explícitamente trunk o access según corresponda) y evitar usar VLAN 1 como VLAN nativa o para tráfico de gestión, entre otras buenas prácticas de hardening.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What does the PCP (Priority Code Point) field within an 802.1Q tag represent?

options.A: An encryption key used to protect the frame's payload as it crosses an untrusted trunk link
options.B: The VLAN ID of the frame, duplicated here for redundancy in case the main 802.1Q VLAN field elsewhere in the tag is corrupted within the same 802.1Q tag structure
options.C: A 3-bit field used to convey Layer 2 QoS priority (commonly referred to as CoS), allowing switches to prioritize frames based on this marking
options.D: The source MAC address of the sender, encoded in a compressed 3-bit representation

questions.explanation_es: El campo PCP (Priority Code Point), comúnmente conocido como CoS (Class of Service), es un campo de 3 bits dentro de la etiqueta 802.1Q que se usa para transmitir prioridad de QoS a nivel de Capa 2, permitiendo que los switches prioricen tramas según este valor.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: For an EtherChannel bundle to form correctly between two switches, what must generally match across the member links?

options.A: Only the port numbers need to be identical on both switches, with no other configuration requirements
options.B: Only the physical cable length needs to match within a few centimeters of tolerance
options.C: Key parameters such as speed, duplex, trunk mode/allowed VLANs (if trunked), and native VLAN must be consistent across all member ports on both sides
options.D: Nothing needs to match; any combination of speeds and duplex settings works fine across every member link in the bundle regardless of vendor or hardware platform

questions.explanation_es: Para que un EtherChannel se forme correctamente, los puertos miembros deben tener parámetros consistentes entre sí y entre ambos extremos: velocidad, duplex, y si es trunk, el modo trunk, las VLANs permitidas y la VLAN nativa deben coincidir; de lo contrario el bundle puede no formarse o comportarse de forma inconsistente.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How many active links does a standard Cisco EtherChannel bundle typically support (without special stacking technology)?

options.A: Only 1 link, since EtherChannel is meant for single-link redundancy only
options.B: Up to 8 active links
options.C: Only 2 links maximum
options.D: Up to 16 active links always

questions.explanation_es: Un EtherChannel estándar en Cisco soporta típicamente hasta 8 enlaces activos en el bundle (con posibilidad de enlaces adicionales en modo standby usando LACP en algunas plataformas), permitiendo agregación de ancho de banda y redundancia.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What risk arises if one side of a link is configured as an EtherChannel bundle while the other side treats the links as individual (non-bundled) switchports?

options.A: The link will always work correctly with no issues, regardless of the mismatch
options.B: The mismatch is automatically detected and corrected by DTP, which renegotiates both sides into a consistent bundled configuration without any administrator intervention required, restoring full connectivity within seconds of the mismatch being introduced
options.C: It can create a Layer 2 loop, since the non-bundled side may forward the same broadcast/multicast frame out multiple individual links that the bundled side sees as a single logical link, confusing STP and potentially causing a broadcast storm
options.D: Only performance is reduced, with no risk of loops forming anywhere in the topology

questions.explanation_es: Un desajuste de EtherChannel (un lado con el bundle configurado y el otro tratando los enlaces como puertos individuales) puede generar un loop de Capa 2, ya que el lado no-bundled puede reenviar la misma trama de broadcast/multicast por múltiples enlaces individuales que el lado bundled interpreta como un solo enlace lógico, confundiendo a STP y potencialmente causando una tormenta de broadcast.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What problem does MST (Multiple Spanning Tree) solve compared to running PVST+ (Per-VLAN Spanning Tree) with hundreds of VLANs?

options.A: MST requires running a completely separate spanning tree for every single VLAN, just like PVST+ does, providing no CPU or control-plane savings across a large campus
options.B: MST eliminates the need for any spanning tree protocol at all, relying purely on static Layer 2 paths instead
options.C: MST maps multiple VLANs to a smaller number of spanning-tree instances, reducing the CPU/control-plane overhead of running a separate STP instance per VLAN
options.D: MST can only be used with a single VLAN, making it impractical for any network with more than one VLAN

questions.explanation_es: MST permite mapear múltiples VLANs a un número reducido de instancias de spanning tree (en lugar de una instancia por VLAN como en PVST+), reduciendo significativamente la carga de CPU y de control-plane en switches con cientos de VLANs, manteniendo la posibilidad de tener topologías distintas por grupo de VLANs si es necesario.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is BPDU Guard commonly enabled together with PortFast on access ports?

options.A: PortFast skips the normal STP listening/learning states for fast connectivity on end-host ports, but this creates risk if a switch is accidentally connected there; BPDU Guard protects against that by shutting down the port if a BPDU is received
options.B: BPDU Guard is required for PortFast to function at all, and PortFast cannot be enabled without it
options.C: PortFast alone already disables the port automatically upon receiving a BPDU, so BPDU Guard is only actually needed on trunk ports rather than on the access ports where PortFast is enabled
options.D: They are never used together in practice, since PortFast and BPDU Guard serve unrelated purposes

questions.explanation_es: PortFast salta los estados normales de listening/learning de STP para dar conectividad rápida en puertos de host final, pero esto es riesgoso si por error se conecta un switch en ese puerto (podría causar loops). BPDU Guard complementa a PortFast apagando el puerto automáticamente si llega a recibir una BPDU, protegiendo contra esa conexión indebida.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does RSTP (802.1w) convergence time generally compare to legacy 802.1D STP?

options.A: RSTP requires manual intervention to converge, unlike 802.1D which converges fully automatically without any configuration
options.B: RSTP converges significantly faster (often sub-second, using mechanisms like proposal/agreement), whereas legacy 802.1D STP can take 30-50 seconds to converge through its listening/learning states
options.C: 802.1D always converges faster than RSTP in every topology, contrary to common belief among network engineers
options.D: RSTP and 802.1D have identical convergence times in all cases, since RSTP is simply a renamed version of legacy 802.1D with no functional or algorithmic changes at all under every possible network condition and topology size

questions.explanation_es: RSTP converge de forma mucho más rápida que el STP clásico 802.1D (a menudo en menos de un segundo, gracias a mecanismos como el intercambio de propuesta/acuerdo entre switches vecinos), mientras que 802.1D puede tardar entre 30 y 50 segundos en converger al pasar por sus estados de listening y learning con temporizadores fijos.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What does Loop Guard protect against in an STP topology?

options.A: It prevents a non-designated port (root or alternate) from erroneously transitioning to the forwarding/designated state due to a unidirectional link failure where BPDUs simply stop arriving
options.B: It prevents any port from ever becoming the root port, regardless of the BPDUs it receives or its configured priority, effectively disabling the root port role entirely
options.C: It is functionally identical to BPDU Guard, differing only in the specific CLI command used to enable it
options.D: It only applies to trunk ports carrying VLAN 1, having no effect on any other VLAN's spanning tree instance

questions.explanation_es: Loop Guard protege contra la situación en la que un puerto root o alternate deja de recibir BPDUs (por ejemplo, por una falla unidireccional del enlace) y, al no recibirlas, erróneamente asumiría que puede pasar a estado forwarding/designado, lo cual podría crear un loop. Loop Guard mantiene el puerto en un estado bloqueado (loop-inconsistent) hasta que vuelvan a recibirse BPDUs normalmente.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: By default, which two metrics does EIGRP's composite metric calculation primarily use (in default K-value configuration)?

options.A: Only reliability
options.B: Hop count and MTU only
options.C: Only hop count, exactly like RIP
options.D: Bandwidth and delay

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto (con los valores K estándar), la métrica compuesta de EIGRP se calcula principalmente usando el ancho de banda mínimo del camino y la suma de los retardos (delay) de las interfaces atravesadas; otros factores (carga, confiabilidad) están disponibles pero no se usan por defecto en la fórmula estándar.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the difference between an OSPF Type 1 (Router LSA) and a Type 2 (Network LSA)?

options.A: A Network LSA describes external routes redistributed into OSPF from another routing protocol entirely
options.B: A Router LSA is only used in totally stubby areas, and has no meaning in a standard OSPF area
options.C: A Router LSA is originated by the DR to describe all routers attached to a multi-access segment, while a Network LSA describes a single router's own links and their costs within the area
options.D: A Router LSA describes a router's own links and their costs within an area; a Network LSA is originated by the DR on a multi-access segment and describes all routers attached to that segment

questions.explanation_es: La LSA Tipo 1 (Router LSA) es originada por cada router y describe sus propios enlaces y costos dentro de un área; la LSA Tipo 2 (Network LSA) es originada por el DR (Designated Router) en un segmento de acceso múltiple y describe todos los routers conectados a ese segmento, sirviendo para representar la topología de la red multiacceso de forma más eficiente.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What does the EIGRP 'variance' command allow?

options.A: It disables load balancing entirely, forcing all traffic onto the single best path regardless of other available routes with similar or better metrics anywhere in the topology table — making 'variance' an administrative-distance override
options.B: Unequal-cost load balancing across multiple paths, as long as the alternate paths' metric is within the configured variance multiple of the best metric and they are feasible successors
options.C: It is used to change the EIGRP autonomous system number, allowing routers in different ASes to peer directly
options.D: It only affects equal-cost paths, having no effect on unequal-cost ones, which EIGRP never supports for load balancing

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'variance' en EIGRP permite balanceo de carga de costo desigual (unequal-cost load balancing): rutas alternativas cuyo métrica esté dentro de un múltiplo configurado (variance) de la mejor métrica, y que además sean feasible successors (garantizando ausencia de loops), pueden usarse simultáneamente para distribuir tráfico junto con la ruta principal.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why is DR/BDR election necessary on an OSPF multi-access (broadcast) network segment, but not on a point-to-point link?

options.A: DR/BDR election exists purely for historical reasons and serves no functional purpose today
options.B: On a multi-access segment, without a DR every router would form full adjacencies with every other router, causing an excessive number of adjacencies and LSA flooding; the DR/BDR reduces this by centralizing adjacency formation and LSA distribution
options.C: DR/BDR election is only relevant for EIGRP, not OSPF
options.D: DR/BDR election also takes place on point-to-point links, but since only two routers are ever present on that link type, the DR role is simply assigned to whichever router has the higher router ID without any actual election process occurring

questions.explanation_es: En un segmento de acceso múltiple (broadcast), sin un DR cada router formaría adyacencias completas con todos los demás routers del segmento, generando una cantidad excesiva de adyacencias y de inundación de LSAs (n*(n-1)/2 adyacencias). El DR (y BDR como respaldo) centraliza la formación de adyacencias y la distribución de LSAs, reduciendo drásticamente esa sobrecarga. En enlaces punto a punto, al haber solo dos routers, no se necesita esta optimización.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the effect of configuring the 'passive-interface' command on an OSPF-enabled interface?

options.A: It completely removes the interface's network from being advertised by OSPF in any Link State Advertisement at all, effectively hiding that subnet from the rest of the network for any router in the area
options.B: It disables IP routing on that interface entirely, effectively shutting down all Layer 3 forwarding through it
options.C: It forces the interface to become the DR regardless of its configured OSPF priority value
options.D: OSPF continues to advertise that interface's network in its LSAs, but stops sending/receiving OSPF hello packets on it, preventing neighbor adjacencies from forming over that interface

questions.explanation_es: 'Passive-interface' hace que OSPF deje de enviar/recibir paquetes hello por esa interfaz (evitando que se formen adyacencias de vecino ahí), pero la red de esa interfaz sigue siendo anunciada normalmente en las LSAs del router, útil por ejemplo en interfaces hacia LANs de usuarios donde no se espera un vecino OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On which OSPF network types is DR/BDR election performed, versus not performed?

options.A: DR/BDR election occurs on broadcast and NBMA network types; it does NOT occur on point-to-point network types, since only two routers are involved
options.B: DR/BDR election only occurs on point-to-point networks, since only two routers are ever involved there
options.C: DR/BDR election occurs on all OSPF network types without exception, including point-to-point and point-to-multipoint links
options.D: DR/BDR election rarely OSPF network type, since OSPF always forms full adjacencies with every neighbor on every segment

questions.explanation_es: La elección de DR/BDR ocurre en los tipos de red broadcast y NBMA (donde múltiples routers comparten el mismo segmento); en enlaces punto a punto no se realiza elección de DR/BDR, ya que al haber solo dos routers no existe la necesidad de optimizar la cantidad de adyacencias.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Where is OSPF route summarization typically configured for inter-area routes, versus for external (redistributed) routes?

options.A: OSPF does not support any form of route summarization
options.B: Both types of summarization can only be configured on the backbone area 0 router directly, regardless of role
options.C: Inter-area summarization is configured on the ABR (Area Border Router); summarization of external routes is configured on the ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router)
options.D: Inter-area summarization is configured on the ASBR using the 'area range' command, while summarization of external redistributed routes is configured on the ABR using the 'summary-address' command

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización de rutas inter-área se configura en el ABR (Area Border Router), que resume las rutas de un área antes de anunciarlas hacia otras áreas. La sumarización de rutas externas (redistribuidas desde otro protocolo) se configura en el ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router), el punto donde esas rutas externas entran al dominio OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What does the OSPFv3 'address family' (AF) feature allow?

options.A: It removes IPv6 support from OSPFv3 entirely, converting it back into an IPv4-only routing protocol
options.B: It replaces the need for OSPFv2 entirely in dual-stack networks, making OSPFv2 fully obsolete for IPv4 routing in any modern enterprise or service provider deployment today
options.C: It allows a single OSPFv3 process to support both IPv4 and IPv6 unicast topologies, maintaining separate address-family-specific routing information within one process
options.D: It is used only to configure authentication, with no relation to IPv4/IPv6 support or address-family separation

questions.explanation_es: La característica de Address Family (AF) en OSPFv3 permite que un único proceso OSPFv3 soporte topologías tanto IPv4 como IPv6 unicast, manteniendo información de enrutamiento separada por familia de direcciones dentro del mismo proceso, simplificando el despliegue dual-stack sin necesitar procesos OSPFv2 y OSPFv3 completamente independientes.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the BGP AS_PATH attribute?

options.A: It only records the next-hop IP address of the neighbor that most recently advertised the route
options.B: It is used for encryption of BGP updates exchanged between peers, ensuring that AS path information cannot be read or modified by any intermediate device along the path between the two autonomous systems during transit across the internet
options.C: It has no impact on best-path selection, serving purely as an informational field for troubleshooting
options.D: It records the sequence of autonomous systems a route has traversed, used both for loop prevention (a router rejects a route containing its own AS) and as a factor in best-path selection (shorter AS_PATH generally preferred)

questions.explanation_es: El atributo AS_PATH registra la secuencia de sistemas autónomos que ha atravesado una ruta; se usa tanto para prevención de loops (un router rechaza una ruta que ya contiene su propio AS en el path) como para la selección de mejor ruta (un AS_PATH más corto es generalmente preferido, todo lo demás igual).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the default administrative distance difference between eBGP and iBGP routes on a Cisco router?

options.A: eBGP has an administrative distance of 20, while iBGP has 200, making eBGP routes preferred over iBGP routes (and over most IGPs) by default when both are present for the same prefix
options.B: Administrative distance does not apply to BGP routes at all, since BGP always overrides every other routing source routing table
options.C: iBGP has a lower administrative distance than eBGP, making iBGP routes preferred whenever both exist
options.D: Both eBGP and iBGP have the same administrative distance of 20, making them equally preferred by default

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto en Cisco, eBGP tiene una distancia administrativa de 20, mientras que iBGP tiene 200. Esto hace que, ante la misma prefijo aprendida por ambos, la ruta eBGP sea preferida (menor distancia administrativa = más confiable), y de hecho eBGP suele preferirse incluso sobre la mayoría de los IGPs internos.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is required for two routers to establish an eBGP neighbor relationship?

options.A: They must use IGP metrics identical to each other before any eBGP session can be established
options.B: They must always be in the same AS number, exactly like iBGP peers within a single autonomous system
options.C: They must be configured with different autonomous system (AS) numbers, and typically be directly reachable (by default, one hop away unless multihop is configured)
options.D: They require no configuration of AS numbers at all, since eBGP determines them automatically from the BGP updates exchanged during session establishment

questions.explanation_es: Para establecer una relación de vecino eBGP, los routers deben pertenecer a AS distintos (a diferencia de iBGP, donde comparten el mismo AS), y típicamente deben ser alcanzables directamente (por defecto, a un salto de distancia, salvo que se configure ebgp-multihop para vecinos más alejados).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the purpose of BGP route aggregation (using the 'aggregate-address' command)?

options.A: To combine multiple more-specific prefixes into a single summarized prefix advertised to neighbors, reducing the size of the routing table advertised externally
options.B: To disable the advertisement of any routes at all, effectively creating a full BGP route filter
options.C: To split a single prefix into many smaller, more-specific prefixes automatically, the opposite of what BGP route aggregation actually accomplishes into the routing table
options.D: To encrypt BGP route advertisements exchanged between two neighboring autonomous systems

questions.explanation_es: La agregación de rutas en BGP (comando 'aggregate-address') combina múltiples prefijos más específicos en un único prefijo resumido que se anuncia a los vecinos, reduciendo el tamaño de la tabla de rutas anunciada externamente y simplificando la topología vista por otros AS.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a Policy-Based Routing (PBR) route-map, which of the following is a typical 'match' criterion used to identify traffic for special routing treatment?

options.A: PBR route-maps only support matching on VLAN ID, with no ability to match Layer 3 or Layer 4 criteria
options.B: An access-list matching specific source addresses, or the packet length, among other criteria defined in the route-map
options.C: PBR route-maps can only match on destination IP address, exactly like normal routing, offering no additional flexibility
options.D: PBR cannot use access-lists as match criteria within a route-map

questions.explanation_es: En un route-map de PBR, un criterio de 'match' típico es una access-list que identifica el tráfico según su dirección de origen (u otros campos permitidos por la ACL), o también se puede hacer match por longitud de paquete, entre otros criterios; luego se define un 'set' para indicar el tratamiento especial (por ejemplo, el next-hop a usar) para ese tráfico coincidente.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Why is NTP authentication (e.g., using MD5 or SHA keys) recommended in a production network?

options.A: It is required for NTP to function at all, even in a lab environment with no external time source configured
options.B: It prevents a malicious or unauthorized source from injecting false time information, which could otherwise disrupt logging correlation, certificate validation, or other time-sensitive processes
options.C: It encrypts all network traffic passing through the router, not just NTP, providing full payload confidentiality for every protocol traversing the device, including HTTP and SSH
options.D: It encrypts the NTP time value itself so that an eavesdropper cannot read the synchronized time, but it does not protect the router against a spoofed source injecting a false time update

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación NTP (usando claves MD5/SHA) previene que una fuente maliciosa o no autorizada inyecte información de tiempo falsa, lo cual podría afectar procesos sensibles al tiempo como la correlación de logs, validación de certificados digitales, o el registro correcto de eventos de seguridad.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What is the role of the 'grandmaster clock' in a PTP (Precision Time Protocol) domain?

options.A: It is the primary time reference source for the entire PTP domain, from which all other clocks in the hierarchy synchronize (directly or indirectly)
options.B: It refers to any client device receiving time from the network, regardless of its position in the PTP hierarchy or its distance from the grandmaster
options.C: It is a backup clock that only activates if all other clocks fail, remaining completely passive otherwise
options.D: It performs no synchronization function in PTP, serving only as a passive monitoring device on the network

questions.explanation_es: El grandmaster clock es la fuente de referencia de tiempo principal para todo el dominio PTP; todos los demás relojes en la jerarquía (boundary clocks, ordinary clocks) sincronizan su tiempo directa o indirectamente a partir de este reloj maestro, seleccionado mediante el Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA).

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What is the difference between Static NAT and Dynamic NAT?

options.A: They are functionally identical, differing only in configuration syntax
options.B: Static NAT creates a fixed, permanent one-to-one mapping between a specific inside local and inside global address; Dynamic NAT maps addresses from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis, without a fixed permanent mapping
options.C: Static NAT selects an address from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis, while Dynamic NAT always maps a host to one fixed address configured in advance, meaning Dynamic NAT actually behaves more predictably in address assignment
options.D: Static NAT can only be used with IPv6, and Dynamic NAT only with IPv4

questions.explanation_es: Static NAT crea un mapeo fijo y permanente uno-a-uno entre una dirección local interna específica y una dirección global externa específica (útil por ejemplo para servidores que deben ser siempre alcanzables en la misma IP pública). Dynamic NAT, en cambio, asigna direcciones de un pool de forma dinámica, por orden de llegada, sin una asignación fija permanente.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: In Cisco NAT terminology, what does 'inside local' refer to, as opposed to 'inside global'?

options.A: 'Inside local' and 'inside global' both refer to addresses on the external network, differing only in whether the address belongs to a remote host or to the NAT device's own outside interface
options.B: 'Inside global' refers to an external host's address, not an internal host's translated address, a distinction that only applies under PAT and not under static or dynamic NAT configurations on the router, with static and dynamic NAT instead using the term interchangeably
options.C: These terms only apply to IPv6 NAT, not IPv4
options.D: 'Inside local' is the address of an internal host as seen within the internal (private) network; 'inside global' is the translated address that represents that same internal host as seen from the external (public) network

questions.explanation_es: 'Inside local' es la dirección de un host interno tal como se ve dentro de la red privada (típicamente una IP privada RFC 1918); 'inside global' es la dirección traducida que representa a ese mismo host interno visto desde la red externa/pública, después de aplicar NAT.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: What is the standard virtual MAC address format used by HSRP (version 1) for a given group?

options.A: FFFF.FFFF.FFFF, the standard broadcast MAC
options.B: A completely random MAC address generated at each failover
options.C: 0000.0C07.ACxx, where 'xx' represents the HSRP group number in hexadecimal
options.D: The real burned-in MAC address of the active router's physical interface, with no virtual MAC

questions.explanation_es: HSRP versión 1 utiliza una dirección MAC virtual con el formato estándar 0000.0C07.ACxx, donde 'xx' representa el número de grupo HSRP en hexadecimal, permitiendo que los hosts sigan usando la misma MAC virtual sin importar cuál router físico esté actualmente activo.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Regarding default preemption behavior, how do HSRP and VRRP differ?

options.A: In VRRP, preemption is enabled by default; in HSRP, preemption is disabled by default and must be explicitly configured
options.B: Both protocols disable preemption by default with no differences between their default configurations at all
options.C: Neither protocol supports preemption at all, requiring a completely manual failover process every time
options.D: In HSRP, preemption is enabled by default and takes effect immediately once a higher-priority router comes online; in VRRP, preemption must be explicitly enabled, since it is disabled by default

questions.explanation_es: Una diferencia clave a tener presente: en VRRP la preferencia (preemption) está habilitada por defecto, mientras que en HSRP está deshabilitada por defecto y debe configurarse explícitamente si se desea que un router de mayor prioridad reclame el rol activo al recuperarse.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol)?

options.A: It is used to encrypt multicast traffic between the source and every receiver in the group
options.B: It allows hosts to inform their local multicast router about which multicast groups they want to receive traffic for, enabling the router to determine where to forward multicast traffic on the local segment
options.C: It only operates between routers, never between a host and its local router, making it purely a router-to-router protocol used for multicast tree maintenance across an entire routed enterprise domain and its RP
options.D: It replaces the need for PIM entirely across a routed network

questions.explanation_es: IGMP es el protocolo que permite a los hosts informar a su router multicast local a qué grupos multicast desean unirse (join), permitiendo que el router determine si debe reenviar tráfico multicast hacia ese segmento local. PIM, en cambio, se encarga del enrutamiento de multicast entre routers a través de la red.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of MSDP (Multicast Source Discovery Protocol)?

options.A: It is used only within a single PIM-SM domain, never between domains, making it purely an intra-domain protocol with no role across separate autonomous multicast networks
options.B: It allows Rendezvous Points (RPs) in different PIM-SM domains to share information about active multicast sources, enabling inter-domain multicast source discovery
options.C: It replaces PIM entirely as the multicast routing protocol, eliminating the need for any RP configuration
options.D: It is used for IGMP snooping on Layer 2 switches, with no role in Layer 3 multicast routing at all

questions.explanation_es: MSDP permite que los Rendezvous Points (RP) de distintos dominios PIM-SM compartan información sobre fuentes multicast activas, habilitando el descubrimiento de fuentes multicast entre dominios independientes (inter-domain), algo que PIM-SM por sí solo no resuelve dentro de un único dominio.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: How does traceroute discover each hop along a path?

options.A: It queries every router along the path via SNMP
options.B: It sends a single packet with a fixed TTL of 255
options.C: It sends probes with rising TTL; each hop that zeroes it replies with Time Exceeded
options.D: It requires every hop to be manually configured in advance, with no dynamic discovery

questions.explanation_es: Traceroute envía paquetes de prueba con TTL creciente; cada router que lleva el TTL a cero responde con ICMP Time Exceeded, revelando el camino salto por salto.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What underlying mechanism does the 'ping' utility use to test basic reachability to a destination?

options.A: ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages
options.B: TCP three-way handshake
options.C: DNS queries
options.D: SNMP GET requests

questions.explanation_es: Ping utiliza mensajes ICMP Echo Request (enviados al destino) y Echo Reply (respondidos por el destino) para probar la conectividad básica y medir el tiempo de ida y vuelta (RTT), sin necesidad de establecer una sesión TCP.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: How does NetFlow differ from SPAN in what data it collects?

options.A: SPAN only provides summarized statistics, never full packets
options.B: NetFlow copies every full packet, the same way SPAN does
options.C: NetFlow collects flow metadata; SPAN mirrors full packet copies
options.D: Both mechanisms collect exactly the same kind of data

questions.explanation_es: NetFlow recolecta metadatos y estadísticas resumidas del flujo (direcciones, contadores); SPAN refleja copias completas de los paquetes reales, más pesado pero con visibilidad total del contenido.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What's a key limitation of local SPAN compared to RSPAN/ERSPAN?

options.A: It can only mirror to a port on the same physical switch
options.B: It requires GRE encapsulation, same as ERSPAN
options.C: It has no limitation at all compared to RSPAN or ERSPAN
options.D: It can mirror across a routed WAN, same as ERSPAN

questions.explanation_es: SPAN local solo puede reflejar tráfico hacia un puerto destino en el mismo switch físico; para otro switch en el mismo dominio L2 se necesita RSPAN, y para cruzar una red enrutada, ERSPAN.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What constraint applies to how RSPAN traffic is transported?

options.A: It needs no dedicated VLAN; any regular data VLAN works fine
options.B: It can cross any number of routed L3 hops without any special encapsulation needed
options.C: It stays on a dedicated VLAN confined to one L2 domain, never crossing Layer 3
options.D: It is automatically encrypted with IPsec by default

questions.explanation_es: RSPAN viaja sobre una VLAN dedicada que debe permanecer dentro de un único dominio L2; no puede cruzar un límite de Capa 3 — para eso se necesita ERSPAN, que encapsula en GRE.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the purpose of an IP SLA 'responder' configured on the target device of a probe?

options.A: It improves measurement accuracy (especially for jitter and latency) by timestamping the probe packets on the target device itself, rather than relying solely on round-trip estimates from the source
options.B: It blocks all IP SLA probes from reaching that device
options.C: It is required only for ICMP-based operations, never for UDP-based ones
options.D: It converts the target device into an IP SLA source itself, allowing it to originate its own independent probes toward other devices on the network without any additional configuration

questions.explanation_es: El IP SLA Responder, configurado en el dispositivo destino de la prueba, mejora la precisión de la medición (especialmente para jitter y latencia) al marcar con timestamp los paquetes de prueba en el propio dispositivo destino, en lugar de depender únicamente de estimaciones basadas en el tiempo de ida y vuelta medido solo desde el origen.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: Which IP SLA operation type is commonly used to measure jitter, useful for validating voice/video quality over a path?

options.A: FTP operation
options.B: HTTP GET operation
options.C: DNS lookup operation
options.D: UDP jitter operation

questions.explanation_es: La operación de tipo UDP jitter de IP SLA está diseñada específicamente para medir jitter (variación en el retardo), latencia y pérdida de paquetes de forma similar al tráfico de voz/video real, siendo comúnmente usada para validar la calidad esperada de esos servicios sobre una ruta determinada antes o durante su despliegue.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: How does Catalyst Center's Assurance capability typically obtain near-real-time visibility into network and client health, as opposed to relying solely on periodic polling?

options.A: By leveraging telemetry streaming from network devices and clients, in addition to traditional data collection methods, to provide more timely insight than polling alone
options.B: By requiring the administrator to manually run 'show' commands on every device and paste the output into a spreadsheet for later analysis into a spreadsheet for later manual analysis
options.C: By disabling all monitoring capabilities on the managed devices
options.D: By relying on SNMP polling every 24 hours

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center Assurance aprovecha el streaming de telemetría desde los dispositivos de red y clientes (además de métodos de recolección más tradicionales), lo que permite una visibilidad mucho más cercana al tiempo real sobre la salud de la red y de los clientes, comparado con depender únicamente de polling periódico tradicional.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does Cisco Catalyst Center's Plug and Play (PnP) capability enable?

options.A: It replaces the need for any IP addressing on new devices
options.B: It is used only for wireless access points, never for switches or routers
options.C: Zero-touch or near-zero-touch onboarding of new network devices, which automatically contact Catalyst Center upon first boot to receive their configuration and software image
options.D: It disables all automatic configuration, requiring fully manual setup for every new device added to the network, one device at a time by an on-site engineer by an on-site engineer every time

questions.explanation_es: Plug and Play (PnP) permite el onboarding de nuevos dispositivos de red con mínima o nula intervención manual: los dispositivos nuevos, al arrancar por primera vez, contactan automáticamente a Catalyst Center para recibir su configuración inicial e imagen de software correspondiente, simplificando el despliegue a gran escala.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Over which transport and default port does NETCONF typically operate?

options.A: SSH, using the dedicated 'netconf' SSH subsystem, typically on TCP port 830
options.B: HTTP on port 80, exactly like RESTCONF uses by default in most deployments, though RESTCONF typically runs over HTTPS on port 443
options.C: UDP on port 161, the same as SNMP
options.D: Plain unencrypted Telnet on port 23

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF típicamente opera sobre SSH, utilizando un subsistema SSH dedicado llamado 'netconf', normalmente en el puerto TCP 830, estableciendo una sesión persistente y segura para el intercambio de mensajes RPC en XML.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of these correctly reflects an advantage of NETCONF's transaction-based approach using candidate/running datastores over RESTCONF's typical single-datastore model?

options.A: There is no meaningful difference between the two approaches
options.B: NETCONF has no concept of validating changes before applying them
options.C: RESTCONF can optionally stage changes in a candidate datastore similar to NETCONF, but unlike NETCONF it provides no explicit validate operation to check those changes before the commit is applied
options.D: NETCONF's candidate datastore allows a set of changes to be staged and validated before an explicit commit is applied to the running configuration, supporting more controlled, transactional configuration changes

questions.explanation_es: El uso del datastore 'candidate' en NETCONF permite preparar y validar un conjunto de cambios antes de aplicarlos formalmente (commit) a la configuración en ejecución (running), soportando un flujo de cambios más controlado y transaccional; RESTCONF, en cambio, opera típicamente de forma directa sobre un único datastore equivalente a running, sin ese paso intermedio de candidate/commit.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the key security difference between the 'enable password' and 'enable secret' commands on a Cisco device?

options.A: 'enable password' is always more secure than 'enable secret', since it uses a stronger and more modern hashing algorithm by default on every current Cisco IOS release regardless of platform or software version
options.B: Neither command has any impact on device security
options.C: 'enable secret' stores the password using a strong hash by default, while the older 'enable password' stores it in a much weaker, reversible/plaintext-like form; 'enable secret' should always be preferred
options.D: They are identical in security, differing only in command syntax

questions.explanation_es: 'enable secret' almacena la contraseña usando un hash fuerte por defecto, mientras que el comando más antiguo 'enable password' la almacena de una forma mucho más débil (tipo 7, fácilmente reversible), por lo que 'enable secret' siempre debe preferirse; si ambos están configurados, 'enable secret' tiene prioridad.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Why is SSH generally preferred over Telnet for remote device management access?

options.A: Telnet encrypts sessions, and SSH does not
options.B: SSH encrypts the entire session (including credentials), while Telnet transmits data, including usernames and passwords, in plaintext, making it vulnerable to eavesdropping
options.C: SSH cannot be used for CLI access, only for file transfer
options.D: SSH and Telnet both support optional session encryption, but Telnet enables it by default while SSH requires the administrator to explicitly generate a crypto key before encryption actually takes effect

questions.explanation_es: SSH cifra toda la sesión, incluyendo las credenciales de acceso, mientras que Telnet transmite todo en texto plano (incluyendo usuario y contraseña), haciéndolo vulnerable a ser interceptado (eavesdropping) por cualquiera con acceso a la ruta de red. Por eso SSH es el estándar recomendado para gestión remota.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which transport protocol and port does TACACS+ use by default, as opposed to RADIUS?

options.A: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49; RADIUS uses UDP ports 1812/1813 (authentication/accounting) — reflecting TACACS+'s reliance on TCP's connection-oriented delivery versus RADIUS's use of UDP
options.B: TACACS+ uses HTTP as its transport
options.C: TACACS+ uses UDP port 49 for faster, connectionless delivery of authentication requests, while RADIUS uses TCP ports 1812 and 1813 to guarantee reliable delivery of accounting records
options.D: Both protocols use TCP port 49 by default, differing only in how they separate authentication from authorization within that single session

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ utiliza TCP en el puerto 49, aprovechando la entrega orientada a conexión de TCP; RADIUS utiliza UDP, típicamente en los puertos 1812 (autenticación/autorización) y 1813 (accounting), reflejando un enfoque más liviano pero sin las garantías de entrega de TCP.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What happens to a packet that does not match any explicit permit or deny statement in a Cisco ACL?

options.A: The packet causes the router to reboot
options.B: The ACL is automatically disabled
options.C: It is always permitted by default if no explicit match occurs, since Cisco ACLs assume permit rather than deny at the end
options.D: It is denied, due to the implicit 'deny any' at the end of every ACL, even though it is not visibly configured

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene un 'deny any' implícito al final, aunque no aparezca explícitamente en la configuración; cualquier paquete que no coincida con ninguna sentencia permit/deny explícita configurada será denegado por este comportamiento implícito por defecto.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What is a practical advantage of using named ACLs over numbered ACLs?

options.A: Numbered ACLs support far more entries than named ACLs, which is their only advantage over the more descriptive naming scheme used by named access lists on modern platforms
options.B: Named ACLs allow individual entries to be added or removed (edited) more easily by line/sequence, and the name itself can be more descriptive of the ACL's purpose
options.C: Named ACLs cannot be applied to any interface
options.D: There is no functional difference between named and numbered ACLs

questions.explanation_es: Las ACLs nombradas (named ACLs) permiten agregar o eliminar entradas individuales de forma más flexible (usando números de secuencia), sin tener que recrear toda la lista, además de que el nombre puede ser descriptivo del propósito de la ACL, facilitando su identificación y mantenimiento frente a una ACL puramente numerada.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is using HTTPS (TLS) essential for securing REST API communications, such as those with Cisco Catalyst Center?

options.A: HTTP and HTTPS provide identical security for API traffic
