options.B: HTTPS eliminates the need for any authentication token
options.C: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit between the client and the API server, protecting credentials, tokens, and payload data from being intercepted or tampered with over the network
options.D: HTTPS is only relevant for browser-based access, not for API calls made by automated scripts or applications talking directly to a REST endpoint without any browser involved at all

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS (HTTP sobre TLS) cifra los datos en tránsito entre el cliente y el servidor de la API, protegiendo credenciales, tokens de autenticación y datos del payload de ser interceptados o manipulados por un atacante en la red, algo que HTTP plano no ofrece.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What does the principle of 'least privilege' mean when applied to API access scopes/roles?

options.A: An API client or user should only be granted the minimum permissions/scopes necessary to perform its intended function, rather than broad or administrative access by default
options.B: Least privilege only applies to human users, never to API service accounts
options.C: It means API calls should always be rate-limited to one request per minute
options.D: Every API client should be granted full administrative access by default for convenience, since revoking access later is always simple and low-risk regardless of how the client authenticates

questions.explanation_es: El principio de menor privilegio (least privilege) establece que a un cliente de API o usuario se le deben otorgar solo los permisos/scopes mínimos necesarios para cumplir su función prevista, en lugar de otorgar acceso amplio o administrativo por defecto, reduciendo el impacto potencial si esas credenciales son comprometidas.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: In 802.1X port-based authentication, what are the three key roles involved?

options.A: Only two roles exist: Supplicant and Authenticator, with no separate Authentication Server required in any 802.1X deployment, regardless of vendor or RADIUS backend used, a claim contradicted by the 802.1X standard itself
options.B: Supplicant (the client device requesting access), Authenticator (the switch/AP enforcing the port state), and Authentication Server (e.g., RADIUS server, which validates credentials)
options.C: Router, Switch, and Access Point, with no client-side role
options.D: Client, Server, and Firewall — with no other roles defined

questions.explanation_es: 802.1X define tres roles clave: el Supplicant (el dispositivo cliente que solicita acceso a la red), el Authenticator (típicamente el switch o access point, que controla el estado del puerto según el resultado de la autenticación), y el Authentication Server (por ejemplo, un servidor RADIUS/ISE, que valida las credenciales del supplicant).

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the purpose of MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) in a NAC deployment?

options.A: It disables all authentication for devices matching a MAC address whitelist without any verification, bypassing every security check entirely regardless of the device's actual compliance posture
options.B: It completely replaces 802.1X for all devices, including those capable of doing 802.1X
options.C: It is used only for wireless guest networks, never for wired ports
options.D: It allows devices that cannot perform 802.1X authentication (such as printers or IoT devices) to be authenticated based on their MAC address instead, as a fallback mechanism

questions.explanation_es: MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) permite que dispositivos incapaces de realizar autenticación 802.1X (como impresoras, cámaras IP, o ciertos dispositivos IoT) sean autenticados basándose en su dirección MAC como mecanismo alternativo (fallback), en lugar de quedar completamente sin acceso o requerir excepciones manuales complejas.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the primary role of Cisco Firepower Management Center (FMC) in a Cisco NGFW deployment?

options.A: It only manages licensing, with no policy or monitoring capability for any connected Firepower device, despite FMC actually serving as the primary policy console for connected devices
options.B: It is a hardware appliance that replaces the FTD firewall itself
options.C: It provides centralized policy management, monitoring, and reporting for one or more Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) NGFW devices
options.D: It is used for wireless controller management

questions.explanation_es: FMC (Firepower Management Center) provee gestión centralizada de políticas, monitoreo y reportes para uno o varios dispositivos NGFW Firepower Threat Defense (FTD), permitiendo administrar de forma consistente múltiples firewalls desde una única consola en lugar de configurarlos individualmente.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What does Application Visibility and Control (AVC) provide within a Cisco NGFW or router?

options.A: AVC replaces the need for any firewall rules
options.B: AVC is used for physical cable diagnostics
options.C: The ability to identify specific applications generating traffic (beyond just port/protocol) and apply granular policy (allow, block, QoS treatment) based on that application identity
options.D: Only the ability to see interface bandwidth utilization, with no application-level detail beyond simple byte and packet counters per interface across the entire managed network, since AVC's DPI engine identifies the application behind a flow

questions.explanation_es: AVC (Application Visibility and Control) permite identificar qué aplicación específica está generando cierto tráfico (más allá de simplemente el puerto/protocolo usado, ya que muchas apps modernas comparten puertos como 443), y aplicar políticas granulares (permitir, bloquear, dar cierto tratamiento de QoS) basadas en esa identidad de aplicación.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In Python, what keyword is used to define a reusable function?

options.A: function
options.B: lambda is the only way to define any function
options.C: func
options.D: def

questions.explanation_es: En Python, una función se define usando la palabra clave 'def', seguida del nombre de la función y sus parámetros entre paréntesis, por ejemplo: 'def mi_funcion(parametro):'. 'lambda' se usa para funciones anónimas de una sola expresión, pero no es la forma estándar de definir una función reutilizable con nombre.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of these data types is NOT natively supported directly by the JSON specification?

options.A: Strings
options.B: Numbers
options.C: Boolean values (true/false), since JSON only natively supports strings and numbers as primitive data types
options.D: Comments (JSON has no native syntax for comments within the document)

questions.explanation_es: JSON no soporta comentarios de forma nativa dentro del documento; a diferencia de YAML u otros formatos, no existe una sintaxis estándar para agregar comentarios en un archivo JSON válido. Sí soporta strings, números, booleanos, null, objetos y arreglos.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What is the key difference between an HTTP 401 Unauthorized and a 403 Forbidden response?

options.A: 401 indicates the request lacks valid authentication credentials (or they were rejected); 403 indicates the client is authenticated but does not have permission to access the requested resource
options.B: 401 and 403 mean exactly the same thing and are used interchangeably
options.C: 403 indicates the credentials were invalid or expired, while 401 indicates the client authenticated successfully but lacks permission for the requested resource, so a script receiving a 401 should simply refresh its stored token
options.D: Both codes only apply to POST requests, never to GET requests

questions.explanation_es: 401 Unauthorized indica que la solicitud carece de credenciales de autenticación válidas (o fueron rechazadas) — el cliente no está autenticado correctamente. 403 Forbidden indica que el cliente SÍ está autenticado, pero no tiene permiso para acceder al recurso solicitado — es un problema de autorización, no de autenticación.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When interpreting a paginated JSON response from an API (such as Catalyst Center's Intent APIs), what is a typical purpose of metadata fields often included in the response envelope?

options.A: To encrypt the response body
options.B: To store the API's licensing key
options.C: To specify which programming language the client must use when parsing the JSON response body returned by the server for that endpoint, regardless of the client's own platform
options.D: To indicate details such as whether more results exist beyond the current page, so the client knows whether to make additional requests to retrieve the full dataset

questions.explanation_es: En respuestas paginadas, los metadatos incluidos (por ejemplo, indicadores de si hay más resultados disponibles) le indican al cliente si debe realizar solicitudes adicionales para obtener el conjunto de datos completo, en lugar de asumir que la primera página contiene todos los resultados.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is a common 'action' type used within an EEM applet once a defined event triggers it?

options.A: EEM applets can only reboot the device as their sole possible action, with no ability to run any other CLI command or generate any log message or configuration, because IOS rejects any 'action X cli command' line if entered
options.B: Actions such as 'action X cli command' (to execute a CLI command) or 'action X syslog' (to generate a syslog message), used to automate a remediation or notification step
options.C: EEM applets cannot perform any actions, only detect events
options.D: Actions in EEM are limited to sending SNMP traps only

questions.explanation_es: Una vez que un evento definido dispara un applet EEM, se pueden configurar distintas acciones, como 'action X cli command' (para ejecutar un comando de CLI de forma automática) o 'action X syslog' (para generar un mensaje de syslog), permitiendo automatizar pasos de remediación, notificación, o recolección de datos de diagnóstico sin intervención manual.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why do agentless automation tools (like Ansible) tend to be particularly well-suited for managing network devices (routers, switches) compared to agent-based tools?

options.A: Most network devices do not support running third-party software agents, so agentless tools that connect via standard protocols (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) fit naturally without requiring vendor support for an installed agent
options.B: There is no practical difference between agent-based and agentless approaches for network devices, since both require exactly the same amount of vendor support and installed software on every single managed device in the network
options.C: Agent-based tools are always faster and simpler to use on network devices than agentless tools
options.D: Network devices always have full support for running any third-party agent software natively

questions.explanation_es: La mayoría de los dispositivos de red (routers, switches) no soportan la instalación de agentes de software de terceros como sí lo hacen los servidores; por eso las herramientas agentless (como Ansible), que se conectan usando protocolos estándar (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) sin requerir un agente instalado, encajan naturalmente mejor para la automatización de infraestructura de red.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does it mean for the HTTP PUT method to be 'idempotent', and how does this compare to POST?

options.A: Sending the same PUT request multiple times results in the same final state (the resource is simply replaced with the same content each time); POST is generally NOT idempotent, since repeating it may create multiple new resources
options.B: PUT is never idempotent, while POST always is
options.C: Idempotency in HTTP refers only to whether a method's response can be cached by an intermediary proxy, which is why GET and PUT are both considered idempotent while a POST response is never eligible for caching
options.D: Both PUT and POST are always non-idempotent by definition

questions.explanation_es: Que PUT sea idempotente significa que enviar la misma solicitud PUT múltiples veces produce el mismo estado final (el recurso queda reemplazado con el mismo contenido cada vez, sin efectos adicionales acumulativos). POST generalmente NO es idempotente, ya que repetir la misma solicitud POST puede crear múltiples recursos nuevos (por ejemplo, múltiples entradas duplicadas) en lugar de producir el mismo resultado.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: Which statement best describes how Policy-Based Routing (PBR) makes forwarding decisions compared to standard destination-based routing?

options.A: PBR only functions on Layer 2 switches, having no applicability to Layer 3 routers at all
options.B: PBR requires BGP to be configured on the router before any route-map can be applied to an interface
options.C: PBR only considers the destination IP address, exactly like the routing table, offering no additional classification criteria based on source or packet attributes
options.D: PBR can forward packets based on criteria such as source address, packet size, or protocol, overriding the routing table before the normal lookup occurs

questions.explanation_es: PBR usa route-maps para clasificar el tráfico por múltiples criterios (IP origen, tamaño de paquete, protocolo, etc.) y aplicar un next-hop distinto al que indicaría la tabla de enrutamiento normal. Se evalúa antes de la búsqueda estándar en la RIB.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a PBR route-map, what is the difference between the 'set ip next-hop' and 'set ip default next-hop' commands?

options.A: They are functionally identical, differing only in the order the keywords appear in the command
options.B: 'set ip default next-hop' overrides BGP routes only, having no effect on static, connected, or any other type of route present in the routing table at the time the route-map is evaluated
options.C: 'set ip next-hop' only works with static routes, and has no effect when used with any dynamic routing protocol
options.D: 'set ip next-hop' forwards to the specified address unconditionally when the route-map matches, while 'set ip default next-hop' is used only as a fallback when the routing table has no explicit route for the destination

questions.explanation_es: 'set ip next-hop' fuerza el next-hop indicado sin importar la tabla de enrutamiento. 'set ip default next-hop' solo se usa como respaldo, cuando el router no tiene una ruta explícita hacia el destino más allá de la default.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: On which interface direction is Policy-Based Routing typically applied with the 'ip policy route-map' command?

options.A: Only on loopback interfaces, since those are the only interfaces PBR is designed to support
options.B: Outbound, after the routing table lookup has already determined the next hop
options.C: It applies globally to the router regardless of interface, affecting every packet the router processes
options.D: Inbound, before the normal routing table lookup is performed

questions.explanation_es: PBR se aplica con 'ip policy route-map' en el sentido entrante de la interfaz; el router evalúa el route-map sobre el tráfico que ingresa, antes de hacer la búsqueda normal en la tabla de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: A company wants traffic from the Finance subnet (10.10.10.0/24) to always exit via ISP-A, while all other traffic uses the normal default route via ISP-B, regardless of destination. Which technology best achieves this without changing destination-based routing for other traffic?

options.A: OSPF route redistribution between ISP-A's and ISP-B's separate routing domains
options.B: VRRP configured to load-balance traffic between ISP-A and ISP-B based on router priority
options.C: A static default route pointing all traffic toward ISP-A regardless of source subnet
options.D: Policy-Based Routing matching source address 10.10.10.0/24

questions.explanation_es: PBR permite clasificar el tráfico según el origen (entre otros criterios) y forzar un next-hop distinto solo para ese tráfico, dejando el resto sujeto al enrutamiento normal — algo que una ruta estática o un protocolo de enrutamiento por destino no logran por sí solos.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What distinguishes PAT (Port Address Translation) from standard dynamic NAT?

options.A: PAT translates only the destination address, never the source, which is the opposite of how PAT actually operates on a Cisco router configured for NAT overload
options.B: PAT allows multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP address by also translating the Layer 4 port number
options.C: PAT requires a one-to-one mapping between inside and outside addresses, exactly like static NAT does
options.D: PAT only works with UDP traffic, having no support for TCP-based sessions at all

questions.explanation_es: PAT (NAT overload) traduce dirección IP y puerto, permitiendo que muchos hosts internos compartan una sola IP pública, distinguiéndose entre sí por el número de puerto de origen traducido.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Why must both an 'ip nat inside' and an 'ip nat outside' interface be configured on a router for NAT to actually take effect?

options.A: Only 'ip nat inside' needs to be configured, on the private-facing interface; the router then automatically infers which remaining interface is 'outside' based on its current default route
options.B: NAT works identically with no interface designation at all; these commands are optional legacy syntax with no real effect, superseded in this mistaken view by automatic direction detection based on which interface first receives a DHCP lease
options.C: These commands configure DNS resolution for NAT and have nothing to do with interface direction
options.D: These commands tell the router which interfaces face the private ('inside') network and which face the public ('outside') network, which NAT needs to know to determine the direction of translation

questions.explanation_es: Estos comandos le indican al router qué interfaces dan hacia la red privada ('inside') y cuáles hacia la red pública ('outside'), lo cual NAT necesita saber para determinar la dirección de la traducción.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Which statement about static NAT is correct?

options.A: It always requires PAT to function, since static NAT cannot operate independently on a Cisco router
options.B: It creates a permanent one-to-one mapping between an inside local and an inside global address, allowing outside hosts to initiate connections to the inside host
options.C: It creates a temporary one-to-one mapping only when traffic is initiated from the inside, expiring once the session ends
options.D: It cannot be used for servers that must be reachable from the internet, since it never allows externally-initiated connections regardless of firewall configuration

questions.explanation_es: El NAT estático crea un mapeo fijo 1:1 entre una IP interna y una IP pública, permitiendo que hosts externos inicien conexiones hacia el host interno (por ejemplo, un servidor web) — a diferencia del NAT dinámico o PAT, que dependen de que la conexión se inicie desde adentro.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In HSRP, which router becomes the Active router by default?

options.A: The router with the lowest priority value, since HSRP always favors the most conservative router configuration in the group in the group
options.B: Whichever router boots up last, regardless of its configured priority or interface IP address
options.C: The router with the highest HSRP priority (default 100); if tied, the highest IP address on the HSRP interface breaks the tie
options.D: The router with the lowest IP address, used only as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal

questions.explanation_es: En HSRP, el router con mayor prioridad (por defecto 100) se convierte en el Active. Si hay empate en la prioridad, se decide por la IP más alta en la interfaz HSRP.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Unlike HSRP, which is a Cisco proprietary protocol, VRRP has what key characteristic?

options.A: VRRP requires a dedicated virtual IP separate from all physical interfaces, exactly like HSRP always does in every configuration
options.B: VRRP does not support preemption, unlike HSRP which enables it by default in every configuration
options.C: VRRP is an IETF standard protocol and can use the real interface IP address of one of the group's routers as the virtual IP
options.D: VRRP only supports 2 routers per group, unlike HSRP which has no such limit on group size

questions.explanation_es: VRRP es un estándar IETF (RFC), y permite que uno de los routers del grupo use su propia IP física de interfaz como la IP virtual (ese router se vuelve el Master 'IP owner'), algo que HSRP no hace, ya que siempre usa una IP virtual separada.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Besides statically configuring the same Rendezvous Point (RP) address on every PIM router, what dynamic mechanisms exist for RP discovery in a PIM Sparse Mode network?

options.A: RP discovery is always handled by OSPF flooding RP information as a special LSA type, with no dedicated PIM mechanism, treating RP reachability like an opaque LSA type 10 payload the way MPLS traffic-engineering data is flooded
options.B: Auto-RP (a Cisco-proprietary protocol) and BSR (Bootstrap Router, a standards-based protocol) both let routers learn the active RP dynamically, without static per-router configuration
options.C: Only DHCP can dynamically assign an RP address to PIM routers; there is no PIM-native discovery mechanism
options.D: Dynamic RP discovery is not possible in PIM Sparse Mode; static RP configuration is the only supported method

questions.explanation_es: Auto-RP (protocolo propietario de Cisco) y BSR (Bootstrap Router, basado en estándares) permiten que los routers aprendan el RP activo dinámicamente, sin necesidad de configuración estática en cada router.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: In PIM Sparse Mode, what is the role of the Rendezvous Point (RP)?

options.A: It is only used in PIM Dense Mode, having no equivalent role or function in PIM Sparse Mode
options.B: It acts as a meeting point where multicast sources register and receivers initially join, before the network potentially shifts to a more optimal shortest-path tree
options.C: It replaces the need for IGMP entirely, since receivers register directly with the RP instead of communicating with their local multicast router, bypassing the last-hop router's own group-membership tracking process entirely
options.D: It is the only device allowed to send multicast traffic, with all sources required to route through it directly

questions.explanation_es: El RP en PIM-SM funciona como un punto de encuentro: las fuentes se registran ahí y los receptores se unen inicialmente al árbol compartido (RPT) a través del RP; luego el tráfico puede migrar al árbol de ruta más corta (SPT) hacia la fuente para mayor eficiencia.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does an NTP stratum value of 16 signify about a device's clock?

options.A: Stratum 16 is used by convention to indicate that the device is unsynchronized, rather than indicating 16 hops from a reference clock
options.B: Stratum values above 15 are invalid and NTP rejects any device reporting stratum 16
options.C: Stratum 16 indicates the highest possible precision, better even than a stratum 1 reference clock, as though a higher stratum number meant added oscillator redundancy rather than hop count
options.D: Stratum 16 is reserved for GPS-based reference clocks

questions.explanation_es: Por convención, el stratum 16 se usa para indicar que el dispositivo está desincronizado, en lugar de indicar 16 saltos desde un reloj de referencia.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does a PTP 'domain number' identify, and why might a network run multiple separate PTP domains?

options.A: The domain number determines the physical cable length PTP messages can travel before requiring a repeater
options.B: Only one PTP domain can ever exist per organization, regardless of network size or the number of applications requiring synchronization
options.C: A domain number groups a set of PTP clocks that synchronize together under one grandmaster; running multiple domains lets independent groups of devices (e.g., different applications or tenants) maintain separate time synchronization on the same physical network
options.D: The domain number sets the priority1 value used by the Best Master Clock Algorithm, so changing a device's domain number can directly shift which clock in the network gets elected grandmaster

questions.explanation_es: Un número de dominio agrupa un conjunto de relojes PTP que se sincronizan juntos bajo un grandmaster; correr múltiples dominios permite que grupos independientes de dispositivos mantengan sincronización de tiempo separada sobre la misma red física.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement about LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) EtherChannel modes is correct?

options.A: Setting both ends to 'active' will not form a channel, since LACP requires exactly one side to be passive
options.B: LACP requires PAgP to be enabled first on both switches before any channel negotiation can begin
options.C: 'passive' mode actively sends LACP packets to initiate negotiation, exactly the opposite of what 'active' mode actually does in a real deployment during the initial handshake
options.D: A channel will form if at least one side is set to 'active' and the other side is set to 'active' or 'passive'; two 'passive' sides will never form a channel

questions.explanation_es: LACP forma el canal si al menos un extremo está en modo 'active' (y el otro en 'active' o 'passive'). Si ambos extremos están en 'passive', ninguno inicia la negociación y el canal nunca se forma, porque 'passive' espera recibir paquetes LACP en lugar de enviarlos.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python data type is immutable and therefore commonly used as a dictionary key?

options.A: dict, since dictionaries are the only built-in Python type that can never be modified after creation
options.B: list
options.C: tuple
options.D: set

questions.explanation_es: Las tuplas son inmutables, por lo que pueden usarse como claves de diccionario (los dicts requieren claves hashables). Las listas y los propios dicts son mutables y no son hashables, así que no pueden usarse como claves.

questions.name: Python básico

options.A: None
options.B: KeyError
options.C: status
options.D: unknown

questions.explanation_es: dict.get(key, default) retorna el valor default indicado si la clave no existe, en vez de lanzar KeyError como haría data["status"]. Como "status" no está en el dict, imprime "unknown".

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In a Python script using the 'requests' library to call a REST API, which method sends an HTTP GET request?

options.A: requests.query()
options.B: requests.send()
options.C: requests.fetch()
options.D: requests.get()

questions.explanation_es: La librería requests usa requests.get(url) para solicitudes GET y requests.post() para POST. Las otras opciones no son métodos reales de la librería.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: How must a JSON boolean value be written, and how does this differ from Python's boolean literals?

options.A: JSON booleans must be lowercase ('true'/'false'), while Python's native booleans are capitalized ('True'/'False') — a library like json.loads() handles the conversion between the two automatically
options.B: JSON has no boolean type at all; booleans must be represented as the strings '1' and '0'
options.C: JSON booleans must be capitalized exactly like Python's ('True'/'False'), with no difference between the two, a mix-up that arises because Python's 'json' module accepts either capitalization as a convenience when encoding custom objects
options.D: JSON booleans must be written in all uppercase ('TRUE'/'FALSE') to be considered valid

questions.explanation_es: Los booleanos de JSON deben ir en minúscula ('true'/'false'), mientras que los booleanos nativos de Python van capitalizados ('True'/'False') — una librería como json.loads() maneja la conversión automáticamente.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What Python type does the JSON value 'null' map to when parsed with json.loads()?

options.B: False
options.C: "" (empty string)
options.D: None

questions.explanation_es: Al parsear JSON en Python, el valor null se convierte en el objeto None, no en 0, cadena vacía ni False.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which JSON structure correctly represents an array of two interface objects?

options.A: {"interfaces": [{"name": "Gi0/1", "status": "up"}, {"name": "Gi0/2", "status": "down"}]}
options.B: {"interfaces": {"Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down"}}, which is exactly equivalent to an array of interface objects in JSON
options.C: {"interfaces": ["Gi0/1", "up", "Gi0/2", "down"]}
options.D: {"interfaces": ("Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down")}

questions.explanation_es: Un array JSON de objetos usa corchetes conteniendo objetos {} separados por comas. La opción A es un objeto (no array), la B mezcla claves y valores en una lista plana, y la D usa paréntesis, que no es sintaxis JSON válida.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Which device role connects a traditional campus segment with an SD-Access fabric?

options.A: Control Plane Node
options.B: Fabric WLC
options.C: Fabric Border Node
options.D: Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node es el punto de interoperabilidad entre la fabric SD-Access y las redes tradicionales, traduciendo entre el encapsulado VXLAN/LISP y el enrutamiento IP tradicional.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: A host in a traditional VLAN needs to reach a host inside an SD-Access fabric. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The traditional host must also run LISP and register its EID with the fabric's Map Server
options.B: The Control Plane Node forwards all external packets itself, besides maintaining the host database
options.C: SD-Access can't interoperate with traditional networks without a full migration first
options.D: Traffic enters/exits through the Border Node, which translates between overlay and traditional routing

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node traduce el tráfico entre el overlay de la fabric y una red tradicional externa; el host tradicional no necesita ejecutar LISP ni ningún protocolo especial.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: During a phased migration from 3-tier campus to SD-Access, which approach is commonly recommended?

options.A: Only wireless clients can be migrated to SD-Access; wired endpoints must remain on the traditional network permanently due to a hard platform limitation
options.B: Migration must start at the core/distribution, since access switches can't convert first
options.C: Migrate site by site or IP pool by IP pool, using the Border Node to bridge migrated and non-migrated segments
options.D: Migrate the entire campus in one maintenance window, all at once

questions.explanation_es: Una migración típica se hace de forma incremental (por sitio o IP pool), aprovechando el Border Node para mantener conectividad entre las partes migradas y las que siguen en la red tradicional.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: On platforms that support fine-grained CoPP, what do the 'host', 'transit', and 'CEF-exception' control-plane sub-interfaces each classify?

options.A: 'Host' classifies traffic destined to the device itself, 'transit' classifies traffic passing through the device that still reaches the CPU, and 'CEF-exception' classifies traffic punted to the CPU due to a forwarding exception
options.B: All three sub-interfaces are functionally identical and exist only for redundancy
options.C: These sub-interfaces classify traffic by physical port only, not by traffic type or destination
options.D: 'Host' and 'transit' both refer to traffic destined to the device itself, while 'CEF-exception' refers only to multicast traffic, a mix-up that overlooks how 'transit' refers to traffic merely passing through the device toward another destination while still reaching the CPU

questions.explanation_es: 'Host' clasifica el tráfico destinado al propio dispositivo, 'transit' clasifica el tráfico que pasa a través del dispositivo pero igual llega a la CPU, y 'CEF-exception' clasifica el tráfico desviado a la CPU por una excepción de reenvío.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: In which direction does Control Plane Policing apply its policy?

options.A: Only to transit traffic passing through the device
options.B: To traffic between two VLANs on the same switch
options.C: To traffic destined TO the device's control plane (the CPU itself)
options.D: Only to traffic sourced by the device toward external hosts, never to traffic destined toward the CPU itself

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se aplica específicamente al tráfico destinado a la CPU del propio dispositivo (control plane), no al tráfico de tránsito que solo pasa por el plano de datos sin involucrar a la CPU.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Which Cisco IOS mechanism is used to configure CoPP?

options.A: A service-policy applied under the 'control-plane' context, using class-maps and a policy-map
options.B: QoS marking with 'mls qos trust'
options.C: A VACL (VLAN ACL) configuration
options.D: An access-list applied directly to a physical interface with 'ip access-group', which is functionally identical to CoPP configuration

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se configura definiendo class-maps para clasificar el tráfico, un policy-map con las acciones (police/drop), y aplicándolo con 'service-policy input <nombre>' bajo el contexto 'control-plane', que representa lógicamente a la CPU del dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Which of these automation tools is classified as agentless (no software needs to be installed on the managed device)?

options.A: Chef
options.B: SaltStack running in agent mode
options.C: Ansible
options.D: Puppet

questions.explanation_es: Ansible es agentless: se conecta a los dispositivos gestionados vía SSH o APIs sin instalar software permanente en ellos. Puppet y Chef típicamente requieren un agente instalado en el nodo gestionado.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is a key operational advantage of an agentless automation approach for network devices?

options.A: It guarantees real-time push notifications from every managed device
options.B: It avoids installing, updating, and maintaining agent software on each device — useful since many network devices cannot run third-party agents
options.C: It typically completes large-scale changes faster than agent-based tools because connections to each device in the batch can be established and torn down in parallel, rather than relying on a persistent agent process on every device
options.D: It eliminates the need for any credentials to connect to devices

questions.explanation_es: Muchos dispositivos de red no pueden ejecutar software de terceros como un agente; el enfoque agentless evita esa necesidad, conectándose bajo demanda (SSH/API) sin instalar ni mantener nada persistente en el dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: In an agent-based orchestration model (e.g., Puppet), what role does the agent play on the managed node?

options.A: It only functions during initial provisioning and is then uninstalled
options.B: It only serves as a passive log collector with no configuration capability, forwarding events to a central server without ever applying any changes
options.C: It runs persistently, periodically pulling configuration from a central server and applying it locally
options.D: It replaces the need for a central server entirely

questions.explanation_es: En un modelo basado en agentes, el agente se instala de forma persistente en el nodo gestionado y contacta periódicamente a un servidor central (master) para obtener y aplicar la configuración deseada.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco Embedded Event Manager (EEM)?

options.A: To replace SNMP entirely
options.B: To encrypt configuration files
options.C: To detect an event on a device (CLI command, syslog message, CPU threshold, etc.) and automatically trigger a defined action in response
options.D: To provide a GUI for network monitoring, replacing the need for any CLI-based scripting or event detection logic entirely across every supported Cisco IOS platform

questions.explanation_es: EEM permite definir applets que combinan un evento disparador (event detector) con una acción automática a ejecutar en respuesta, como enviar un email, correr un comando o generar un log.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector triggers an applet when a specific CLI command is entered by a user?

options.A: event cli
options.B: event syslog
options.C: event snmp
options.D: event timer

questions.explanation_es: 'event cli' detecta cuando se ingresa un patrón de comando CLI específico (con 'match' sobre una expresión regular), disparando el applet antes o después de ejecutarse ese comando.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: An EEM applet is configured with 'event syslog pattern "%LINK-3-UPDOWN"' and an action to send an email. What triggers this applet?

options.A: An SNMP trap received from another device
options.B: A scheduled timer
options.C: The router generating a syslog message matching that pattern, such as an interface changing state
options.D: A manual CLI command entered by the administrator immediately before the applet is configured on the device

questions.explanation_es: 'event syslog' dispara el applet cuando el dispositivo genera internamente un mensaje de syslog que coincide con el patrón indicado, en este caso un cambio de estado de una interfaz.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: In RESTful API design, which HTTP method is idempotent and used to completely replace an existing resource?

options.A: GET
options.B: PUT
options.C: POST
options.D: PATCH

questions.explanation_es: PUT reemplaza por completo el recurso indicado con el cuerpo enviado y es idempotente. POST no es idempotente (crea un nuevo recurso cada vez) y PATCH aplica una modificación parcial, no un reemplazo completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to apply a partial update to an existing resource, modifying only specific fields?

options.A: OPTIONS
options.B: PUT
options.C: DELETE
options.D: PATCH

questions.explanation_es: PATCH se usa para aplicar una modificación parcial a un recurso existente (cambiar solo algunos campos), a diferencia de PUT, que reemplaza el recurso completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which statement about the HTTP GET method is correct?

options.A: GET should be safe and idempotent, retrieving a representation of a resource without side effects on the server
options.B: GET is used to create new resources on the server
options.C: GET requires a request body containing the resource data
options.D: GET is the only method that can return a 201 Created status, since every other HTTP method is forbidden from creating new resources

questions.explanation_es: GET es un método seguro (no debería modificar el estado del servidor) e idempotente, usado para leer un recurso. Crear un recurso, que puede devolver 201 Created, es responsabilidad típica de POST.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Before 802.1X authentication completes, what kind of access does a switch port typically allow the connecting endpoint?

options.A: Trunk-level access to all VLANs
options.B: No traffic, including DHCP
options.C: Full, unrestricted access to the network, exactly as if 802.1X authentication had already completed successfully on that switch port regardless of the connected device's identity
options.D: Restricted access via a pre-authentication ACL, allowing only what's needed for the authentication process itself (e.g., DHCP, ISE communication)

questions.explanation_es: Antes de completarse la autenticación 802.1X, el puerto suele permitir un acceso restringido mediante una ACL de pre-autenticación, habilitando solo el tráfico necesario para el propio proceso (DHCP, DNS, comunicación con ISE), no acceso completo.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes TACACS+ from RADIUS?

options.A: TACACS+ encrypts the entire packet body, while RADIUS encrypts only the password field
options.B: TACACS+ encrypts only the password in the packet, while RADIUS encrypts the entire packet body
options.C: Neither protocol encrypts any part of the packet
options.D: Both encrypt the entire packet identically

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ cifra todo el cuerpo del paquete, mientras que RADIUS solo cifra el campo de contraseña, dejando el resto del paquete (como el username) sin cifrar.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which AAA protocol separates authentication and authorization into distinct processes, making it well suited for granular per-command authorization on network devices?

options.A: LDAP
options.B: RADIUS
options.C: Kerberos
options.D: TACACS+

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ separa claramente autenticación, autorización y accounting en procesos independientes, permitiendo un control granular como autorizar comandos individuales en el CLI — algo que RADIUS, al combinar autenticación y autorización, no maneja tan bien.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: In a standard IPv4 ACL, which criterion can be used to match traffic?

options.A: Source IP address only
options.B: Destination MAC address
options.C: VLAN tag
options.D: Source and destination IP address plus Layer 4 port

questions.explanation_es: Las ACL estándar de IPv4 solo pueden filtrar según la dirección IP de origen. Para filtrar por IP destino, protocolo o puertos de Capa 4 se necesita una ACL extendida.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: By default, what happens to a packet that matches no explicit statement in an ACL applied to an interface?

options.A: It is queued until an administrator manually decides how to handle it during the next maintenance window
options.B: It is denied, due to an implicit 'deny all' at the end of every ACL
options.C: It is permitted, since ACLs default to permit
options.D: It is forwarded using the next ACL in sequence

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene una sentencia implícita de 'deny all' al final (aunque no se muestre en la configuración), por lo que el tráfico que no coincide explícitamente con un 'permit' se descarta.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What does a CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) score help an organization do when triaging discovered vulnerabilities?

options.A: It provides a standardized numeric severity rating, helping prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first based on relative risk
options.B: It only classifies vulnerabilities by which vendor reported them, not by their actual severity or exploitability
options.C: It has no practical use in prioritization; every vulnerability must be treated as equally urgent regardless of score, ignoring that CVSS scores exist to differentiate urgency
options.D: It automatically patches the vulnerability once scored, removing the need for manual remediation planning

questions.explanation_es: Provee una calificación numérica estandarizada de severidad, ayudando a priorizar qué vulnerabilidades remediar primero según su riesgo relativo.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Which authentication mechanism involves the client sending a token in the 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' HTTP header on each API request?

options.A: IPsec
options.B: OAuth 2.0 token-based authentication
options.C: Basic authentication with username/password on every request

questions.explanation_es: En OAuth 2.0, tras autenticarse el cliente recibe un token de acceso que envía en el header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' en cada solicitud posterior, sin reenviar usuario/contraseña cada vez.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is HTTPS (TLS) considered essential for securing REST API calls that carry authentication credentials or tokens?

options.A: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit, preventing credentials/tokens from being intercepted in cleartext
options.B: HTTPS is only needed for GET requests
options.C: HTTPS makes the API respond faster
options.D: HTTPS replaces the need for any authentication mechanism entirely, since TLS alone verifies the identity of every client

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS cifra el tráfico entre cliente y servidor, protegiendo credenciales y tokens de ser interceptados en texto plano (por ejemplo en un ataque man-in-the-middle); no reemplaza la autenticación, la complementa.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What does IP SLA 'scheduling' (using the 'ip sla schedule' command) allow an administrator to configure for a defined operation?

options.A: It configures which VRF the operation's probe traffic uses, unrelated to timing
options.B: It controls when the operation starts and how long it runs (its 'life'), including whether it runs once, for a fixed duration, or indefinitely
options.C: It has no effect; all IP SLA operations start immediately and run forever by default with no way to change that, though an operation without an explicit life value still eventually stops on its own
options.D: It only allows renaming the operation; timing must be configured elsewhere

questions.explanation_es: Controla cuándo inicia la operación y cuánto tiempo corre (su 'life'), incluyendo si corre una sola vez, por una duración fija, o indefinidamente.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: How can IP SLA be combined with object tracking to improve network resiliency?

options.A: IP SLA replaces the need for a routing protocol entirely
options.B: IP SLA automatically reconfigures BGP neighbor relationships whenever a monitored path degrades below a defined threshold whenever a monitored path degrades in quality
options.C: IP SLA cannot be combined with any other feature
options.D: A 'track' object can monitor an IP SLA operation and trigger actions like removing a static route from the routing table if the tracked path fails

questions.explanation_es: Un objeto 'track' puede monitorear el estado de una operación de IP SLA (por ejemplo, alcanzabilidad de un gateway) y, si falla, disparar acciones automáticas como retirar una ruta estática, logrando una conmutación por falla más rápida.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: How does NetFlow v9 differ from the fixed-format NetFlow v5?

options.A: Both use the same fixed format; v9 only changes the UDP port
options.B: v9 removed the ability to export any flow data at all
options.C: v9 uses template-based records with customizable fields; v5's fields are fixed
options.D: v5 introduced the template-based format first; v9 reverted to a fixed record layout

questions.explanation_es: La v9 usa un formato basado en templates, donde un mensaje separado define los campos del registro, permitiendo personalizarlos; la v5 tiene un conjunto de campos fijo y no configurable.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: Which components must be configured to enable Flexible NetFlow on an interface?

options.A: A flow record and a flow monitor, with the monitor applied to the interface
options.B: Only a route-map bound directly to the interface
options.C: A SPAN session paired with a VLAN ACL
options.D: Just an access-list applied to the interface; no record or monitor needed at all

questions.explanation_es: Se necesita un flow record (define los campos) y un flow monitor (asocia el record, opcionalmente un exporter, y se aplica a la interfaz); el exporter es opcional.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What's the key difference between SPAN and RSPAN?

options.A: RSPAN mirrors across switches via a dedicated VLAN; SPAN stays on one switch
options.B: SPAN encrypts mirrored traffic; RSPAN does not encrypt it
options.C: SPAN can span traffic across multiple switches using a VLAN; RSPAN can't do that at all
options.D: There's no real difference; RSPAN is just a newer name for SPAN

questions.explanation_es: SPAN copia tráfico dentro del mismo switch. RSPAN extiende esa capacidad usando una VLAN dedicada para llevar el tráfico espejado a través de varios switches.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: Why would an admin choose ERSPAN over SPAN or RSPAN?

options.A: ERSPAN only works within a single VLAN on one switch
options.B: ERSPAN wraps mirrored traffic in GRE so it can cross a routed network
options.C: ERSPAN isn't supported on any Catalyst switch platform
options.D: ERSPAN is required even when mirroring within the very same local switch

questions.explanation_es: ERSPAN encapsula el tráfico espejado en GRE, permitiendo enviarlo a través de una red L3 hacia un destino remoto — algo que SPAN y RSPAN, limitados a Capa 2, no pueden hacer.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Which command creates a local username/password database entry for authentication on a Cisco device?

options.A: line vty 0 4
options.B: username admin password Cisco123
options.C: aaa new-model
options.D: enable secret Cisco123, which also creates a full local username database entry automatically

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'username <nombre> password <clave>' crea una entrada en la base de datos local de usuarios del dispositivo, usada para autenticación local en líneas configuradas con 'login local'.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'login local' command applied under 'line vty 0 4'?

options.A: It disables authentication entirely for VTY lines
options.B: It applies only to console line access, not VTY
options.C: It requires users connecting via those VTY lines to authenticate using the local username database configured on the device
options.D: It forces authentication through a RADIUS server, bypassing the local username database entirely regardless of configuration

questions.explanation_es: 'login local' bajo las líneas VTY indica que la autenticación debe validarse contra la base de datos local de usuarios (creada con 'username'), en lugar de usar solo una contraseña de línea genérica o un servidor AAA externo.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: What is the difference between NETCONF's '<get>' and '<get-config>' operations?

options.A: '<get>' retrieves configuration data only from the candidate datastore, while '<get-config>' retrieves both configuration and operational state data from the running datastore
options.B: They are two identical aliases for the same operation, with no functional difference between them
options.C: '<get-config>' retrieves configuration data from a specified datastore (such as running or candidate), while '<get>' retrieves both configuration and operational state data
options.D: '<get-config>' is used only to delete configuration, unrelated to retrieving any data

questions.explanation_es: '<get-config>' obtiene datos de configuración de un datastore especificado (como running o candidate), mientras que '<get>' obtiene tanto datos de configuración como de estado operativo.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which encoding format does NETCONF use to structure its messages, such as <get-config> and <edit-config> operations?

options.A: XML
options.B: Only plain text
options.C: CSV
options.D: Only JSON

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF utiliza XML para codificar sus mensajes y operaciones, a diferencia de RESTCONF, que soporta tanto XML como JSON.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) feature provides end-to-end visibility into network health and can proactively identify issues affecting client connectivity?

options.A: Path Trace
options.B: Template Editor
options.C: Assurance
options.D: Plug and Play

questions.explanation_es: Assurance en Catalyst Center recopila telemetría de la red y los clientes para dar visibilidad de salud end-to-end, detectando proactivamente problemas y sugiriendo posibles causas raíz.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does the Catalyst Center 'Path Trace' tool do?

options.A: It only shows historical CPU utilization graphs
options.B: It automatically remediates any configuration errors found and can even suggest likely root causes for connectivity problems along that path automatically
options.C: It is used for wireless site surveys
options.D: It simulates and traces the actual path a packet would take between two endpoints, showing each hop and potential issues along the way

questions.explanation_es: Path Trace traza la ruta real (hop por hop) que seguiría o está siguiendo el tráfico entre un origen y un destino, mostrando el estado de cada salto y ayudando a identificar dónde ocurre un problema.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: How does managing an FTD device via FDM (Firepower Device Manager) differ from managing it via FMC (Firepower Management Center)?

options.A: FDM can manage multiple FTD devices centrally, while FMC can only manage a single device at a time
options.B: FDM and FMC both run as separate centralized platforms capable of managing multiple FTD devices, differing mainly in licensing tier rather than in their overall scope of management
options.C: FDM requires a separate physical appliance, while FMC runs directly on each FTD device with no separate platform needed, a description that reverses which of the two products actually needs its own dedicated platform
options.D: FDM is a locally hosted, single-device web UI built into the FTD appliance itself, while FMC is a centralized platform that manages policy across many FTD devices at once

questions.explanation_es: FDM es una interfaz web local, de un solo dispositivo, integrada en el propio equipo FTD, mientras que FMC es una plataforma centralizada que gestiona política a través de muchos dispositivos FTD a la vez.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Beyond QoS shaping, how can AVC's application-visibility reporting help with a security use case like detecting 'shadow IT'?

options.A: AVC can only detect applications that are already known and pre-approved, making it unable to surface anything unexpected
options.B: AVC has no visibility-reporting capability at all; it can only apply QoS marking, not generate reports
options.C: AVC reporting can reveal applications actually running on the network that weren't expected or sanctioned, helping identify unauthorized software or services in use
options.D: Shadow IT detection requires a completely separate product; AVC's application data cannot be used for this purpose in any way, overlooking that AVC's per-flow data would surface an unsanctioned cloud app

questions.explanation_es: Los reportes de AVC pueden revelar aplicaciones que realmente corren en la red y que no eran esperadas o autorizadas, ayudando a identificar software o servicios no sancionados en uso.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: In vSphere, what does Fault Tolerance (FT) provide?

options.A: Encryption of VM network traffic between hosts
options.B: A live, synced secondary VM copy that takes over instantly with zero downtime if the primary host fails
options.C: Scheduled nightly backups of VM disk images
options.D: Automatic load balancing of VMs across hosts based on current resource usage, migrating them live

questions.explanation_es: FT mantiene una VM secundaria sincronizada en tiempo real en otro host; si el primario falla, la secundaria toma el control sin pérdida de estado.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What's the purpose of Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) in a cluster?

options.A: It performs VM backups on a fixed schedule
options.B: It provides zero-downtime failover identical to Fault Tolerance
options.C: It manages physical firewall rules on the network perimeter
options.D: It automatically balances VM workloads across hosts by migrating them

questions.explanation_es: DRS monitorea el uso de recursos y migra VMs automáticamente entre hosts para balancear la carga, sin la tolerancia a fallas instantánea de FT.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What distinguishes a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor from a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?

options.A: There's no meaningful architectural difference between them at all in any real deployment
options.B: Type 1 runs directly on hardware; Type 2 runs as an app on a host OS
options.C: Type 1 requires a host OS; Type 2 doesn't need one
options.D: Type 2 always performs better than Type 1

questions.explanation_es: Un Tipo 1 se ejecuta directamente sobre el hardware físico sin un SO host intermedio; un Tipo 2 se ejecuta como aplicación dentro de un SO host existente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why are Type 1 hypervisors generally preferred in enterprise data centers?

options.A: Better performance and lower overhead, without an extra host-OS layer
options.B: Type 1 hypervisors are always free to license
options.C: Type 1 hypervisors do not support live migration between hosts, unlike Type 2 which fully supports it natively
options.D: Type 2 can't run more than one VM at a time on a host

questions.explanation_es: Al ejecutarse directamente sobre el hardware, los Tipo 1 tienen menor overhead y mejor rendimiento, preferidos en centros de datos de producción.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What does it mean for a service like DHCP relay or NTP to be 'VRF-aware'?

options.A: VRF-awareness has no practical effect on how these services work
options.B: The service can only operate in the global table, never a VRF
options.C: It auto-replicates identically into every VRF with no customization
options.D: The service can be configured to operate within a specific VRF's context

questions.explanation_es: El servicio puede configurarse para operar dentro del contexto de una VRF específica, como reenviar DHCP o alcanzar un NTP solo accesible por esa VRF.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: For two devices in different VRFs on the same router to communicate, what's typically required?

options.A: VRFs automatically bridge all instances at Layer 2
options.B: Nothing extra; VRFs share the router's single global table underneath
options.C: Both devices must be in the same VLAN
options.D: Route leaking or an intermediate device, since VRFs are isolated by design

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs están aisladas por diseño; se necesita route leaking (vía route-targets) o un dispositivo intermedio para que se comuniquen entre sí.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In LISP, what do EID and RLOC represent?

options.A: EID identifies the device's identity; RLOC identifies where it's topologically reachable
options.B: EID is IPv6-only; RLOC is IPv4-only
options.C: EID and RLOC are simply two different names for the exact same underlying address
options.D: RLOC identifies identity; EID identifies location

questions.explanation_es: El EID identifica quién es el dispositivo (no cambia si se mueve); el RLOC identifica dónde está topológicamente alcanzable.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What's the role of the LISP Map Server/Map Resolver system?

options.A: It encrypts LISP-encapsulated packets between sites
options.B: It performs NAT translation for all LISP-encapsulated data-plane traffic between every pair of sites
options.C: It replaces BGP in the underlay entirely
options.D: It answers mapping queries between EIDs and RLOCs, like DNS maps names to IPs

questions.explanation_es: El sistema Map Server/Resolver mantiene el mapeo EID-a-RLOC y resuelve consultas sobre dónde está alcanzable un EID, similar a cómo DNS resuelve nombres.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which statement about GRE tunnels is correct?

options.A: GRE requires IPsec to be fully configured and functioning before any GRE tunnel can be established
options.B: GRE encapsulates many protocols (including multicast) inside IP, but provides no encryption
options.C: GRE can only encapsulate TCP traffic
options.D: GRE encrypts the payload by default using AES

questions.explanation_es: GRE encapsula una amplia variedad de protocolos (incluido multicast) dentro de paquetes IP, pero por sí solo no cifra ni autentica el tráfico.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Why is GRE often combined with IPsec instead of using IPsec alone?

options.A: IPsec can't encrypt any IP traffic at all without GRE
options.B: GRE improves the encryption strength IPsec uses
options.C: GRE is required for IPsec to establish a Security Association at all, since IPsec can't negotiate one alone
options.D: IPsec alone doesn't transport multicast/dynamic routing well; GRE can encapsulate it first

questions.explanation_es: IPsec en modo túnel puro no soporta bien multicast ni protocolos de enrutamiento dinámico; GRE puede encapsular ese tráfico antes de que IPsec lo cifre.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which statement about the 'debug' command is correct?

options.A: It permanently rewrites the device's running configuration
options.B: It can consume real CPU, so it should be scoped and disabled after use
options.C: Its output is visible only through an SNMP trap
options.D: It has zero measurable CPU impact and is safe to leave running indefinitely

questions.explanation_es: Los comandos 'debug' pueden consumir CPU significativa; se recomienda acotarlos (por ejemplo con ACLs) y desactivarlos con 'undebug all' apenas se termina el troubleshooting.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What does an HTTP 204 No Content response typically indicate?

options.A: The request succeeded, but there is no content to return in the response body (common after a successful DELETE)
options.B: The request failed due to a client error
options.C: The requested resource was permanently moved to a new URL that the client must follow for all future requests, generated by the same framework middleware
options.D: The server is temporarily unavailable

questions.explanation_es: HTTP 204 No Content indica que la solicitud se procesó exitosamente pero no hay contenido para devolver — es común, por ejemplo, como respuesta a un DELETE exitoso donde no hace falta retornar datos.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a spine-leaf (Clos) data center fabric, what's a defining architectural principle?

options.A: Only one spine switch is allowed, with every leaf connecting to it
options.B: Leaves mesh directly to each other; the spine is a passive patch panel
options.C: Every leaf connects to every spine, and leaves never connect to each other directly
options.D: Spine switches connect only to each other in a ring, forming a separate mesh apart from the leaves

questions.explanation_es: En spine-leaf, cada leaf se conecta a todos los spines y los leaves nunca se conectan directamente entre sí, dando caminos ECMP predecibles entre cualquier par de leaves.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Why do data center fabrics favor spine-leaf over a traditional 3-tier design?

options.A: Spine-leaf eliminates Layer 3 routing, relying on a flat Layer 2 fabric with pure MAC learning at every leaf
options.B: It eliminates the need for any IP addressing in the data center
options.C: It always uses fewer total switch ports than an equivalent 3-tier design
options.D: It gives predictable, low-latency East-West bandwidth, matching server-to-server traffic

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico moderno de data center es mayormente East-West; spine-leaf ofrece ancho de banda y latencia predecibles entre cualquier par de leaves, mejor que un diseño jerárquico de 3 capas.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What does 'oversubscription ratio' refer to in a spine-leaf or hierarchical design?

options.A: The ratio of IPv4 to IPv6 addresses on a given VLAN
options.B: The percentage of switch ports administratively shut down
options.C: The ratio of downlink bandwidth to uplink bandwidth toward the next layer
options.D: Switches purchased versus switches actually installed in the rack

questions.explanation_es: El ratio de oversubscription compara el ancho de banda de los downlinks contra el de los uplinks hacia la capa siguiente; indica cuánto tráfico podría congestionarse si todos los downlinks se saturaran a la vez.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What distinguishes 'North-South' traffic from 'East-West' traffic?

options.A: North-South only occurs on IPv6; East-West only on IPv4
options.B: East-West traffic refers only to traffic between two data center sites; North-South only within one rack
options.C: North-South is between racks in the same row; East-West crosses sites
options.D: North-South flows client-to-server toward the edge; East-West flows server-to-server

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico North-South entra o sale del data center/campus hacia clientes o internet; el East-West ocurre entre servidores o cargas de trabajo dentro del mismo data center.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What best characterizes a 'hybrid cloud' deployment?

options.A: A mix of private and public cloud infrastructure, interconnected so workloads can move between them
options.B: On-premises infrastructure with no connection to any public cloud
options.C: A model defined solely by paying a subscription instead of buying hardware
options.D: A cloud model where a single provider hosts all workloads for unrelated customers on strictly isolated hardware, more accurately called single-tenant

questions.explanation_es: Una nube híbrida combina infraestructura privada con recursos de nube pública, interconectados para que cargas de trabajo o datos puedan moverse entre ambos entornos.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Which statement about Cisco Validated Designs (CVDs) is accurate?

options.A: CVDs are a personal certification engineers must hold before deploying any design
options.B: CVDs eliminate the need for any site-specific customization
options.C: A CVD is a physical hardware component installed in every switch
options.D: CVDs are tested reference architectures published by Cisco, reducing design risk

questions.explanation_es: Los CVD son arquitecturas de referencia probadas y documentadas por Cisco que ofrecen guías de diseño para escenarios específicos, reduciendo el riesgo frente a un diseño totalmente a medida.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a 2-tier (collapsed core) design, what trade-off is typically accepted versus 3-tier?

options.A: Lower cost/complexity for smaller networks, but less failure-domain separation and scale headroom
options.B: A 2-tier design always provides strictly higher total bandwidth than any 3-tier design of equal size, regardless of how many access switches connect
options.C: It requires strictly more physical switches than an equivalent 3-tier design
options.D: It cannot support any form of Layer 3 routing

questions.explanation_es: Al fusionar core y distribución en una capa, un diseño de 2 niveles reduce costo y complejidad para redes pequeñas, pero ofrece menos separación de dominios de falla y margen de crecimiento.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What does IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) refer to?

options.A: A cloud model where the provider delivers fully finished, ready-to-use applications with nothing at all for the customer to manage
options.B: A licensing term for a vendor's hardware warranty period
options.C: The provider offers compute/storage/network resources; the customer manages OS, apps, and much of the network
options.D: A protocol used to encrypt traffic between two IaaS providers

questions.explanation_es: IaaS es un modelo donde el proveedor ofrece recursos de cómputo fundamentales (VMs, almacenamiento, redes), mientras el cliente gestiona el sistema operativo, las aplicaciones y buena parte de la red.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What's the general idea behind expressing network configuration as 'intent' (IBN)?

options.A: An admin declares a high-level desired outcome, and the system translates and verifies it into low-level config
options.B: It eliminates the need for any network monitoring, since the network is assumed to always work once intent is declared
options.C: Every setting must still be typed manually into each device's CLI, with no automation
options.D: It refers to naming conventions used for VLAN IDs

questions.explanation_es: En redes basadas en intención, el administrador declara un resultado deseado de alto nivel, y el sistema traduce esa intención a la configuración detallada necesaria, verificando que el estado real coincida.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: How does a controller-based design approach compare to box-by-box CLI configuration?

options.A: A controller still requires configuring each device individually via CLI, just reviewing state after
options.B: A controller-based approach can only manage one device at a time, like box-by-box CLI
options.C: A controller centralizes config/policy, pushing consistency to many devices from one source of truth
options.D: Box-by-box CLI is always faster to deploy at scale than any controller-based approach

questions.explanation_es: Un enfoque basado en controlador centraliza configuración y política, empujando consistencia a muchos dispositivos desde una única fuente de verdad, a diferencia de configurar cada uno vía su propio CLI.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Why might a designer keep certain workloads on-premises rather than moving them to public cloud?

options.A: On-premises infrastructure typically achieves lower total cost of ownership than public cloud once hardware is fully depreciated
options.B: Public cloud providers are legally barred from hosting business applications
options.C: On-prem infrastructure needs no operational staff once installed
options.D: Regulatory, data sovereignty, latency, or legacy compatibility requirements may block a public-cloud move

questions.explanation_es: Requisitos regulatorios, de soberanía de datos, sensibilidad a latencia, o compatibilidad legacy pueden hacer poco práctico migrar ciertas cargas de trabajo a la nube pública.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What's the relationship between underlay and overlay in a fabric design (SD-Access, VXLAN DC)?

options.A: The overlay is the physical routed infrastructure; the underlay is the logical VXLAN on top
options.B: The underlay gives basic IP reachability between fabric nodes; the overlay builds segmented traffic on top of it
options.C: Underlay and overlay are unrelated networks that never interact
options.D: The overlay must be built first, and the underlay is generated automatically afterward with no IP addressing plan required at all

questions.explanation_es: El underlay provee conectividad IP básica entre nodos de la fabric; el overlay (VXLAN) se construye lógicamente encima para transportar tráfico segmentado y consciente de políticas.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What's the goal of deploying redundant links and devices at the distribution/core layer?

options.A: It's a purely cosmetic requirement with no real availability benefit
options.B: To intentionally create Layer 2 loops that STP is tested against during maintenance windows
options.C: To eliminate single points of failure, with automatic failover via STP, FHRP, or dynamic routing
options.D: To ensure the network requires manual intervention after every link failure

questions.explanation_es: El objetivo es eliminar puntos únicos de falla, de forma que la caída de un enlace o dispositivo no interrumpa la conectividad general, con conmutación automática vía STP, FHRP o enrutamiento dinámico.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How do NSF (Non-Stop Forwarding) and SSO work together?

options.A: NSF replaces the need for SSO entirely, making SSO obsolete and unnecessary on any modern Cisco platform available today
options.B: SSO syncs control-plane state so switchover skips a reboot; NSF keeps the data plane forwarding meanwhile
options.C: NSF only applies to wireless controllers; SSO only to routers
options.D: They're unrelated and can't be used together on the same device

questions.explanation_es: SSO sincroniza el estado del plano de control para que un switchover no requiera reinicio; NSF permite que el plano de datos siga reenviando durante ese switchover usando la última información conocida.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How many virtual MACs can GLBP use per group, compared to HSRP?

options.A: Up to four (one per AVF), letting client gateways load-balance across routers; HSRP uses just one
options.B: One unique virtual MAC per VLAN interface on every router, regardless of group membership
options.C: A single shared virtual MAC for the whole group, same as HSRP
options.D: No virtual MAC at all; it relies purely on virtual IP addressing

questions.explanation_es: GLBP puede asignar hasta cuatro MAC virtuales distintas (una por AVF) dentro de un grupo, balanceando respuestas ARP entre routers; HSRP usa una única MAC virtual por router activo.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What do the HSRP/VRRP 'hello timer' and 'hold timer' do?

options.A: Both control how often DHCP leases renew for hosts using the virtual gateway
options.B: The hello timer controls how often the port's link light blinks
options.C: The hello timer sets how often status messages are sent; the hold timer sets how long to wait before declaring a peer dead
options.D: The hold timer must always be set to a value smaller than the hello timer, or the protocol will fail to start entirely

questions.explanation_es: El hello timer controla cada cuánto se envían mensajes de estado; el hold/dead timer define cuánto puede pasar sin recibir un hello antes de considerar caído al peer e iniciar failover.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What does it mean for a router to be the VRRP 'IP address owner'?

options.A: It means the router has purchased a static public IP from a registry specifically for that VRRP group's address
options.B: It's the only device on the network permitted to send any traffic at all
options.C: It must be physically located in the same rack as every other group member
options.D: Its real interface IP matches the group's virtual IP, affecting default preemption/ping behavior

questions.explanation_es: El 'IP address owner' es el router cuya IP real de interfaz coincide con la IP virtual del grupo VRRP, afectando comportamientos por defecto como preemption automática y respuesta a pings.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How does a client host typically use an FHRP virtual IP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP)?

options.A: It must be manually reconfigured with a new gateway every time a failover occurs
options.B: It uses the virtual IP only for DNS resolution, never as a default gateway
options.C: FHRP virtual IPs can never be used as a default gateway; they exist purely for internal router-to-router hello negotiation of active/standby priority
options.D: It's configured as the client's default gateway, so off-subnet traffic always goes there regardless of which router is active

questions.explanation_es: El host cliente se configura con la IP virtual del FHRP como su default gateway, enviando siempre el tráfico fuera de subred a esa IP, sin importar qué router físico esté activo.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What's a valid reason to prefer VRRP over HSRP in a design?

options.A: VRRP encrypts user data traffic far more strongly than HSRP in every configuration
options.B: VRRP eliminates the need for any IP addressing on the participating routers
options.C: VRRP is the only FHRP that supports more than two routers per group
options.D: The environment includes non-Cisco routers needing an open, multi-vendor FHRP standard

questions.explanation_es: Si el entorno incluye routers de otros fabricantes que necesitan participar del mismo grupo de redundancia, se necesita un estándar abierto como VRRP en lugar del protocolo propietario HSRP.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What does FHRP authentication (HSRP/VRRP plaintext or MD5) actually do?

options.A: It only works over IPv6, with no IPv4 equivalent
options.B: It encrypts all user data traffic through the virtual gateway, like a full IPsec tunnel
options.C: It verifies hello/advertisement packets come from a legitimate group member, blocking rogue devices
options.D: It's mandatory; the protocol can't start without it configured

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación FHRP verifica que los mensajes hello/advertisement provienen de un miembro legítimo del grupo, ayudando a prevenir que un dispositivo no autorizado se inserte en el grupo.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What does OMP run over between vSmart and WAN Edge routers?

options.A: A separate physical out-of-band cable connecting every WAN Edge to vSmart directly
options.B: Only satellite links; it can't function over MPLS or broadband transport
options.C: Raw, unencrypted UDP with no session-layer protection
options.D: A DTLS- or TLS-secured control connection, similar in spirit to BGP over TCP

questions.explanation_es: OMP corre dentro de una conexión de control asegurada con DTLS o TLS entre vSmart y cada WAN Edge, protegiendo el intercambio de rutas, TLOCs y políticas del overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What does the 'color' attribute of a TLOC represent in SD-WAN?

options.A: A tag identifying the transport type (mpls, biz-internet, lte), usable in policy to influence path selection
options.B: The physical LED color shown on the router's chassis
options.C: A field that determines the DSCP marking applied to packets leaving that TLOC, used by ISPs but not evaluated by vSmart policy at all
