options.D: The IPsec cipher suite used for that TLOC's control connection

questions.explanation_es: El 'color' de un TLOC identifica el tipo de transporte subyacente; se usa en políticas centralizadas para influir en la selección de camino o restringir tráfico a ciertos transportes.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Why is vBond often given a publicly reachable IP, even if vSmart/vManage sit behind NAT?

options.A: New WAN Edges (often behind branch NAT) must reach it for initial orchestration and NAT traversal
options.B: A public IP address is a licensing requirement unrelated to any functional need for orchestration or reachability at all
options.C: vBond is never deployed with a public IP; this scenario doesn't occur
options.D: Only vBond needs internet access for periodic software updates

questions.explanation_es: vBond necesita ser alcanzable por cualquier WAN Edge nuevo/desconocido a través de internet para realizar la orquestación inicial y ayudar con el traspaso de NAT.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: How many vSmart controllers are typically deployed in production, and why?

options.A: Two or more, for redundancy, so losing one doesn't disrupt OMP distribution
options.B: None redundantly; OMP alone provides all needed control-plane redundancy
options.C: Exactly one per WAN Edge router, one vSmart per branch site
options.D: Exactly one only; the architecture forbids more than one

questions.explanation_es: Típicamente se despliegan dos o más vSmart por redundancia, de forma que la pérdida de uno no interrumpa la distribución de rutas OMP y políticas.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: How do WAN Edge routers protect data-plane traffic between sites?

options.A: In plaintext by default, with encryption as a rarely-used optional add-on
options.B: They build IPsec tunnels between each other, keyed via information distributed through OMP
options.C: vManage handles all data-plane encryption; WAN Edges have no role in it
options.D: Only via GRE tunnels, with no encryption capability

questions.explanation_es: Los WAN Edge establecen túneles IPsec entre sí, con claves distribuidas vía OMP/vSmart, para proteger el tráfico del plano de datos mientras cruza el underlay entre sitios.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What role does a WAN Edge's local configuration still play alongside controller-pushed policy?

options.A: WAN Edge routers download their entire configuration fresh from vBond on every single reboot, discarding controller policy
options.B: Local config only matters for wireless APs, never for the router's own routing
options.C: It keeps some device-specific settings (interfaces, templates) that work alongside centralized policy
options.D: It has no role at all; everything comes from the controllers

questions.explanation_es: Los WAN Edge mantienen cierta configuración local específica del dispositivo, que trabaja junto con la política empujada centralmente en lugar de ser completamente reemplazada por ella.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: How does a WAN Edge decide which remote TLOCs to build tunnels/BFD sessions with?

options.A: It builds a tunnel to literally every TLOC that has ever existed on the internet
options.B: Each edge is manually configured with every peer's IP; vSmart plays no role
options.C: Tunnel peers are chosen purely at random, with no controller influence
options.D: vSmart, via centralized policy, determines and advertises via OMP which TLOCs to connect to

questions.explanation_es: vSmart, guiado por la política centralizada, determina y anuncia vía OMP qué TLOCs debe conocer un WAN Edge, controlando efectivamente la topología resultante del overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is BFD used for between WAN Edge routers in an SD-WAN tunnel?

options.A: Rapidly detecting path failures or degraded conditions, enabling faster failover than routing-protocol timers alone
options.B: BFD only operates between vManage and a single WAN Edge, never between two WAN Edges directly, relying solely on OMP route withdrawal timers
options.C: Negotiating the initial IPsec encryption keys between two edges
options.D: Replacing the need for any IP addressing on transport interfaces

questions.explanation_es: BFD detecta rápidamente fallas o condiciones degradadas en el camino del plano de datos entre dos extremos de túnel, permitiendo una conmutación más rápida que los timers de un protocolo de enrutamiento.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does application-aware routing benefit a business-critical app like VoIP?

options.A: It monitors per-tunnel loss/latency/jitter and steers that app's traffic to whichever path meets its SLA
options.B: It requires disabling all encryption for the prioritized application
options.C: It eliminates the need for any WAN bandwidth at each site
options.D: It only works for file transfer protocols and has no effect on real-time applications like VoIP at all, since UDP flows are classified generically

questions.explanation_es: El enrutamiento consciente de aplicación monitorea métricas por túnel y puede dirigir dinámicamente el tráfico de una aplicación hacia el camino que cumpla su SLA definido.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is centralized, template-based config a benefit over manual branch CLI configuration?

options.A: Templates let admins define config once and apply it consistently, cutting errors and provisioning time
options.B: Template-based config guarantees no branch will ever experience an outage
options.C: Templates eliminate the need for any IP addressing plan
options.D: Templates are purely cosmetic in the vManage GUI, with the actual running config still entered manually on each router

questions.explanation_es: Las plantillas permiten definir la configuración una sola vez y aplicarla de forma consistente en muchos dispositivos, reduciendo errores y el tiempo de aprovisionamiento.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What's a legitimate concern about SD-WAN controllers being a centralized dependency?

options.A: Controller unavailability has no effect on the network at all
options.B: Sustained controller outage can block new config/policy changes, though existing data tunnels usually keep forwarding for a while
options.C: There's no such concern; centralizing control has zero downside
options.D: If any controller goes down for even one second, every WAN Edge router immediately loses all connectivity to every other WAN Edge instantly

questions.explanation_es: La falta de disponibilidad sostenida de los controladores puede afectar la capacidad de hacer nuevos cambios de configuración/política, aunque los túneles ya establecidos sigan reenviando tráfico por un tiempo.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does SD-WAN's transport independence help migrate away from expensive MPLS?

options.A: SD-WAN requires MPLS at every site and can't function if it's removed
options.B: Transport independence means no physical WAN circuit is needed at all
options.C: An org can gradually add broadband/LTE alongside or instead of MPLS, site by site
options.D: Transport independence only applies to data centers, not branch migrations

questions.explanation_es: Como SD-WAN corre su overlay sobre cualquier combinación de transportes, una organización puede introducir gradualmente banda ancha/LTE en reemplazo del MPLS, sitio por sitio.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why prefer DIA with local security inspection over backhauling internet traffic centrally?

options.A: Backhauling internet traffic to a central site always provides lower latency than accessing the internet locally at the branch
options.B: DIA avoids the extra latency/WAN cost of backhauling every request, if security controls exist at each branch
options.C: Backhauling is never supported to configure in an SD-WAN environment
options.D: DIA eliminates the need for any firewall or security inspection anywhere

questions.explanation_es: DIA con inspección de seguridad local evita la latencia y el costo de ancho de banda de retroceder cada solicitud a un hub central, mejorando la experiencia para aplicaciones en la nube.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What's a risk of enabling DIA at many branches without adequate local security?

options.A: DIA automatically disables all encryption for every branch application
options.B: There's no risk; DIA is always strictly safer than centralized internet access under every possible circumstance, regardless of local security posture
options.C: DIA can only be enabled if the branch site has zero connected users
options.D: Weak local security expands the attack surface, since each branch now has its own path to secure

questions.explanation_es: Habilitar DIA sin controles de seguridad locales adecuados amplía la superficie de ataque, ya que cada sucursal pasa a tener su propio camino a internet que debe asegurarse de forma independiente.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What TCO benefit does blending cheaper broadband with intelligent path selection offer over pure MPLS?

options.A: SD-WAN always costs more overall than an equivalent pure-MPLS design
options.B: SD-WAN guarantees that broadband internet will always be technically superior to MPLS in every performance metric, with zero trade-offs
options.C: TCO benefits only apply if an org eliminates all WAN circuits for satellite internet
options.D: Blending broadband/LTE with (or instead of) MPLS, plus app-aware routing, often cuts WAN spend while protecting key apps

questions.explanation_es: Combinando transporte de menor costo con MPLS y usando enrutamiento consciente de aplicación para el tráfico crítico, las organizaciones suelen reducir el gasto total en WAN manteniendo rendimiento aceptable.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What benefit does zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) offer when deploying SD-WAN to new sites?

options.A: ZTP requires an experienced engineer physically on-site at every branch to manually type the full configuration before joining the overlay
options.B: A device can be shipped, powered on by non-technical staff, and auto-fetch its identity/config from vBond/vManage
options.C: ZTP only works for wireless access points, not WAN Edge routers
options.D: ZTP eliminates the need for the device to ever have IP addressing configured

questions.explanation_es: ZTP permite que un WAN Edge se envíe, se conecte a energía y transporte por personal no técnico, y contacte automáticamente a vBond/vManage para recibir su identidad, software y configuración.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What happens when a wired endpoint first connects to a Fabric Edge Node?

options.A: The endpoint's traffic is immediately flooded unencapsulated to every other switch in the entire campus network, bypassing any authentication step
options.B: The edge node authenticates it (802.1X/MAB), then registers its identity and location with the control plane
options.C: The endpoint must manually register itself using a dedicated software client
options.D: The border node handles all registration; the edge node has no role

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Edge Node autentica/incorpora al endpoint (802.1X o MAB) y luego registra su identidad (EID) y ubicación ante el Fabric Control Plane node.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What role does LISP play in the SD-Access control plane?

options.A: It provides the EID-to-RLOC mapping the control plane node uses to track endpoint location
options.B: It's used to assign VLAN IDs to fabric-enabled switch ports
options.C: It's been fully replaced by BGP EVPN in every SD-Access release
options.D: It only encrypts data-plane traffic between edge nodes, with no control-plane role

questions.explanation_es: LISP provee el mecanismo de mapeo EID-a-RLOC que el Fabric Control Plane node usa para rastrear y resolver dónde está ubicado un endpoint dentro de la fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What happens control-plane-wise when a wired endpoint roams between Fabric Edge Nodes?

options.A: The new edge node updates the control plane with the endpoint's new location, without changing its IP
options.B: The endpoint must obtain a completely new IP address every time it roams
options.C: The old Fabric Edge Node continues to receive all traffic for the endpoint indefinitely, with no update ever sent
options.D: Roaming isn't supported for wired endpoints; only wireless clients can move

questions.explanation_es: El nuevo Fabric Edge Node actualiza al Control Plane node con la nueva ubicación (RLOC) del endpoint, sin que este necesite cambiar su propia dirección IP.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What does an 'anycast gateway,' configured identically on every Fabric Edge Node, mean?

options.A: It requires a different gateway IP configured per edge node
options.B: It's a wireless-only concept with no meaning for wired edge nodes
options.C: Every edge node shares the same gateway IP/MAC for a subnet, so endpoints keep the same gateway wherever they roam
options.D: An anycast gateway refers to one physically centralized router that all fabric traffic must always pass through, no matter where the endpoint is located

questions.explanation_es: El anycast gateway significa que todos los Fabric Edge Node usan la misma IP y MAC virtual de gateway para una subred, permitiendo que un endpoint siga usando la misma dirección al moverse.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does SD-Access integrate wireless traffic into the fabric data plane with a fabric-enabled WLC?

options.A: Wireless traffic is always sent unencapsulated onto the underlay
options.B: Wireless clients must obtain a completely separate, non-fabric IP addressing scheme entirely disconnected from any wired virtual network
options.C: Wireless traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated at the AP/edge node and carried over the same overlay as wired traffic
options.D: Wireless traffic can never be integrated into an SD-Access fabric

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico inalámbrico se encapsula en VXLAN en el access point (o el Fabric Edge Node) y se transporta sobre el mismo overlay usado para tráfico cableado, unificando la política.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What happens at the Fabric Border Node when the fabric advertises its VN subnets to a traditional routed core?

options.A: The Border Node requires every external router to run LISP natively first
options.B: The Border Node drops all traffic destined outside the fabric by default
options.C: The Border Node redistributes fabric routes into standard IP routing (BGP/OSPF) toward the external network
options.D: The Border Node converts all external traffic into VXLAN before it even reaches the fabric boundary regardless of support

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node redistribuye o anuncia las rutas de la fabric hacia el enrutamiento IP estándar (BGP u OSPF) hacia la red externa, traduciendo la alcanzabilidad interna a una forma entendible fuera.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why is careful IP addressing/subnet planning recommended before an SD-Access migration?

options.A: It's only necessary for IPv6 deployments, irrelevant to IPv4-only networks
options.B: IP addressing only matters for wireless clients in SD-Access, not wired migration
options.C: It has little bearing; the fabric renumbers every device automatically with no planning
options.D: SD-Access maps subnets to IP pools per VN, so clean planning simplifies grouping endpoints correctly

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access mapea subredes a IP pools asociados a redes virtuales, así que un esquema bien planeado facilita agrupar endpoints correctamente y simplifica el mapeo desde VLANs legacy.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What role can a traditional distribution switch play temporarily during a phased migration?

options.A: It must be powered off the instant any part of the campus starts migrating
options.B: It keeps serving non-migrated access switches/VLANs, connecting to the fabric via the Border Node
options.C: It can only interoperate if manually added as an unmanaged Fabric Edge Node
options.D: Traditional distribution switches automatically gain full fabric awareness the instant SD-Access is enabled anywhere in the campus

questions.explanation_es: Un switch de distribución tradicional puede seguir sirviendo a los switches/VLANs aún no migrados, conectándose a la fabric a través del Border Node durante todo el período de transición.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What's a common design approach for reaching shared services (DNS, DHCP, ISE) from SD-Access VNs?

options.A: Route leaking (often via a Fusion device) lets each VN's VRF reach the shared-services subnet in the global table
options.B: Shared services must be physically duplicated inside every single VN
options.C: Shared services become reachable by extending each VN's VRF directly onto the same VLAN as the global table at Layer 2
options.D: Shared services can only be reached by a direct cable from every access switch

questions.explanation_es: Se configura route leaking (a menudo vía un dispositivo Fusion) para que la VRF de cada VN pueda alcanzar la subred de servicios compartidos en la tabla global, sin fusionar toda la tabla de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: How does a Fabric Border Node typically handle internet-bound traffic from inside the fabric?

options.A: The Border Node requires every endpoint to manually configure its own static default route pointing directly at an ISP router with no dynamic option
options.B: It commonly advertises a default/external route into the fabric control plane, directing unknown traffic to itself
options.C: Internet-bound traffic from inside the fabric is always silently dropped
options.D: Every Fabric Edge Node needs its own direct physical internet connection

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node comúnmente anuncia una ruta default hacia el plano de control de la fabric, dirigiendo el tráfico interno destinado a destinos desconocidos (como internet) hacia sí mismo.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the purpose of the DiffServ QoS model, versus IntServ?

options.A: DiffServ marks traffic into a few classes (DSCP) with per-hop behavior, scaling without per-flow signaling like IntServ's RSVP
options.B: Both models rely on RSVP to signal reservations hop-by-hop, differing only in how many priority levels each one happens to support
options.C: DiffServ requires reserving bandwidth per flow beforehand, exactly like IntServ
options.D: DiffServ only applies to wireless networks

questions.explanation_es: DiffServ clasifica y marca el tráfico en pocas clases (DSCP) con comportamiento por salto, dando QoS escalable sin señalización por flujo, a diferencia de IntServ que usa RSVP por flujo individual.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the purpose of NBAR as a QoS classification mechanism, versus port-based classification?

options.A: NBAR replaces the need for any QoS marking or queuing configuration entirely, automating end-to-end QoS with zero policy-map
options.B: It only classifies encrypted traffic, never unencrypted flows
options.C: It inspects traffic beyond the port number (payload signatures) to identify apps without a fixed port
options.D: It only works for traffic using fixed, well-known ports

questions.explanation_es: NBAR inspecciona características del tráfico más allá del número de puerto para identificar la aplicación real, útil para aplicaciones que no usan un puerto fijo y predecible.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which queuing mechanism gives strict priority to a class like voice, ahead of other queues, up to a bandwidth limit?

options.A: WRED, a congestion-avoidance mechanism, is sometimes assumed to also grant priority queuing on lower-end platforms
options.B: FIFO queuing, which treats every packet from every class identically
options.C: Round-robin queuing, servicing every queue in strict rotation
options.D: LLQ, which adds a strict-priority queue on top of CBWFQ, policed to a configured bandwidth limit

questions.explanation_es: LLQ agrega una cola de prioridad estricta sobre CBWFQ, de forma que el tráfico de esa cola (como voz) siempre se atienda antes, dentro de un límite de ancho de banda policiado.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does CBWFQ provide that basic WFQ doesn't?

options.A: CBWFQ removes any bandwidth guarantee entirely, while WFQ guarantees 100% of bandwidth to every flow at the exact same time
options.B: CBWFQ and WFQ are identical, differing only in the IOS command used
options.C: CBWFQ lets admins define classes and guarantee bandwidth per class; WFQ auto-classifies with no admin-defined guarantee
options.D: CBWFQ only applies to wireless interfaces, WFQ only to wired ones

questions.explanation_es: CBWFQ permite definir explícitamente clases de tráfico y asignar un ancho de banda mínimo garantizado a cada una, mientras que WFQ básico clasifica flujos automáticamente sin garantía por clase.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the general purpose of Cisco's 'AutoQoS' feature?

options.A: It disables all QoS functionality to simplify troubleshooting
options.B: It auto-generates a baseline QoS config (classification, marking, queuing) from best practices
options.C: It only applies to wireless controllers, with no wired equivalent
options.D: It automatically detects and blocks all non-business traffic with no configuration

questions.explanation_es: AutoQoS genera automáticamente una configuración QoS base según las mejores prácticas recomendadas por Cisco, reduciendo el esfuerzo manual de construir una política desde cero.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which DSCP class typically marks call-signaling traffic (SCCP/SIP), distinct from voice bearer?

options.A: Signaling can't be marked with DSCP at all; it relies on Layer 2 CoS only
options.B: Signaling is always marked best-effort (0), same as web browsing
options.C: CS3 is the commonly recommended marking, lower priority than EF but still preferential over best-effort
options.D: Signaling traffic is typically marked AF31 rather than a Class Selector value, placing it in the multimedia streaming band instead

questions.explanation_es: CS3 es la marca comúnmente recomendada para señalización de llamadas, con menor prioridad garantizada que el tráfico de voz marcado con EF, pero aún preferencial frente a best-effort.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the recommended DSCP marking for interactive video, distinct from voice?

options.A: CS4, giving it the same strict-priority scheduling as voice
options.B: Best-effort (0), identical to ordinary web browsing
options.C: AF41 — strong preferential treatment, though not strict-priority like EF
options.D: No DSCP value at all; it relies solely on physical bandwidth reservation

questions.explanation_es: AF41 es la marca comúnmente recomendada para video interactivo, dando un trato preferencial fuerte, aunque no con la garantía de cola de prioridad estricta que sí tiene EF.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What's the relationship between a class-map, policy-map, and service-policy in Cisco QoS?

options.A: A policy-map can only be applied globally, never to an individual interface
options.B: A class-map defines what to match; a policy-map defines actions per class; a service-policy applies it to an interface
options.C: A service-policy defines classification; class-map/policy-map handle speed/duplex only
options.D: Class-map and policy-map are configured together as one combined statement, while service-policy actually defines the match criteria itself

questions.explanation_es: El class-map define qué hacer match; el policy-map define las acciones de QoS por clase; el service-policy aplica el policy-map a una interfaz específica — la jerarquía típica en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does 'admission control' (CAC) refer to in voice/video QoS design?

options.A: It guarantees unlimited simultaneous calls of any quality on any link
options.B: It refers to which VLANs are permitted to trunk across a switch port
options.C: It refers to a physical badge reader granting building access to equipment, unrelated to any bandwidth-based limiting function at all
options.D: It limits simultaneous voice/video sessions on a constrained link, rejecting new calls once bandwidth is exceeded

questions.explanation_es: El CAC limita el número de llamadas/sesiones simultáneas permitidas sobre un enlace de ancho de banda limitado, rechazando nuevos intentos una vez superado el umbral configurado.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why is marking most traffic as high priority or EF considered a QoS design mistake?

options.A: There's no downside; it always improves every application's performance
options.B: It mainly changes how traffic is displayed in NetFlow and monitoring tools, while actual queuing keeps using the default FIFO regardless
options.C: QoS marking is limited to one traffic class per router globally
options.D: Priority loses meaning as a differentiator — an oversubscribed priority queue can't protect truly latency-sensitive traffic

questions.explanation_es: Si la mayoría del tráfico se marca alta prioridad, la marca pierde su valor diferenciador — una cola de prioridad sobre-suscrita ya no protege confiablemente a las aplicaciones realmente sensibles a latencia.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is 'tail drop,' and why is it less desirable than WRED for TCP-heavy traffic?

options.A: It discards new packets once a queue is full, and can trigger many TCP flows to slow down simultaneously (global synchronization)
options.B: It refers to physically disconnecting the last centimeters of a cable to intentionally reduce signal quality for lab testing on shared-media Ethernet
options.C: It guarantees TCP flows never reduce their sending rate, no matter how full the queue is
options.D: It only occurs on wireless interfaces, with no wired equivalent

questions.explanation_es: Tail drop ocurre cuando una cola llena descarta cualquier paquete nuevo; en TCP esto puede sincronizar la reducción de tasa de muchos flujos a la vez, provocando oscilación de subutilización y recongestión.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why is preserving DSCP markings important as traffic crosses from LAN into WAN?

options.A: DSCP markings are automatically regenerated identically at every hop, making preservation an automatic behavior needing no design at all
options.B: If markings are stripped at the boundary, the WAN edge and downstream devices can't apply the correct treatment
options.C: DSCP markings only matter within a single VLAN, not once traffic leaves it
options.D: Preserving DSCP across the LAN/WAN boundary is prohibited by RFC 2474

questions.explanation_es: Si las marcas se eliminan en el límite LAN/WAN, el equipo de borde y los dispositivos aguas abajo no podrían aplicar el trato diferenciado correcto, anulando la clasificación hecha dentro del campus.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What are 'conform-action' and 'exceed-action' in a Cisco policing configuration (CIR)?

options.A: Conform-action handles traffic within the committed rate; exceed-action handles traffic above it (drop/re-mark)
options.B: Conform-action only applies inbound; exceed-action only to already-dropped traffic, making it moot
options.C: They determine which egress queue a packet enters based on VLAN tag, not measured rate
options.D: Both apply only to traffic exceeding CIR, differing in whether they re-mark DSCP or CoS

questions.explanation_es: El conform-action define qué hacer con el tráfico dentro de la tasa comprometida; el exceed-action define qué hacer con el que la supera (descartarlo o remarcarlo a menor prioridad).

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Which of these is a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor commonly used in data centers?

options.A: VMware ESXi, installed directly on server hardware with no separate host OS
options.B: A standard web browser, since browsers can virtualize an OS natively
options.C: VMware Workstation, which needs a full desktop OS first
options.D: Oracle VirtualBox, designed to run as a desktop app on a host OS

questions.explanation_es: VMware ESXi es un hipervisor Tipo 1 clásico: se instala directamente sobre el hardware sin un SO host de propósito general debajo. Workstation y VirtualBox son Tipo 2.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What resource-management responsibility does a hypervisor take on with multiple VMs?

options.A: None at all; each VM owns a physically separate copy of CPU/memory
options.B: It only manages network connectivity and has almost no role in CPU or memory allocation at all
options.C: It's handled entirely by the guest OS, with no hypervisor role
options.D: It schedules CPU, memory, storage, and I/O among VMs, giving each the illusion of dedicated hardware

questions.explanation_es: El hipervisor programa y asigna CPU, memoria, almacenamiento y E/S entre las VMs, dándole a cada una la ilusión de hardware dedicado mientras comparten el físico.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Which scenario is a more typical use case for a Type 2 hypervisor than Type 1?

options.A: A developer running a single test VM on their laptop alongside normal apps
options.B: Running dozens of production VMs in an enterprise data center
options.C: Providing the virtualization layer for a public cloud provider's compute service
options.D: Hosting a large-scale, highly available private cloud for an organization

questions.explanation_es: Un caso típico de Tipo 2 es un desarrollador probando una VM en su laptop personal; los escenarios de producción a gran escala son dominio de los Tipo 1.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What does hardware-assisted virtualization (Intel VT-x/AMD-V) provide?

options.A: It eliminates the need for a hypervisor altogether
options.B: A dedicated physical network card reserved only for hypervisor management traffic, unrelated to CPU virtualization at all
options.C: A guarantee every VM runs at the same clock speed as the host
options.D: CPU-level extensions that let the processor trap/handle privileged instructions more efficiently

questions.explanation_es: VT-x/AMD-V son extensiones a nivel de CPU que permiten al procesador manejar de forma más eficiente las instrucciones privilegiadas del SO huésped, reduciendo el overhead del hipervisor.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is a 'virtual machine monitor' (VMM), and how does it relate to 'hypervisor'?

options.A: They're essentially synonymous — the software layer creating/managing VMs
options.B: A VMM is a guest OS that can only run inside a Type 2 hypervisor
options.C: A VMM is a dedicated physical hardware device unrelated to hypervisors
options.D: A VMM is a guest-side driver translating hardware calls to hypervisor API calls

questions.explanation_es: VMM y 'hypervisor' son términos esencialmente sinónimos: la capa de software que crea, ejecuta y gestiona VMs, asignando el hardware físico a cada una.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: How does managing a Type 1 hypervisor typically differ from managing a Type 2 hypervisor?

options.A: Both can only be managed via a physically attached keyboard and monitor
options.B: There's no actual difference in management interface between the two
options.C: Type 1 is managed remotely (client/web/platform); Type 2 through a window in the host OS's desktop
options.D: Type 1 hypervisors can never be managed remotely and always require physical console access for every operation

questions.explanation_es: Un Tipo 1 se gestiona típicamente de forma remota, ya que no tiene escritorio propio; un Tipo 2 se gestiona vía una ventana de aplicación en el escritorio del SO host.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What's the difference between a 'cold migration' and a 'live migration' of a VM?

options.A: Live migration can only move a VM across hypervisor vendors; cold migration only within one vendor
options.B: They're the same process, distinguished only by time of day performed
options.C: Cold migration moves a powered-off VM (downtime); live migration moves a running VM with minimal downtime
options.D: Cold migration is always faster, since powered-off VMs transfer instantly

questions.explanation_es: Una migración en frío mueve una VM apagada (requiere downtime); una migración en vivo mueve una VM en ejecución con interrupción mínima o nula.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What does a DRS affinity or anti-affinity rule let an admin configure?

options.A: Affinity rules apply only to network switch port configuration, unrelated to VM placement
options.B: Affinity keeps certain VMs on the same host; anti-affinity keeps them on separate hosts
options.C: Anti-affinity forces every VM in the cluster onto the same single host
options.D: They only control a cosmetic color label in the management console

questions.explanation_es: Afinidad mantiene ciertas VMs en el mismo host; anti-afinidad las mantiene en hosts separados (por ejemplo, servidores redundantes), influyendo dónde DRS las coloca.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: How does VM encapsulation benefit disaster recovery strategies?

options.A: It has little relevance to DR, only day-to-day operations
options.B: A VM's files can be replicated to a secondary site and powered on quickly, without shipping/rebuilding hardware
options.C: Encapsulated VMs can't be replicated to any other site
options.D: It requires physically shipping the host server's hard drive to the DR site by courier, since a VM's files are assumed permanently bound to that disk

questions.explanation_es: Como el estado de una VM son archivos portables, pueden replicarse al storage de un sitio secundario y encenderse allí rápido durante un desastre, sin enviar hardware físico.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: What does 'promiscuous mode' on a vSwitch port group mean, and why is it disabled by default?

options.A: It encrypts all traffic on the port group and is disabled to save CPU
options.B: It only affects physical switches, with no vSwitch equivalent
options.C: It has little security implication and is disabled by default only to save a small amount of power, since copying frames to every vNIC uses extra CPU
options.D: It lets a VM's vNIC see all port-group traffic, not just its own; disabled since it'd expose other VMs' traffic

questions.explanation_es: El modo promiscuo permite que la vNIC de una VM vea todo el tráfico del port group, no solo el propio; se deshabilita por defecto porque expondría tráfico de otras VMs.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: In Open vSwitch, what is a 'bridge,' and how does it relate to physical/virtual interfaces?

options.A: OVS bridges have no relation to VM networking; used only for cable labeling
options.B: An OVS bridge is a physical cable connecting two data centers
options.C: A logical switch instance to which vNICs and physical NICs attach as ports
options.D: It can only ever have exactly one port attached, like a single cable

questions.explanation_es: Un bridge de OVS es una instancia de switch lógico a la que se conectan vNICs y NICs físicas como puertos, permitiendo que OVS conmute tráfico entre ellas.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: How does a router with multiple VRFs decide which routing table to use for an incoming packet?

options.A: It uses the RIB associated with the VRF the packet's ingress interface belongs to
options.B: It's based on the packet's source subnet, not the ingress interface's VRF, so two interfaces sharing a subnet would collide
options.C: It depends solely on the destination MAC address
options.D: The router randomly picks one of the configured VRF tables

questions.explanation_es: El router usa la tabla de enrutamiento asociada a la VRF de la interfaz de ingreso del paquete, ya que cada VRF mantiene su propia tabla independiente.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Why would a provider use VRFs to offer MPLS L3VPN to multiple customers on shared infrastructure?

options.A: VRFs keep each customer's routes/traffic logically isolated on the same shared PE routers
options.B: VRFs are used purely for internal management labeling with no effect at all on traffic isolation whatsoever
options.C: A provider can only support one customer VRF per chassis
options.D: VRFs require a completely separate physical network per customer

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs mantienen las rutas y el tráfico de cada cliente aislados de otros clientes que comparten los mismos routers PE y enlaces de core — la base del servicio MPLS L3VPN.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Which command shows the routing table specific to a particular VRF on IOS/IOS-XE?

options.A: VRF-specific tables can never be viewed independently
options.B: 'show vlan brief' is the only command that shows VRF routing info
options.C: 'show ip route vrf <name>', as distinct from the global 'show ip route'
options.D: 'show interfaces status' shows per-VRF routing table contents

questions.explanation_es: 'show ip route vrf <nombre>' muestra la tabla de enrutamiento específica de esa VRF, a diferencia de 'show ip route' que muestra la tabla global.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Why place guest wireless traffic into its own VRF, separate from the corporate VRF?

options.A: VRFs have no relevance to guest isolation at all; they're used only for voice traffic prioritization on switch uplinks
options.B: Guest VRF isolation requires physically separate cabling to every AP
options.C: Guest devices can't route to corporate resources via that VRF's table by default, a strong baseline of isolation
options.D: A separate VRF guarantees guest devices get faster internet than corporate

questions.explanation_es: Colocar el tráfico de invitados en su propia VRF asegura que, por defecto, no puedan enrutar hacia recursos corporativos, dando una base sólida de aislamiento a nivel de red.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What happens to global routing table entries once some interfaces move into custom VRFs?

options.A: A router can only ever have VRFs or a global table, never both
options.B: Interfaces left outside any VRF keep using the global table as before; only VRF-assigned interfaces use that VRF's table
options.C: Every interface, whether assigned to a VRF or not, is forced to share one combined table the moment any VRF exists anywhere on the device
options.D: Moving an interface into a VRF deletes every route in the global table

questions.explanation_es: Las interfaces sin asignar a ninguna VRF siguen usando la tabla global como antes; solo las interfaces asignadas a una VRF usan la tabla separada de esa VRF.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: How does a VRF relate to the broader idea of Layer 3 network virtualization?

options.A: A VRF is Layer 3 network virtualization: a logically separate routing instance on one device, like a hypervisor's VMs
options.B: Network virtualization and VRF are mutually exclusive concepts
options.C: A VRF creates a separate L2 domain, but all VRFs continue to share one single L3 table when making any forwarding decision at all
options.D: VRF is a physical hardware add-on card unrelated to virtualization

questions.explanation_es: Una VRF es una forma de virtualización de red en Capa 3: crea una instancia lógicamente separada de la función de enrutamiento en un único dispositivo, similar a cómo un hipervisor crea VMs.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What does the GRE header primarily contain, and what's its main function?

options.A: It carries routing protocol hellos and can't encapsulate anything else
options.B: It's functionally identical to a standard Ethernet header and operates only at Layer 2, indistinguishable from plain framing
options.C: It contains full encryption key material, making GRE as secure as IPsec
options.D: It identifies the encapsulated payload's protocol type and provides basic framing, with no encryption/authentication

questions.explanation_es: El encabezado GRE identifica el tipo de protocolo del payload encapsulado y provee el framing básico, sin proveer por sí mismo cifrado, autenticación ni entrega confiable.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: In IPsec, what's the role of IKE relative to AH and ESP?

options.A: IKE negotiates the Security Associations (keys, parameters) that AH/ESP then use to protect traffic
options.B: IKE encrypts user data directly; AH and ESP only negotiate keys
options.C: IKE, AH, and ESP are three interchangeable names for the same protocol
options.D: IKE encrypts data directly once a tunnel is established; AH/ESP only agree on the algorithm during initial negotiation

questions.explanation_es: IKE negocia y establece las Asociaciones de Seguridad (claves, parámetros) que AH y/o ESP luego usan para autenticar/cifrar el tráfico; IKE maneja el plano de control.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What is a Security Association (SA) in IPsec?

options.A: A bidirectional relationship needing only one instance total
options.B: A physical fiber-optic cable connector standard for IPsec links
options.C: A single globally shared encryption key used identically by every IPsec deployment worldwide, requiring no per-session negotiation at all
options.D: A unidirectional relationship defining security parameters for one traffic direction; a session needs at least two SAs

questions.explanation_es: Una SA es una relación unidireccional entre dos peers que define los parámetros de seguridad usados en una dirección; una sesión bidireccional típica requiere al menos dos SAs.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What does Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) provide in an IPsec IKE negotiation?

options.A: Past sessions stay undecryptable even if a later key is compromised, since each session derives fresh key material
options.B: A guarantee that IPsec traffic will never experience any packet loss under any network condition or configuration
options.C: It eliminates the need for any encryption key at all
options.D: A physical security camera feature unrelated to cryptography

questions.explanation_es: PFS asegura que, aunque una clave posterior se vea comprometida, el tráfico de sesiones anteriores no pueda descifrarse, porque cada sesión deriva claves de material fresco e independiente.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Why is MTU/fragmentation a concern with GRE and/or IPsec tunnels?

options.A: Encapsulation always reduces the total packet size, so MTU concerns only apply to native unencapsulated traffic
options.B: Fragmentation concerns only apply to IPv6 tunnels, not IPv4
options.C: MTU has no relevance; tunnel interfaces are exempt from fragmentation rules
options.D: Each encapsulation layer adds overhead that can push the packet above the path MTU, causing fragmentation or drops

questions.explanation_es: Cada capa de encapsulación agrega bytes de overhead, lo cual puede empujar el paquete por encima del MTU del camino, causando fragmentación o descarte si no se ajusta el MTU del túnel.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: Why does LISP maintain a map-cache on ITRs, and what happens on a cache miss?

options.A: It stores only local ETRs' RLOCs, for picking a local egress interface
options.B: It caches EID-to-RLOC mappings for fast reuse; on a miss, the ITR sends a map-request before encapsulating
options.C: It's purely optional and provides no benefit, since every packet always triggers a fresh lookup regardless of any prior mapping
options.D: A cache miss permanently blocks all future traffic to that EID

questions.explanation_es: El map-cache guarda mapeos EID-a-RLOC aprendidos recientemente; ante un cache miss, el ITR envía un map-request al sistema de mapeo antes de encapsular y reenviar.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What's the general structure of a LISP-encapsulated data packet?

options.A: LISP uses TCP as its outer transport, never UDP
options.B: The original EID-addressed packet is wrapped in UDP/IP with RLOC outer addressing, plus a LISP header
options.C: LISP discards the original packet entirely, generating a brand new one
options.D: LISP packets carry no outer IP header at all, transported purely using Layer 2 MAC addressing between ITR and ETR

questions.explanation_es: El paquete original (con su direccionamiento EID intacto) se encapsula dentro de UDP/IP, donde el encabezado externo usa RLOCs, con un encabezado LISP entre ambos.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What does an ETR do once it receives a LISP-encapsulated packet for one of its local EIDs?

options.A: It can only process plain unencapsulated IP, never decapsulate LISP
options.B: It decapsulates the LISP header and forwards the original packet to its local EID destination
options.C: It re-encapsulates the packet a second time with an entirely new destination before forwarding it anywhere at all
options.D: It discards every LISP packet it receives without processing

questions.explanation_es: El ETR decapsula el encabezado LISP y reenvía el paquete interno original hacia su destino EID local, tal como se veía antes de que el ITR remoto lo encapsulara.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: Why is LISP described as more scalable than injecting every endpoint's host route into the global table?

options.A: LISP still injects every single host route into the global routing table exactly the same way, providing zero scalability benefit
options.B: LISP keeps per-host EID-to-RLOC mapping in its own mapping system, avoiding bloating the core table with host routes
options.C: LISP eliminates the need for any routing table on any device
options.D: LISP's scalability claim has no technical basis

questions.explanation_es: LISP mantiene el mapeo EID-a-RLOC por host en su propio sistema separado, en lugar de inyectar rutas de host individuales en el core, evitando saturar la tabla de enrutamiento.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In SD-Access, how does LISP's ITR/ETR/Map-Server architecture map onto fabric roles?

options.A: LISP concepts apply only to wireless roaming between access points, not wired endpoints anywhere in the fabric
options.B: The Fabric Edge Node performs the Map-Server/Map-Resolver role
options.C: LISP roles apply only to wireless SD-Access, with no relevance to wired fabric roles
options.D: The Fabric Control Plane node takes the Map-Server/Map-Resolver role; Edge/Border Nodes act as xTRs

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Control Plane node asume el rol de Map-Server/Map-Resolver; los Edge y Border Nodes actúan en roles similares a xTR, aplicando la separación identidad/ubicación de LISP.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: How does EVPN's BGP control plane help detect duplicate/flapping MAC addresses in a VXLAN fabric?

options.A: Duplicate MAC detection relies on manually configured static MAC tables at every VTEP
options.B: EVPN prevents duplicate MACs by permanently disabling any VNI that has ever contained more than one host, regardless of configuration
options.C: Type-2 routes (with sequence numbers) let the control plane spot the same MAC advertised from two VTEPs nearly at once
options.D: EVPN's control plane has no ability to detect duplicate MACs at all

questions.explanation_es: Como la alcanzabilidad MAC se anuncia vía rutas Tipo 2 con números de secuencia, el plano de control puede detectar cuando la misma MAC se anuncia desde dos VTEPs casi simultáneamente.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: In a design where an IP phone and a PC share a single switch port (phone in the middle, PC connected to the phone's own switch port), how does 802.1Q trunking commonly get used at that access-layer port?

options.A: This scenario requires the port to become a completely unrestricted 802.1Q trunk carrying every VLAN configured anywhere in the switch, with no distinction between voice and data, since the phone's internal three-port switch is assumed to require full trunk visibility to tag its own management traffic, rather than only the two specific VLAN IDs it actually needs for voice and data
options.B: The switch port is often configured as a sort of limited multi-VLAN access port (using an auxiliary/voice VLAN alongside a data VLAN), where the IP phone tags its own voice traffic with the voice VLAN ID while the PC's traffic remains untagged in the native/data VLAN — a specialized trunking-like behavior rather than a full unrestricted trunk
options.C: IP phones can never share a switch port with a PC ; each device always requires a fully separate physical cable run
options.D: The PC's traffic must always be tagged with the voice VLAN ID, identical to the phone's traffic, with no separate data VLAN involved

questions.explanation_es: El puerto suele configurarse como una especie de puerto de acceso multi-VLAN limitado (usando una VLAN auxiliar/de voz junto a una VLAN de datos), donde el teléfono IP etiqueta su propio tráfico de voz con el VLAN ID de voz mientras el tráfico del PC permanece sin etiquetar en la VLAN nativa/de datos — un comportamiento tipo trunking especializado, no un trunk completo sin restricciones.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Which show command is commonly used on a Cisco IOS switch to verify the current trunking status, native VLAN, and allowed VLAN list of an interface?

options.A: 'show interfaces trunk', which lists trunk interfaces along with their native VLAN, allowed VLAN list, and the VLANs currently active/forwarding on that trunk
options.B: 'show spanning-tree vlan 1', which only shows STP topology information for VLAN 1 and does not display trunk allowed-VLAN configuration
options.C: 'show vlan brief', which lists each VLAN's assigned access ports but does not display a trunk interface's native VLAN or allowed-VLAN list directly
options.D: 'show mac address-table', which only shows learned MAC-to-port bindings and does not display trunk status directly

questions.explanation_es: 'show interfaces trunk' lista las interfaces trunk junto con su VLAN nativa, la lista de VLANs permitidas, y las VLANs actualmente activas/reenviando en ese trunk — el comando de verificación más directo para confirmar el estado de trunking en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the relationship between a trunk link's configured 'allowed VLAN' list and the VLAN database (VLAN configuration) that must also exist on the switch?

options.A: A VLAN must generally exist in the switch's VLAN database before it can be meaningfully carried across a trunk's allowed-VLAN list; listing a VLAN as 'allowed' on a trunk does not itself create that VLAN if it was never configured/active on the switch
options.B: The VLAN database only needs to be configured on the switch acting as the VTP server, while any other switch's trunk allowed-VLAN list can reference VLAN IDs that were never locally created in that switch's own VLAN database
options.C: The allowed-VLAN list on a trunk automatically creates every listed VLAN in the switch's VLAN database, with no separate VLAN configuration step ever required — provisioning each VLAN with default parameters the moment the 'switchport trunk allowed vlan' command is entered on the interface
options.D: There is no relationship between the two; a trunk can carry any VLAN ID at all, whether or not that VLAN exists anywhere in the switch's configuration

questions.explanation_es: Generalmente una VLAN debe existir en la base de datos VLAN del switch antes de que pueda transportarse de forma significativa a través de la lista de VLANs permitidas de un trunk; listar una VLAN como 'permitida' en un trunk no crea esa VLAN por sí sola si nunca se configuró/activó en el switch.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'switchport trunk pruning vlan' command, in environments where VTP pruning is used?

options.A: It is only relevant on Layer 3 routed interfaces and cannot be applied to a Layer 2 trunk port at all
options.B: It restricts which VLANs are eligible to be automatically pruned by VTP pruning on that specific trunk, refining the default set of prunable VLANs rather than statically hardcoding the entire allowed-VLAN list the way 'switchport trunk allowed vlan' does
options.C: It defines which VLAN is treated as that trunk's native VLAN for untagged traffic, and has no effect on which VLANs VTP is allowed to automatically prune from the link
options.D: It immediately removes the listed VLANs from that trunk's allowed-VLAN list, functioning identically to the 'switchport trunk allowed vlan remove' command rather than only affecting which VLANs are eligible for automatic VTP pruning

questions.explanation_es: Restringe qué VLANs son elegibles para ser podadas automáticamente por VTP pruning en ese trunk específico, refinando el conjunto por defecto de VLANs podables, en lugar de fijar de forma estática toda la lista de VLANs permitidas como hace 'switchport trunk allowed vlan'.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is the relationship between an EtherChannel's logical 'Port-channel' interface and its physical member interfaces, in terms of Layer 3 configuration (for a routed EtherChannel)?

options.A: A Layer 3 EtherChannel cannot have any IP address configured anywhere, on either the Port-channel interface or its members
options.B: The logical Port-channel interface and its physical members must always be assigned to two entirely different, unrelated VRFs
options.C: For a Layer 3 EtherChannel, IP addressing and most Layer 3 configuration is applied to the logical Port-channel interface itself, not to each individual physical member interface, since the member interfaces operate as part of the single logical bundled link represented by the Port-channel
options.D: Layer 3 IP addressing must always be configured identically and separately on every individual physical member interface, with no IP configuration ever applied to the logical Port-channel interface

questions.explanation_es: Para un EtherChannel de Capa 3, el direccionamiento IP y la mayor parte de la configuración de Capa 3 se aplica a la interfaz lógica Port-channel en sí, no a cada interfaz física miembro individualmente, ya que las interfaces miembro operan como parte del único enlace agrupado lógico representado por el Port-channel.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is 'Cross-Stack EtherChannel' (or similar multi-chassis EtherChannel technologies like StackWise or VSS-based EtherChannel), and what availability benefit does it provide over a standard single-switch EtherChannel?

options.A: Cross-stack EtherChannel allows member links to terminate on separate switches only when those switches are running completely independent control planes, without requiring any StackWise or VSS synchronization between the chassis involved
options.B: This technology is used for wireless access point redundancy and has no application to wired switch-to-switch EtherChannel links
options.C: Cross-stack EtherChannel eliminates the need for any physical cabling between the two switches involved in the bundle entirely
options.D: It allows the individual physical member links of a single logical EtherChannel bundle to terminate on two (or more) physically separate switches that act as one logical switching entity, so that the failure of one entire physical chassis does not take down the whole EtherChannel bundle, only the member links that happened to terminate on the failed chassis

questions.explanation_es: Permite que los enlaces físicos individuales miembro de un único bundle lógico de EtherChannel terminen en dos (o más) switches físicamente separados que actúan como una única entidad de switching lógica, de forma que la falla de un chasis físico completo no derribe todo el bundle de EtherChannel, solo los enlaces miembro que terminaban en el chasis que falló — una mejora de disponibilidad importante sobre un EtherChannel de un solo switch.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is a common recommended practice regarding the physical diversity of the individual links that make up an EtherChannel bundle, when availability is a priority?

options.A: Physical diversity of member links has little bearing on EtherChannel availability, since all member links are logically treated identically regardless of which physical hardware they terminate on
options.B: EtherChannel technology itself physically prevents an administrator from ever placing member links on different line cards or modules
options.C: Best practice generally treats line-card placement of member links as having negligible impact on availability, since a modular chassis's supervisor is expected to reroute a failed line card's traffic internally to a backup card before the EtherChannel protocol itself would ever detect a member-link failure
options.D: Where practical, spreading member links across different physical line cards/modules (on a modular chassis) or different physical paths reduces the risk that a single hardware fault (like one line card failing) takes down every member link of the bundle simultaneously, preserving the redundancy benefit the bundle is meant to provide

questions.explanation_es: Cuando es práctico, distribuir los enlaces miembro entre distintas tarjetas de línea/módulos físicos (en un chasis modular) o distintos caminos físicos reduce el riesgo de que una sola falla de hardware (como una tarjeta de línea cayéndose) derribe todos los enlaces miembro del bundle simultáneamente, preservando el beneficio de redundancia que el bundle está pensado para dar.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does RSTP's 'proposal/agreement' mechanism enable much faster convergence than classic 802.1D STP's timer-based transitions?

options.A: RSTP's proposal/agreement mechanism has nothing to do with convergence speed and exists purely for logging/auditing purposes
options.B: RSTP allows a switch to actively propose that its port become the new designated forwarding port and receive an explicit agreement back from its neighbor, enabling both sides to synchronize and move directly to forwarding without waiting through the fixed listening/learning timer delays that classic 802.1D relies on
options.C: The proposal/agreement mechanism only functions on the Root Bridge itself and has no effect on convergence anywhere else in the topology
options.D: RSTP achieves faster convergence by disabling all STP calculations entirely and simply forwarding on every port unconditionally with no loop prevention at all, treating RSTP as though it traded away loop protection rather than merely replacing 802.1D's fixed timers with an explicit proposal/agreement handshake that still fully computes and enforces the spanning tree

questions.explanation_es: RSTP permite que un switch proponga activamente que su puerto se convierta en el nuevo puerto designado de reenvío y reciba un acuerdo explícito de su vecino, permitiendo que ambos lados se sincronicen y pasen directamente a forwarding sin esperar los retrasos de temporizador fijos de listening/learning en los que se basa el 802.1D clásico.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is a 'backup port' role, specific to RSTP, and when does it typically appear?

options.A: A backup port is simply another name for the Root Port, with the two terms being fully interchangeable
options.B: Backup ports only exist in classic 802.1D STP and were entirely removed from RSTP, with no equivalent role present in RSTP
options.C: A backup port refers to a completely separate physical switch kept powered off in a storage closet as a spare replacement unit — intended to be manually swapped in by an administrator if the primary switch fails, with the term 'backup port' generally understood by analogy to a cold-spare hardware unit rather than to any specific RSTP port-role designation assigned during normal spanning-tree operation
options.D: A backup port is a non-designated port role that appears when a switch has more than one port connected to the same shared LAN segment (e.g., via a hub), representing a redundant path to a segment the switch can already reach via its own designated port on that same segment; it is ready to take over the designated role if the current designated port on that segment fails

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto backup es un rol de puerto no designado que aparece cuando un switch tiene más de un puerto conectado al mismo segmento de LAN compartido (por ejemplo, vía un hub), representando un camino redundante hacia un segmento que el switch ya puede alcanzar por su propio puerto designado en ese mismo segmento; está listo para asumir el rol designado si el puerto designado actual de ese segmento falla.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does 'err-disable recovery' functionality help operationally after a port has been automatically shut down by a protective feature like BPDU Guard or UDLD?

options.A: Err-disable recovery can be configured to automatically re-enable a port that was shut down due to a specific cause (like BPDU Guard or UDLD) after a configured timeout period, reducing the need for an administrator to manually intervene and re-enable the port every single time the protective feature triggers, while still preserving the initial protective shutdown behavior
options.B: Enabling err-disable recovery for a given cause also raises the violation threshold for that specific trigger, so a port tolerates several additional BPDU Guard or UDLD events before being shut down again, rather than the recovery feature simply re-enabling the port unconditionally once the configured timeout period has elapsed each time the same condition occurs
options.C: Err-disable recovery works by lowering the severity of the triggering violation so that subsequent identical events are merely logged rather than causing another shutdown, rather than by re-enabling the port itself after a timer expires
options.D: Err-disable recovery disables the affected port forever, with no possibility of it ever being automatically or manually re-enabled again

questions.explanation_es: La recuperación de err-disable puede configurarse para volver a habilitar automáticamente un puerto que fue apagado por una causa específica (como BPDU Guard o UDLD) después de un período de timeout configurado, reduciendo la necesidad de que un administrador intervenga manualmente y vuelva a habilitar el puerto cada vez que se dispara la función protectora, mientras sigue preservando el comportamiento inicial de apagado protectivo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the role of the 'successor' route in EIGRP's DUAL algorithm?

options.A: The successor is always a backup-only route that is never installed in the routing table
options.B: A successor route is selected based only on the lowest hop count to the destination, with the composite bandwidth/delay metric used only as a tiebreaker when two or more neighbors report an identical hop count to that destination, similar to how RIP falls back to additional criteria only after hop count fails to produce a single best path
options.C: The successor is the route with the lowest overall composite metric to a given destination, and it is the route that is actually installed in the routing table and used for forwarding, while a feasible successor (if one exists) is kept as a loop-free backup in the topology table
options.D: EIGRP does not use the term 'successor' at all; this terminology is exclusive to OSPF's SPF algorithm

questions.explanation_es: El successor es la ruta con el menor costo compuesto general hacia un destino dado, y es la ruta que realmente se instala en la tabla de enrutamiento y se usa para reenviar tráfico, mientras que un feasible successor (si existe) se mantiene como respaldo libre de loops en la tabla de topología.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the 'Feasibility Condition' that a backup route must satisfy in EIGRP to be considered a valid feasible successor (and thus be loop-free)?

options.A: There is no such thing as a Feasibility Condition in EIGRP; any advertised route from any neighbor is automatically accepted as a feasible successor with no verification — this is because EIGRP is generally described as relying on the DUAL finite state machine's query/reply process for loop avoidance rather than an upfront metric check against the successor's feasible distance
options.B: The Feasibility Condition only applies to OSPF's SPF calculation and has little equivalent concept in EIGRP
options.C: A neighbor's advertised distance (its own reported metric to the destination) to that destination must be strictly less than the current successor's feasible distance (the local router's own best metric to that destination); this guarantees the neighbor is not routing back through the local router itself, avoiding a loop
options.D: The Feasibility Condition requires the backup route to have an identical metric to the successor route in every single case, with no tolerance for any difference

questions.explanation_es: La distancia anunciada de un vecino (su propio costo reportado hacia el destino) debe ser estrictamente menor que la distancia factible (feasible distance) actual del successor (el mejor costo propio del router local hacia ese destino); esto garantiza que el vecino no esté enrutando de vuelta a través del propio router local, evitando un loop.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How does EIGRP behave when a successor route fails and no feasible successor exists in the topology table for that destination?

options.A: EIGRP enters 'Active' state for that route and sends Query packets to its neighbors asking whether they have an alternate loop-free path to the destination, waiting for Reply packets before recalculating and re-installing a new best route (or declaring the destination unreachable if no neighbor has a valid path)
options.B: EIGRP immediately and permanently marks the entire routing process as failed and requires a full router reboot to recover from the loss of any single route — since the DUAL finite state machine is considered to have no recovery path once a destination loses both its successor and every feasible successor, forcing a restart from a clean table
options.C: EIGRP silently drops all traffic to that destination forever with no attempt to query neighbors or recompute an alternate path
options.D: EIGRP always has a feasible successor pre-computed for every possible destination in every topology, making this active-state query scenario not supported

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP entra en estado 'Active' para esa ruta y envía paquetes Query a sus vecinos preguntando si tienen un camino alternativo libre de loops hacia el destino, esperando paquetes Reply antes de recalcular e instalar una nueva mejor ruta (o declarar el destino inalcanzable si ningún vecino tiene un camino válido).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why does OSPF, as a link-state protocol, generally require every router within the same area to have an identical Link State Database (LSDB) before their individual SPF calculations produce a consistent, loop-free view of the topology?

options.A: OSPF routers within the same area synchronize their LSDBs only at initial adjacency formation; after that, each router's LSDB evolves independently based on locally received updates, and OSPF relies on periodic SPF recalculation alone (rather than continuous LSDB synchronization) to eventually reconcile any resulting differences between neighbors without requiring a flooding mechanism to actively keep every router's database identical in real time
options.B: Because SPF calculates each router's own shortest-path tree from the same underlying topology information, all routers within an area must have synchronized, identical LSDBs — if routers had inconsistent topology information, their independently calculated shortest-path trees could disagree and potentially create routing loops or blackholes
options.C: OSPF does not use an LSDB at all; that term is exclusive to EIGRP's topology table
options.D: LSDB synchronization is only relevant across different OSPF areas and has little importance for routers within the same single area

questions.explanation_es: Como SPF calcula el árbol de menor camino de cada router a partir de la misma información de topología subyacente, todos los routers dentro de un área deben tener LSDBs sincronizadas e idénticas — si los routers tuvieran información de topología inconsistente, sus árboles de menor camino calculados independientemente podrían no coincidir y potencialmente crear loops de enrutamiento o agujeros negros.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is EIGRP 'unequal-cost load balancing' via the 'variance' command, and how does it differ from OSPF's typical equal-cost-only load balancing?

options.A: OSPF natively supports unequal-cost load balancing by default in every implementation, while EIGRP only ever supports equal-cost load balancing with no variance capability at all, reversing which protocol actually offers the variance-based unequal-cost feature that lets traffic split across multiple loop-free paths at once, not merely whichever single path happens to carry the lowest overall cost
options.B: Neither EIGRP nor OSPF is capable of load balancing traffic across more than a single path
options.C: The variance command in EIGRP disables load balancing entirely, forcing all traffic onto a single best path
options.D: EIGRP's variance command allows traffic to be load-balanced across multiple feasible-successor paths even when their metrics are not exactly equal (as long as each qualifies as a feasible successor and falls within the configured variance multiplier of the best metric), whereas standard OSPF (without additional features) only load-balances across paths that have exactly equal cost

questions.explanation_es: El comando variance de EIGRP permite balancear tráfico entre múltiples caminos feasible successor aunque sus métricas no sean exactamente iguales (siempre que cada uno califique como feasible successor y esté dentro del multiplicador de variance configurado respecto a la mejor métrica), mientras que OSPF estándar (sin funciones adicionales) solo balancea entre caminos de costo exactamente igual.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why might an organization prefer OSPF over EIGRP in a multi-vendor network environment containing routers from vendors other than Cisco?

options.A: Because EIGRP was published as an informational RFC, most non-Cisco router vendors have since implemented full EIGRP support in their platforms, making EIGRP just as viable a choice as OSPF for a genuinely multi-vendor environment today, with only minor differences remaining in how each vendor implements the DUAL algorithm's timer defaults
options.B: Multi-vendor environments must always use RIP instead of either EIGRP or OSPF, since neither is considered usable outside a single-vendor network
options.C: Vendor interoperability considerations mainly come down to licensing cost rather than protocol design, since both EIGRP and OSPF require a separate paid feature license on non-Cisco platforms before either protocol can be enabled
options.D: OSPF is an open, IETF-standardized protocol (RFC 2328 for OSPFv2) implemented by essentially every major router vendor, providing straightforward multi-vendor interoperability, whereas EIGRP was historically Cisco-proprietary (though Cisco has since published parts of it as an informational RFC, it remains predominantly a Cisco-centric protocol in practice)

questions.explanation_es: OSPF es un protocolo abierto, estandarizado por el IETF (RFC 2328 para OSPFv2) e implementado esencialmente por todos los principales fabricantes de routers, dando interoperabilidad multi-vendor directa, mientras que EIGRP fue históricamente propietario de Cisco (aunque Cisco luego publicó partes de él como un RFC informativo, en la práctica sigue siendo un protocolo predominantemente centrado en Cisco).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What must generally match between two OSPF neighbors for them to successfully form a full adjacency (beyond just being on the same subnet)?

options.A: OSPF adjacencies require both routers to be running the identical IOS or NX-OS software train and version, since a mismatched OSPF software version between routers is treated as a fatal parameter mismatch during the initial hello exchange
options.B: OSPF neighbors primarily need matching hello and dead timers to form an adjacency; the area ID and authentication settings are only used after the adjacency is already up, to control which LSAs are subsequently accepted from that neighbor
options.C: Only the router's hostname needs to match between neighbors; all other OSPF-specific parameters are irrelevant to adjacency formation
options.D: Key parameters such as the area ID for that link, hello/dead timer intervals, authentication configuration (if used), and MTU (if MTU mismatch checking is not disabled) generally need to be consistent between neighbors, or the adjacency will fail to form or get stuck in an incomplete state

questions.explanation_es: Parámetros clave como el área ID de ese enlace, los intervalos de temporizador hello/dead, la configuración de autenticación (si se usa), y el MTU (si la verificación de desajuste de MTU no está deshabilitada) generalmente deben ser consistentes entre vecinos, o la adyacencia no logrará formarse o quedará atascada en un estado incompleto.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the purpose of the OSPF 'router-id', and how is it typically determined if not manually configured?

options.A: The router-id is a randomly generated value that changes every time the router reboots, with no consistent selection logic
options.B: The router-id is derived from the router's chassis serial number by default whenever a loopback interface is configured, and only falls back to using an interface IP address if the platform does not support serial-number-based ID generation, which is why two routers of the same model purchased in sequence sometimes need their router-ids manually adjusted to avoid a collision
options.C: The router-id is a unique 32-bit identifier (formatted like an IP address) used to identify a router within the OSPF domain; if not manually configured, it is typically automatically selected as the highest IP address among the router's active loopback interfaces, or if none exist, the highest IP address among its active physical interfaces at the time OSPF starts
options.D: Every router within the same OSPF area must have a router-id that falls within that area's configured address range, similar to how interface IP addresses must belong to the area's subnet

questions.explanation_es: El router-id es un identificador único de 32 bits (con formato de dirección IP) usado para identificar a un router dentro del dominio OSPF; si no se configura manualmente, típicamente se selecciona de forma automática como la IP más alta entre las interfaces loopback activas del router, o si no existe ninguna, la IP más alta entre sus interfaces físicas activas al momento en que OSPF arranca.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the function of the OSPF 'network' command (or, alternatively, enabling OSPF directly under an interface) when configuring OSPF on a router?

options.A: The network command is used to configure static routes and has little relevance to dynamic OSPF operation
options.B: It specifies which interfaces (matched by their IP address falling within the specified network/wildcard-mask range) should participate in the OSPF process, both by enabling OSPF to form adjacencies over them and by causing their connected network(s) to be advertised into OSPF
options.C: The network command primarily controls which interfaces are permitted to form OSPF adjacencies, but the actual advertisement of that interface's connected subnet into OSPF must be configured separately using a distinct 'redistribute connected' statement
options.D: Every interface on a router automatically participates in OSPF the moment the 'router ospf' process is created, making the network command unnecessary and non-functional

questions.explanation_es: Especifica qué interfaces (identificadas porque su dirección IP cae dentro del rango de red/wildcard-mask especificado) deben participar en el proceso OSPF, tanto habilitando que formen adyacencias a través de ellas como haciendo que su(s) red(es) conectada(s) se anuncien en OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why does configuring an OSPF interface's network type as 'point-to-point' (instead of the default broadcast type) make sense on a subnet where only exactly two routers will ever be connected?

options.A: Point-to-point network type configuration is only valid on interfaces with more than ten connected routers, making it inapplicable to a two-router segment
options.B: DR/BDR election always improves convergence time on a two-router segment, so configuring point-to-point network type would actually be a mistake in this scenario
options.C: Network type configuration has little effect on DR/BDR election regardless of how many routers share the segment
options.D: With only two routers on the segment, DR/BDR election serves no real purpose (there's no need to reduce adjacency count on a link that only ever has two potential neighbors), so configuring point-to-point skips that election process, allowing the two routers to form a full adjacency directly and slightly speeding up convergence, since point-to-point links don't need a DR/BDR relationship at all

questions.explanation_es: Con solo dos routers en el segmento, la elección de DR/BDR no cumple un propósito real (no hace falta reducir la cantidad de adyacencias en un enlace que de todos modos solo tiene dos vecinos potenciales), así que configurar point-to-point se salta ese proceso de elección, permitiendo que los dos routers formen una adyacencia completa directamente y acelerando levemente la convergencia, ya que los enlaces point-to-point no necesitan ninguna relación de DR/BDR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the purpose of configuring OSPF authentication (plaintext, MD5, or newer cryptographic methods) on an interface or area?
