options.B: Tuning an intrusion policy always and disables every single rule in the entire rule set, leaving the policy with zero active detection capability regardless of the specific tuning performed
options.C: There is no meaningful reason an organization's specific environment or technology stack would ever warrant any tuning of a default intrusion policy rule set, since every organization is assumed to always have exactly identical traffic patterns and application usage, overlooking that FTD's inspected traffic mix, exposed applications, and OS/patch baseline genuinely differ across organizations, which is exactly why Cisco Talos periodically updates recommended rule sets per deployment profile
options.D: Intrusion policy rule sets can never be tuned or customized in any way from their default, out-of-the-box configuration on any Cisco Firepower/FTD platform

questions.explanation_es: Un conjunto de reglas por defecto y ampliamente aplicable puede incluir firmas para vulnerabilidades/ataques no relevantes a la pila tecnológica específica de esa organización (generando ruido de alertas innecesario), mientras potencialmente no está específicamente ajustado a las aplicaciones y patrones de tráfico que realmente están presentes, así que el ajuste (deshabilitando reglas irrelevantes, ajustando umbrales) ayuda a enfocar la detección en amenazas genuinamente relevantes y reduce el volumen de alertas de falsos positivos.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Why might FMC's dashboard prominently surface 'top attackers' and 'top targets' summary views, rather than only presenting a flat, chronological list of every individual security event?

options.A: FMC's dashboard summary views like top attackers and top targets are generated only once per day during a scheduled reporting job, so an analyst investigating an event as it happens must still work from the flat, real-time chronological event list instead
options.B: Top attackers/targets views are only relevant for wireless network traffic, and provide no meaningful analytical value for wired network traffic passing through an FTD device
options.C: These summary views provide no practical analytical value beyond what a flat chronological event list alone already provides, since an analyst is assumed to always be able to just as easily identify significant patterns by manually scrolling through every individual event one at a time, an assumption that overlooks how quickly manual review becomes impractical once event volume exceeds what a human can scan
options.D: Aggregated summary views (like top attackers/targets) help an analyst quickly identify which sources or destinations are involved in the most significant volume of security-relevant activity, surfacing patterns that might not be immediately obvious when scrolling through potentially thousands of individual, chronologically-ordered event log entries one at a time

questions.explanation_es: Las vistas resumen agregadas (como top attackers/targets) ayudan a un analista a identificar rápidamente qué orígenes o destinos están involucrados en el mayor volumen de actividad relevante para la seguridad, revelando patrones que podrían no ser inmediatamente obvios al desplazarse por potencialmente miles de entradas de log de eventos individuales ordenadas cronológicamente una por una.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What command is commonly used on a Cisco switch to verify whether MACsec is actually established and encrypting traffic on a given interface?

options.A: 'show ip route' displays MACsec session status directly alongside routing table entries, with no separate MACsec-specific command needed
options.B: 'show macsec summary' (or 'show macsec interface <int>'), which displays the MACsec status, cipher suite, and key/session information for that interface, confirming whether encryption is actually active rather than simply configured
options.C: MACsec status can never be verified through any Cisco IOS command output, and can only be inferred by physically inspecting the cable with a specialized optical tool, a claim that overlooks the dedicated show commands built specifically to display MACsec session and cipher status
options.D: 'show authentication sessions interface <int>' displays whether 802.1X authentication succeeded on that port, but it does not separately confirm whether the resulting MACsec encryption session itself is actually up and passing encrypted traffic

questions.explanation_es: 'show macsec summary' (o 'show macsec interface <int>') muestra el estado de MACsec, el conjunto de cifrado, y la información de clave/sesión de esa interfaz, confirmando si el cifrado realmente está activo en lugar de solo configurado.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What role does the SD-Access Border Node play in interoperability with external networks?

options.A: A border node can only exist in a fabric with zero external connectivity
options.B: Border node functionality is only relevant to SD-WAN, not SD-Access
options.C: It advertises fabric routes outward and imports external routes in, translating fabric traffic to/from traditional traffic
options.D: The border node's primary role is providing extra port density for endpoint connections, with route advertisement handled elsewhere entirely

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node es el dispositivo responsable de anunciar las rutas conocidas por la fabric hacia la red externa e importar rutas externas, actuando como punto de traducción entre ambos mundos.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which two protocols make up the IPsec header options used to protect a packet? (Select two)

options.A: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
options.B: AH (Authentication Header)
options.C: DES
options.D: AES

questions.explanation_es: AH (Authentication Header) y ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) son los dos protocolos de cabecera de IPsec. AES y DES son algoritmos de cifrado usados dentro de ESP, no cabeceras de IPsec en sí.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What IP protocol number is assigned to ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)?
questions.explanation_es: ESP usa el número de protocolo IP 50. AH usa el 51, GRE usa el 47, y OSPF usa el 89.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which factors does a router evaluate, in order, when choosing the best route to install in the routing table? (Select three)

options.A: Administrative distance
options.B: Prefix length (longest match)
options.C: Router ID
options.D: Metric

questions.explanation_es: El router primero prefiere la ruta con el prefijo más específico (longest match), luego, entre rutas con el mismo prefijo, la de menor distancia administrativa, y finalmente, entre rutas de la misma distancia administrativa, la de menor métrica. El Router ID solo se usa como desempate en casos muy específicos (p. ej. OSPF), no como criterio general de selección de ruta.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the output of 'show ip route', which code letter identifies a static route?

options.A: C
options.B: D
options.C: S
options.D: O

questions.explanation_es: 'S' identifica una ruta estática en la tabla de ruteo de Cisco IOS. 'C' es conectada, 'O' es OSPF, y 'D' es EIGRP.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which command correctly configures a static route to network 10.10.10.0/24 via next-hop 20.20.20.2?
questions.explanation_es: La sintaxis correcta en IOS es 'ip route <red> <máscara> <next-hop>', por lo que sería 'ip route 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0 20.20.20.2'.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: If a router learns the same destination network via both OSPF and RIP, which route does it install by default?

options.A: Both routes, load-balanced equally
options.B: The OSPF route, since OSPF's default administrative distance (110) is lower than RIP's (120)
options.C: Neither route is installed until manually resolved
options.D: The RIP route, since RIP has a lower administrative distance — because RIP's default administrative distance of 100 is treated as lower than OSPF's 110

questions.explanation_es: OSPF tiene distancia administrativa 110 por defecto, menor que la de RIP (120), así que el router prefiere e instala la ruta OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of these are commonly cited advantages of static routing over dynamic routing protocols? (Select two)

options.A: It consumes very little CPU and memory on the router
options.B: It scales better than dynamic protocols on very large networks
options.C: It requires essentially no extra bandwidth for route advertisements
options.D: It automatically adapts to any topology change

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas estáticas no generan tráfico de actualización entre routers (bajo consumo de ancho de banda) y no requieren cálculos de un algoritmo de ruteo (bajo consumo de CPU/memoria). No se adaptan automáticamente a cambios de topología, y en redes grandes escalan peor que un protocolo dinámico.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of these statements about EIGRP are correct? (Select three)

options.A: It uses Dijkstra's SPF algorithm to calculate paths
options.B: Its default internal administrative distance is 90
options.C: It uses the DUAL algorithm to calculate loop-free paths
options.D: Its default IPv4 multicast address is 224.0.0.10

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP usa el algoritmo DUAL (no SPF, que es de OSPF), su dirección multicast IPv4 por defecto es 224.0.0.10, y su distancia administrativa interna por defecto es 90 (170 es la distancia administrativa externa de EIGRP, no la interna).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why is EIGRP sometimes described as having both distance-vector and link-state characteristics?

options.A: Because it floods the full network topology to every router just like OSPF does
options.B: Because it maintains neighbor and topology tables and reacts quickly to changes via DUAL, behaving like a distance-vector protocol with some link-state-like traits
options.C: Because it only ever exchanges routes with directly connected neighbors, with no additional link-state-like behavior at all
options.D: Because it only calculates hop count, exactly like RIP, with no link-state traits

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP se describe a veces como un protocolo 'híbrido avanzado': funciona fundamentalmente como vector-distancia (solo intercambia rutas con vecinos directos), pero mantiene tablas de vecinos y topología y reacciona rápido a cambios mediante DUAL, características que recuerdan a un protocolo de estado de enlace.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the output of 'show ip route', what does the '>' symbol next to a route typically indicate?

options.A: That the route is pending validation
options.B: That the route was learned via a default route
options.C: That the route is a summarized route
options.D: That the route is currently the best route installed and used for forwarding

questions.explanation_es: El símbolo '>' junto a una ruta en la tabla de ruteo de Cisco indica que esa es la ruta actualmente instalada y utilizada para reenviar tráfico hacia ese destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What does it mean when an EIGRP route enters the 'Active' state in the topology table?

options.A: The route's successor and all feasible successors have failed, and the router is now actively querying neighbors for a new path
options.B: The route is currently being used to forward traffic normally
options.C: The route was just learned and is being validated for the first time — a transient status EIGRP assigns to a newly discovered route while it waits for a hold-down timer to expire
options.D: The route has been manually marked as preferred by the administrator

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta EIGRP entra en estado 'Active' cuando su sucesor y todos sus sucesores factibles fallan, y el router debe enviar consultas (queries) a sus vecinos para encontrar una nueva ruta. Mientras está en ese proceso, la ruta se considera activa (en contraste con 'Passive', su estado normal y estable).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which type of EIGRP packet is primarily responsible for carrying routing information used to build the topology and routing tables?

options.A: Query packets
options.B: Acknowledgment packets
options.C: Hello packets
options.D: Update packets

questions.explanation_es: Los paquetes Update llevan la información de ruteo que EIGRP usa para construir las tablas de topología y de ruteo. Los paquetes Hello sirven para descubrir y mantener vecinos, no para transportar rutas.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In a routing table entry like '10.10.20.0/24 [110/15] via 10.10.1.1', what does the second number (15) represent?

options.A: The administrative distance
options.B: The hop count limit
options.C: The interface index
options.D: The metric

questions.explanation_es: En la notación '[AD/metric]' de Cisco IOS, el primer número (110) es la distancia administrativa y el segundo (15) es la métrica de la ruta para ese protocolo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which command enables real-time debugging of EIGRP packets being sent and received on a Cisco router?

options.A: show eigrp packets
options.B: debug ip eigrp neighbors
options.C: clear eigrp packets
options.D: debug eigrp packets

questions.explanation_es: 'debug eigrp packets' habilita el debug en tiempo real de los paquetes EIGRP (Hello, Update, Query, etc.) enviados y recibidos por el router.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which type of OSPF router connects two or more OSPF areas together?

options.A: ABR (Area Border Router)
options.B: DR (Designated Router)
options.C: BDR (Backup Designated Router)
options.D: ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router)

questions.explanation_es: El ABR (Area Border Router) es el router que tiene interfaces en más de un área OSPF, conectándolas entre sí.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which interface command sets the OSPF hello interval to 20 seconds?

options.A: ospf hello time 20
options.B: ip ospf interval 20
options.C: ip hello-interval ospf 20
options.D: ip ospf hello-interval 20

questions.explanation_es: El comando de interfaz correcto es 'ip ospf hello-interval 20'. Al cambiarlo, normalmente también hay que ajustar el 'dead-interval' para que siga siendo consistente (por defecto 4x el hello).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: If an interface's OSPF priority is set to 0, what effect does this have on DR/BDR election?

options.A: The router is guaranteed to become the BDR on that segment
options.B: The router will never be elected DR or BDR on that segment
options.C: The priority value has no effect on DR/BDR election at all
options.D: The router is guaranteed to become the DR on that segment

questions.explanation_es: Una prioridad OSPF de 0 hace que el router quede excluido de la elección de DR/BDR en ese segmento: nunca será elegido como DR ni como BDR, aunque sigue participando como vecino normal (DROTHER).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: During which state of OSPF neighbor establishment does DR/BDR election take place?

options.A: Exchange
options.B: Full
options.C: 2-Way
options.D: Exstart

questions.explanation_es: La elección de DR/BDR ocurre en el estado 2-Way, una vez que los routers se reconocen mutuamente como vecinos (bidireccionalidad confirmada), antes de pasar al intercambio de bases de datos (Exstart/Exchange).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is OSPF's default administrative distance on a Cisco router?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF tiene una distancia administrativa por defecto de 110 en dispositivos Cisco.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of the following are accurate descriptions of OSPF? (Select three)

options.A: It supports a hierarchical, multi-area design
options.B: It uses Cisco's proprietary DUAL algorithm
options.C: It uses Dijkstra's SPF algorithm to compute the shortest path
options.D: It is a link-state routing protocol

questions.explanation_es: OSPF es un protocolo de estado de enlace que usa el algoritmo de Dijkstra (SPF) y soporta un diseño jerárquico de múltiples áreas. DUAL es de EIGRP, no de OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of these router roles are specific to OSPF terminology? (Select three)

options.A: DR (Designated Router)
options.B: Route Reflector
options.C: BDR (Backup Designated Router)
options.D: ABR (Area Border Router)

questions.explanation_es: ABR, DR y BDR son roles definidos específicamente dentro de OSPF. El Route Reflector es en cambio un concepto de BGP, no de OSPF.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the correct order of BGP peer states from initial connection to a fully established session?

options.A: Active, Connect, Idle, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.B: Idle, Active, Connect, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.C: Connect, Idle, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.D: Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established

questions.explanation_es: El orden correcto de los estados de una sesión BGP es: Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Under 'router bgp 200', which command sets a weight of 150 for neighbor 1.2.1.2?

options.A: set neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150
options.B: match neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150
options.C: neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150
options.D: weight neighbor 1.2.1.2 150

questions.explanation_es: El comando correcto, dentro del modo de configuración 'router bgp 200', es 'neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150'.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which of the following are well-known BGP path attributes? (Select three)

options.A: AS-Path
options.B: Local Preference
options.C: Origin
options.D: Weight

questions.explanation_es: Origin, AS-Path y Local Preference son atributos 'well-known' de BGP (well-known mandatory los dos primeros, well-known discretionary Local Preference). Weight ni siquiera es un atributo BGP estándar: es un valor puramente local de Cisco IOS que nunca se anuncia a otros routers.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which BGP peer state indicates that the session has fully converged and the peers are exchanging routing updates?

options.A: OpenSent
options.B: OpenConfirm
options.C: Established
options.D: 2-Way

questions.explanation_es: El estado 'Established' indica que la sesión BGP convergió completamente y los peers ya están intercambiando actualizaciones de ruteo. '2-Way' no es un estado de BGP, sino de OSPF.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the correct order (highest to lowest priority) of the main steps in Cisco's BGP best-path selection process?

options.A: MED, Origin, AS-Path length, Local Preference, Weight, Locally Originated
options.B: Weight, Local Preference, Locally Originated, AS-Path length, Origin, MED
options.C: AS-Path length, Weight, Local Preference, Origin, MED, Locally Originated
options.D: Local Preference, Weight, AS-Path length, Locally Originated, Origin, MED

questions.explanation_es: El orden (de mayor a menor prioridad) del algoritmo de selección de mejor ruta de BGP en Cisco es: Weight (mayor), Local Preference (mayor), rutas originadas localmente, AS-Path (más corto), Origin (menor), y MED (menor).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which multicast address range is reserved for local-subnet-only traffic (link-local, not forwarded by routers)?
questions.explanation_es: El rango 224.0.0.0 a 224.0.0.255 está reservado para tráfico multicast local al segmento (link-local), como Hellos de protocolos de ruteo; los routers no reenvían ese tráfico fuera del subnet.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which global configuration command enables IGMP snooping on a Cisco switch?

options.A: ip snooping igmp
options.B: igmp snooping start
options.C: igmp snooping enable
options.D: ip igmp snooping

questions.explanation_es: El comando global correcto es 'ip igmp snooping' (en muchos Catalyst viene habilitado por defecto, pero el comando explícito es ese).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the IPv6 multicast address range, identified by its leading hex bits?

options.A: FFFF to FFFF only
options.B: FE80 to FEBF
options.C: FF00 to FFFF
options.D: FEC0 to FEFF

questions.explanation_es: Las direcciones multicast IPv6 comienzan con el prefijo FF00::/8, es decir, el primer byte va de FF00 a FFFF. FE80 corresponde en cambio al rango de direcciones link-local unicast.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: Which command correctly configures extended ACL 120 to permit only ICMP traffic from network 192.168.1.0/24 to host 2.2.2.2?

options.A: access-list 120 deny icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2
options.B: access-list 120 permit icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2
options.C: access-list 120 permit icmp host 2.2.2.2 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255

questions.explanation_es: La sintaxis correcta es 'access-list 120 permit icmp <origen> <wildcard> host <destino>', es decir: 'access-list 120 permit icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2'.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: Which command correctly configures standard ACL 10 to deny all traffic from network 10.10.10.0/24?

options.A: access-list 10 permit 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255

questions.explanation_es: En una ACL estándar la sintaxis es 'access-list <número> deny <red> <wildcard>', usando wildcard mask (no máscara de subred), por lo que sería 'access-list 10 deny 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255'.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python code correctly prompts the user for input and stores it in variable x?

options.A: x = input("Enter your value: ")
options.B: x == input("Enter your value: ")
options.C: input x = "Enter your value: "
options.D: x = ("Enter your value: ")

questions.explanation_es: La forma correcta es 'x = input("Enter your value: ")', que llama a la función input() y asigna el resultado (lo que el usuario escriba) a la variable x.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which line of Python code correctly prints 'Hello World!' to the console?

options.A: print("Hello World!")
options.B: print "Hello World!"
options.C: print(Hello World!)
options.D: echo("Hello World!")

questions.explanation_es: En Python 3, la forma correcta es 'print("Hello World!")', con el texto entre paréntesis y comillas.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python condition correctly checks whether integer variable X is even?
questions.explanation_es: 'if X % 2 == 0:' usa el operador módulo (%) para verificar si el resto de dividir X por 2 es cero, lo cual indica que X es par. '=' es asignación, no comparación, por lo que 'X % 2 = 0' sería un error de sintaxis.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python code correctly assigns the string 'ABC' to variable String1 and then prints it?

options.A: String1 = 'ABC'\nprint(String1)
options.B: String1 == 'ABC'\nprint(String1)
options.C: print(String1)\nString1 = 'ABC'
options.D: String1 = ABC\nprint(String1)

questions.explanation_es: Hay que encerrar el string entre comillas ('ABC', no ABC sin comillas, que Python interpretaría como un nombre de variable), asignarlo con '=', y luego imprimirlo con print(String1).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How many distinct BPDU (Bridge Protocol Data Unit) types does classic 802.1D Spanning Tree define?

options.A: Four, one for each STP port state transition (blocking, listening, learning, forwarding)
options.B: One single BPDU type that carries both configuration and topology-change information in every message, with no separate TCN message ever defined
options.C: Two: the Configuration BPDU used for normal tree-building, and the Topology Change Notification (TCN) BPDU used to signal a topology change
options.D: Three: a hello BPDU, a topology-change BPDU, and a root-election BPDU, each with its own distinct format

questions.explanation_es: 802.1D define dos tipos de BPDU: la Configuration BPDU (usada normalmente para construir y mantener el árbol) y la Topology Change Notification (TCN) BPDU, que un switch envía hacia el root cuando detecta un cambio de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Which attribute is compared first when switches elect the STP root bridge?

options.A: The switch's serial number, since Cisco is sometimes assumed to encode it directly into the bridge ID to guarantee a globally unique tiebreak, when in fact the bridge ID is built from priority plus system MAC address, with serial number playing no role
options.B: The cumulative root path cost each switch has calculated so far, before any bridge ID is even examined
options.C: The bridge priority value encoded in each switch's bridge ID, with the lowest value winning (the system MAC address is used only as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal)
options.D: The per-port priority configured on each switch's lowest-numbered interface

questions.explanation_es: El root bridge se elige comparando primero la prioridad de puente (bridge priority) de cada switch; el valor más bajo gana. Si hay empate en prioridad, se usa la dirección MAC del sistema como desempate (la MAC más baja gana).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Under the original 802.1D short-mode STP cost table, what interface cost is assigned to a 1 Gbps link?

options.A: 100, matching the cost historically assigned to 10 Mbps Ethernet
options.B: 19, the same value used for 100 Mbps links, since short mode does not distinguish speeds above Fast Ethernet
options.D: 1, since short mode uses a linear cost scale of 1 unit per Gbps of link speed

questions.explanation_es: En la tabla de costos original de 802.1D (modo corto, 16 bits), un enlace de 1 Gbps tiene un costo de 4 (10 Mbps=100, 100 Mbps=19, 1 Gbps=4, 10 Gbps=2).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What STP port role do every one of the root bridge's own active ports hold?

options.A: Root port, since the root bridge is the reference point that every root path cost is measured against
options.B: Backup port, reserved in case another switch takes over the root role
options.C: Alternate port, because the root bridge does not forward traffic on any interface by design
options.D: Designated port

questions.explanation_es: El root bridge nunca tiene un puerto raíz (root port) propio, porque el concepto de puerto raíz es 'el puerto más cercano al root bridge' y el root bridge ya es el root. Por eso, todos sus puertos activos son puertos designados (designated ports).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Using 802.1D default timers, how long does a port normally remain in the listening state before moving to learning?

options.A: 20 seconds, matching the default max-age timer
options.B: 2 seconds, matching the default hello timer
options.C: 50 seconds, the sum of the default max-age (20s) and forward delay (15s) timers combined, a total some engineers mistakenly cite for the listening state alone instead of the full non-forwarding window across listening and learning
options.D: 15 seconds, matching the default forward delay timer

questions.explanation_es: Con los temporizadores por defecto, tanto el estado listening como el learning duran 15 segundos cada uno (el valor del forward delay), por lo que un puerto tarda un total de 30 segundos en pasar de blocking a forwarding tras perder su BPDU superior.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What actually happens on downstream switches when they receive a configuration BPDU with the Topology Change (TC) flag set?

options.A: They temporarily shorten their MAC address table aging timer to the forward delay value, so stale entries age out and are flushed much faster than the normal aging period
options.B: They immediately reboot the STP process on every VLAN, forcing a full re-election of the root bridge network-wide, rather than the far lighter-weight response of shortening the MAC aging timer that RSTP and 802.1D actually perform on a topology change
options.C: They ignore the flag entirely unless BPDU Guard is also enabled on the receiving port
options.D: They permanently disable MAC address learning on all trunk ports until an administrator manually re-enables it

questions.explanation_es: Al recibir una BPDU con el flag de Topology Change, los switches reducen temporalmente el tiempo de aging de la tabla MAC al valor del forward delay (normalmente 15 segundos), en vez del aging normal (300 segundos), logrando que las entradas viejas se depuren mucho más rápido tras un cambio de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: RSTP (802.1w) consolidates the classic 802.1D port states into fewer active states. Which pair of 802.1D states no longer exist as distinct named RSTP states? (Choose two.)

options.A: Listening
options.B: Forwarding
options.C: Blocking
options.D: Learning

questions.explanation_es: RSTP fusiona blocking y listening (además del estado disabled) en un único rol llamado 'discarding', dejando efectivamente tres estados operativos: discarding, learning y forwarding, en lugar de los cinco de 802.1D.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Does a large Layer 2 topology running RSTP need to fully converge network-wide before any port can start forwarding traffic?

options.A: Yes, RSTP still requires the entire topology to reach a stable state before any single port transitions to forwarding, identical to 802.1D in this respect, since RSTP is often mistakenly treated as just a faster-timer version of 802.1D rather than a protocol with its own rapid-transition handshake
options.B: Only edge ports can skip convergence, and only if BPDU Guard is also disabled on them
options.C: Only the root bridge's ports can forward before convergence; all non-root switches must always wait
options.D: No — RSTP's proposal/agreement handshake on point-to-point links (and edge ports connected to end hosts) allows individual ports to transition to forwarding rapidly, without waiting for the whole topology to converge

questions.explanation_es: Una de las mejoras clave de RSTP es el mecanismo de proposal/agreement en enlaces punto a punto, que permite que puertos individuales pasen rápidamente a forwarding sin esperar la convergencia de toda la topología, a diferencia de 802.1D.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In what increments can a switch's STP bridge priority be configured?

options.A: In increments of 4096
options.B: In increments of 1, since Cisco IOS allows any arbitrary integer between 0 and 65535
options.C: In increments of 256, matching the extended system ID field width
options.D: In increments of 100, matching the legacy port-cost scale

questions.explanation_es: La prioridad de puente STP se configura en incrementos de 4096 (0, 4096, 8192, ... hasta 61440), porque los 12 bits inferiores del campo de 16 bits están reservados para el extended system ID (el número de VLAN).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: When a switch calculates its root path cost from a received configuration BPDU, whose interface cost gets added into that calculation?

options.A: The cost of the port the BPDU was sent out of on the advertising (upstream) switch
options.B: The cost of the receiving switch's own interface on which the BPDU arrived
options.C: No interface cost is added at all; root path cost is purely a hop count between the local switch and the root bridge
options.D: The average of the sending and receiving interfaces' costs

questions.explanation_es: El switch que envía la BPDU anuncia el costo acumulado SIN incluir el costo de su propio puerto de salida. Es el switch receptor quien suma el costo de SU puerto de entrada (por el que recibió la BPDU) al valor recibido, para calcular su propio root path cost.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: When two ports are tied on root path cost during STP port role selection, which STP port priority value wins the tiebreak?

options.A: The lower numeric port priority value
options.B: Port priority is never used as a tiebreaker; ties are always broken using the port's physical slot/module number only
options.C: Whichever port came up first chronologically, regardless of any configured priority
options.D: The higher numeric port priority value, since STP treats port priority the opposite way it treats bridge priority

questions.explanation_es: Igual que con la prioridad de puente, en STP un valor de prioridad de puerto más bajo es más preferido. Se usa como criterio de desempate cuando dos puertos tienen el mismo costo de camino hacia la raíz.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In Multiple Spanning Tree (MST), a VLAN is directly mapped to which construct?

options.A: A physical switch, since VLAN-to-switch mapping determines MST behavior directly
options.B: An MST instance (MSTI)
options.C: An MST region, since each region is defined as containing exactly one VLAN
options.D: An MST area, borrowing the OSPF-style hierarchical terminology

questions.explanation_es: En MST, las VLANs se asocian directamente a instancias (MSTIs, MST Instances), no a regiones ni a switches. Una región es un grupo de switches con la misma configuración MST; dentro de esa región, muchas VLANs se agrupan en un número reducido de instancias.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is special about MST instance 0, known as the Internal Spanning Tree (IST)?

options.A: It runs on every switch port in the MST region regardless of VLAN membership, and carries the other MST instances' information nested inside its own BPDUs, so only one set of BPDUs needs to be exchanged
options.B: It only carries BPDUs for VLANs that have not been explicitly mapped to another MST instance, acting as a default catch-all rather than as an instance that runs on every port in the region regardless of VLAN mapping
options.C: It only exists in networks with fewer than 16 VLANs; larger environments must renumber it out of instance 0
options.D: It is optional and can be disabled if an administrator only wants to use instances 1-15

questions.explanation_es: La IST (instancia 0) corre en todos los puertos de switch de la región MST, sin importar qué VLANs tengan asociadas, y transporta anidada la información del resto de las MSTIs dentro de sus propias BPDUs, permitiendo que MST anuncie un solo conjunto de BPDUs en vez de uno por instancia.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: For two connected switches to be considered part of the same MST region, what must match between them?

options.A: The configured region name, the configuration revision number, and the VLAN-to-instance mapping table (compared via a digest) — a mismatch in any of these places the switches in different regions
options.B: Only the physical cabling topology; MST region membership is determined by Layer 1 adjacency, not configuration
options.C: The region name and revision number must match, but the VLAN-to-instance mapping table only needs to be compatible rather than identical, since MST is understood to reconcile any differing VLAN assignments automatically once adjacency forms
options.D: Only the priority configured for MST instance 0, since that alone determines the region boundary

questions.explanation_es: La pertenencia a una región MST se determina comparando tres elementos: el nombre de región configurado, el número de revisión, y el mapeo VLAN-a-instancia (comparado mediante un digest/hash). Si alguno de estos difiere entre dos switches conectados, quedan en regiones MST distintas aunque estén físicamente conectados.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What do legacy 802.1D and CST (Common Spanning Tree, as used by 802.1Q) have in common that PVST+ and MST were designed to improve on?

options.A: Both were deprecated by the IEEE before Cisco ever implemented them in IOS
options.B: Both mandate that every switch in the topology run in transparent VTP mode
options.C: Both compute only a single spanning tree topology across the entire network, so per-VLAN load balancing across redundant links isn't possible
options.D: Both require dedicated hardware ASICs not found on typical Cisco Catalyst switches, a hardware dependency that has nothing to do with why per-VLAN load balancing is unavailable under a single shared spanning tree topology

questions.explanation_es: 802.1D clásico y CST calculan una única topología de árbol para toda la red (todas las VLANs comparten el mismo árbol), por lo que no permiten balancear carga por VLAN entre enlaces redundantes. PVST+ (una instancia por VLAN) y MST (varias instancias agrupando VLANs) resuelven esta limitación.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid VTP switch role/mode?

options.A: Proxy
options.B: Transparent
options.C: Off
options.D: Client

questions.explanation_es: Los roles válidos de VTP son Server, Client, Transparent, y (desde VTPv3) Off. 'Proxy' no es un rol de VTP real.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What information does a VTP summary advertisement actually carry?

options.A: Header-level identification information such as the VTP version, domain name, and configuration revision number — the actual per-VLAN details are carried separately in subset advertisements
options.B: Only the MD5 password used to authenticate the VTP domain, with no other fields
options.C: The full list of VLANs that were recently added, deleted, or renamed, encoded directly in the summary advertisement itself
options.D: A complete copy of the switch's running configuration, compressed for transport over the VTP domain

questions.explanation_es: La summary advertisement de VTP transporta información de encabezado (versión de VTP, nombre de dominio, número de revisión de configuración, etc.), pero no el detalle de las VLANs en sí — eso viaja en las subset advertisements que la siguen cuando hay un cambio real.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why can physically relocating an old, previously configured switch into an active VTP domain be dangerous?

options.A: If that switch's stored configuration revision number is higher than the domain's current revision, other switches can accept it as more current and overwrite their VLAN databases with its (possibly outdated) VLAN set — potentially deleting VLANs domain-wide
options.B: It has no effect at all as long as the switch is set to VTP client mode before being reconnected
options.C: The relocated switch always defaults to transparent mode automatically upon reboot, which fully isolates it from any risk
options.D: The relocated switch will refuse to send any VTP updates unless manually configured as a VTP server first

questions.explanation_es: Si el switch reubicado conserva un número de revisión de configuración más alto que el del dominio activo (por ejemplo, de una configuración vieja no reseteada), los demás switches lo aceptan como más reciente y sobrescriben su base de datos de VLANs con la de ese switch, pudiendo borrar VLANs en todo el dominio. Por eso se recomienda resetear la revisión a 0 antes de reconectar un switch.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: If both ends of a link are configured with 'switchport mode dynamic auto', what is the resulting port mode?

options.A: A trunk forms, since DTP treats the combination of two auto ports as a valid negotiation match
options.B: The link becomes a Layer 3 routed port automatically, bypassing DTP entirely
options.C: The link flaps continuously between trunk and access as both switches repeatedly try to negotiate
options.D: The link stays in access mode — neither side initiates DTP negotiation, so no trunk forms

questions.explanation_es: 'Dynamic auto' espera pasivamente a que el otro extremo inicie la negociación DTP. Si ambos extremos están en auto, ninguno toma la iniciativa, así que el enlace permanece como puerto de acceso y nunca se forma un trunk.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which port types can be bundled into an EtherChannel?

options.A: Only loopback and tunnel interfaces, since EtherChannel was designed specifically for logical interface types
options.B: Only trunk ports; EtherChannel requires 802.1Q tagging on every member link
options.C: Only access ports; trunk and routed ports cannot participate in any EtherChannel bundle
options.D: Access, trunk, and routed (Layer 3) ports

questions.explanation_es: Un EtherChannel puede agrupar puertos de acceso, puertos trunk, o puertos enrutados de Capa 3 (formando un port-channel L3). Las interfaces loopback no son elegibles para EtherChannel.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Beyond the obvious bandwidth increase, what STP-related benefit does bundling multiple physical links into a single EtherChannel provide?

options.A: STP sees the whole bundle as a single logical link, so an individual member link flapping up/down doesn't trigger a full STP topology change/recalculation the way a flapping standalone link would
options.B: It doubles the default STP port cost for the logical interface compared to any single member link
options.C: It forces the bundle to always become the STP root port on every VLAN, regardless of actual path cost
options.D: It disables STP entirely on the bundled links, since STP is assumed to be unnecessary once redundancy exists inside the bundle

questions.explanation_es: Al presentarse ante STP como una única interfaz lógica, la caída o recuperación de un enlace miembro individual dentro del bundle no dispara un topology change de STP en toda la red, a diferencia de lo que ocurriría si ese mismo enlace estuviera solo (sin EtherChannel). Esto reduce la inestabilidad de la topología además de sumar ancho de banda.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: In Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's 'Know Your Network' request path, which of the following is NOT one of its subdomains?

options.A: Sites
options.B: Devices
options.C: Environment
options.D: Clients

questions.explanation_es: Los subdominios del 'Know Your Network' request path de DNA/Catalyst Center incluyen Devices, Clients y Sites, entre otros. 'Environment' no es uno de esos subdominios.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to submit a username and password when authenticating to the Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center or vManage REST API?

options.A: OPTIONS, to first discover which authentication schemes the server accepts
options.B: GET, with the credentials passed as URL query parameters
options.C: PUT, since authenticating is treated as replacing the prior session resource
options.D: POST

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación contra la API de DNA/Catalyst Center o vManage se realiza enviando el usuario y contraseña mediante una solicitud POST, que retorna un token que se usa en las solicitudes posteriores.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector publishes an event when an administrator manually executes a policy using the 'event manager run' CLI command?

options.A: The counter event detector, which fires once an internal invocation counter increments
options.B: The CLI event detector, since it is the general-purpose detector for anything typed at the CLI
options.C: The syslog event detector, since manually invoking a policy is logged as a syslog message first
options.D: The none event detector

questions.explanation_es: El detector de eventos 'none' es el que se dispara cuando un administrador ejecuta manualmente una política con el comando 'event manager run', en vez de que la política se dispare por un evento real del sistema.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which command lets you observe, in real time, the CLI actions an EEM applet is executing while it runs?

options.A: show event manager detector all
options.B: event manager run applet-name
options.C: show event manager policy active
options.D: debug event manager action cli

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'debug event manager action cli' permite observar en tiempo real las acciones de CLI que un applet EEM va ejecutando mientras corre, útil para depurar un applet que no se comporta como se espera.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: How does an administrator manually trigger an already-configured EEM applet from the CLI, outside of its normal event trigger?

options.A: event manager run applet-name
options.B: debug event manager action cli applet-name
options.C: show event manager policy registered applet-name
options.D: event manager apply applet-name

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'event manager run applet-name' ejecuta manualmente un applet EEM ya configurado, sin esperar a que ocurra su evento disparador normal — útil para probarlo bajo demanda.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Puppet's three high-level architectural components?

options.A: Puppet target
options.B: Puppet master
options.C: Puppet agent
options.D: Puppet database

questions.explanation_es: Los tres componentes de alto nivel de Puppet son el master, el agent y la database. 'Puppet target' no es un componente real de la arquitectura de Puppet.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: In Chef, what does a 'cookbook' represent, in relation to a 'recipe'?

options.A: A cookbook is a single low-level instruction, while a recipe is the larger structure that groups many cookbooks together
options.B: A cookbook is the full scenario definition, bundling everything (recipes, templates, files, attributes) needed to support that scenario — a recipe is one of the smaller units inside it
options.C: A cookbook only exists on the Chef server and has no equivalent concept on the managed node itself
options.D: A cookbook is the packaged unit distributed and versioned through a Chef supermarket or server, while a recipe refers only to the human-readable documentation describing what that cookbook does, rather than to any executable resource definitions

questions.explanation_es: Un cookbook en Chef define un escenario completo y agrupa todo lo necesario para soportarlo (recipes, templates, archivos, atributos); una recipe es una unidad más pequeña dentro de ese cookbook, con instrucciones de configuración específicas.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Puppet and Chef both build their configuration-management tooling on which programming language?

options.A: Java, matching the JVM-based tooling common in enterprise configuration management
options.B: Python, the same language Ansible is built on
options.C: Go, chosen specifically for its concurrency model when managing many nodes in parallel
options.D: Ruby

questions.explanation_es: Tanto Puppet como Chef están construidos sobre Ruby (sus DSLs de manifests/recipes y el propio motor son Ruby), a diferencia de Ansible, que está escrito en Python.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What file format do Ansible playbooks use to describe plays and tasks?

options.A: JSON, matching the format most REST APIs Ansible modules call also use natively
options.B: YAML
options.C: A Ansible-specific binary format compiled ahead of time, unlike Puppet manifests or Chef recipes which are plain text
options.D: XML, since it needs strict schema validation for network device modules

questions.explanation_es: Los playbooks de Ansible se escriben en YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language), un formato más simple de leer y escribir que XML, e incluyen una o más 'plays', cada una compuesta de tareas.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: In HSRP, if two routers end up with the same configured priority, which additional attribute breaks the tie to elect the active router?

options.A: Neither router becomes active until an administrator manually breaks the tie by adjusting priority
options.B: The router that has been up the longest (highest uptime) always wins, regardless of IP addressing
options.C: The router with the lowest configured interface bandwidth wins, since HSRP favors conserving faster links for user traffic
options.D: The router with the higher primary IP address on the HSRP interface wins

questions.explanation_es: Cuando dos routers HSRP tienen la misma prioridad configurada, el desempate se resuelve comparando la dirección IP primaria de la interfaz HSRP: el router con la IP más alta gana la elección como router activo.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is the distinction between Cisco Cloud OnRamp for SaaS and Cloud OnRamp for IaaS?

options.A: OnRamp for SaaS chooses the optimal network path for a given SaaS application's traffic; OnRamp for IaaS automatically deploys WAN Edge router instances in the public cloud to join the SD-WAN overlay
options.B: OnRamp for SaaS and OnRamp for IaaS both function by deploying WAN Edge router instances directly inside the public cloud provider, differing mainly in which cloud marketplace listing each one is published and licensed through
options.C: OnRamp for SaaS and OnRamp for IaaS both only apply to on-premises data center connectivity and have no relationship to any public cloud provider
options.D: OnRamp for SaaS automatically deploys WAN Edge router instances inside the public cloud provider; OnRamp for IaaS instead chooses the best path for SaaS application traffic

questions.explanation_es: Cloud OnRamp for SaaS elige el mejor camino de red para el tráfico de una aplicación SaaS específica; Cloud OnRamp for IaaS, en cambio, despliega automáticamente instancias de WAN Edge router dentro de la nube pública para que pasen a formar parte del overlay SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Can a Cisco SD-WAN WAN Edge router be deployed as something other than a dedicated physical appliance?

options.A: Yes — it can also be deployed as a software-based virtual router, hosted in a private cloud (e.g., VMware ESXi, KVM) or a public cloud (e.g., AWS, Azure)
options.B: Yes, but only as a container running directly inside vManage itself, sharing vManage's own compute resources rather than running as an independent router instance
options.C: No, a WAN Edge router must always be a dedicated physical hardware appliance; software-based deployment is not supported by the SD-WAN architecture
options.D: Yes, but only when paired with a physical vSmart controller located at the same site, since virtual WAN Edge routers cannot reach a cloud-hosted vSmart

questions.explanation_es: Un WAN Edge router puede ser un appliance físico o un router basado en software (virtual), pudiendo alojarse en una nube privada (VMware ESXi, KVM) o en una nube pública (AWS, Azure), sin requisito de coubicación física con el resto de los controladores.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Of the four SD-WAN planes of operation (control, data, orchestration, management), which one is responsible for the automatic onboarding of WAN Edge routers into the SD-WAN overlay fabric?

options.A: Orchestration plane
options.B: Data plane
options.C: Management plane
options.D: Control plane

questions.explanation_es: El plano de orquestación (implementado por vBond) es el responsable de la incorporación automática ('onboarding') de los routers WAN Edge al fabric overlay de SD-WAN, autenticándolos y ayudándolos a descubrir a los demás controladores.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In the four SD-Access operational planes (control, data, policy, management), which plane does VXLAN encapsulation belong to?

options.A: Data plane
options.B: Policy plane, since the VXLAN header's reserved bits carry the SGT used for segmentation
options.C: Control plane, since VXLAN headers also carry the LISP mapping information used for control-plane lookups
options.D: Management plane, since Cisco DNA Center generates the VXLAN configuration pushed to fabric nodes

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN es una técnica de encapsulamiento MAC-in-IP que efectivamente mueve los paquetes de datos a través del fabric — corresponde al data plane de SD-Access. El control plane usa LISP, el policy plane usa TrustSec (SGT), y el management plane lo provee Cisco DNA Center.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In SD-Access, assigning a Security Group Tag (SGT) to a packet as it enters the fabric is a function of which operational plane?

options.A: Policy plane
options.B: Control plane
options.C: Management plane
options.D: Data plane

questions.explanation_es: La asignación de un SGT a un paquete en su punto de ingreso al fabric es una función del policy plane, implementado con Cisco TrustSec — se usa luego para aplicar políticas (QoS, ACLs, segmentación) basadas en el SGT en lugar de direcciones de red.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In an SD-Access fabric, which fabric role does a fabric-mode access point directly connect to?

options.A: The control plane node, so it can register endpoints directly into the host-tracking database itself
options.B: The border node, since APs need direct reachability to the fabric's external connections
options.C: The intermediate node, bypassing the edge layer entirely to reduce hop count for wireless traffic
options.D: The fabric edge node

questions.explanation_es: Un access point en modo fabric debe conectarse directamente al switch de fabric edge node del sitio, que es quien maneja el registro del endpoint y su tráfico dentro del fabric — no se conecta directamente a un border node, control plane node, ni intermediate node.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which type of network delay specifically accounts for the time a router or switch takes to move a packet from an input interface into the output queue of the outbound interface?

options.A: Processing delay
options.B: Queuing delay, the time a packet waits inside the output queue before being transmitted
options.C: Propagation delay, the time for a signal to physically travel across the transmission medium
options.D: Serialization delay, the time to clock all the bits of a frame onto the physical link

questions.explanation_es: El 'processing delay' es el tiempo que le toma a un router o switch tomar un paquete desde la interfaz de entrada y colocarlo en la cola de salida de la interfaz de salida — distinto del queuing delay (tiempo de espera dentro de esa cola), la serialización (tiempo de clockear los bits al medio), o la propagación (tiempo de viaje de la señal por el medio).

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Type 2 hypervisors (such as VMware Fusion or VMware Workstation) are typically deployed in which kind of environment?

options.A: Production data center environments hosting business-critical VMs
options.B: Test/development environments
options.C: Cloud service provider environments offering IaaS to external customers
options.D: Large-scale service provider multi-tenant environments

questions.explanation_es: Los hypervisors tipo 2 (que corren sobre un sistema operativo host, como VMware Fusion o Workstation) se usan típicamente en entornos de prueba/desarrollo, a diferencia de los tipo 1 (bare-metal, como ESXi), que son los usados en producción.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is the primary benefit of achieving a higher server consolidation ratio (more VMs per physical host)?

options.A: Higher return on investment (ROI), since fewer physical hosts are needed to run the same overall workload
options.B: It allows each individual VM to be provisioned with unlimited vCPUs regardless of the host's physical core count
options.C: Higher power consumption per rack, which is treated as inherently desirable regardless of cost
options.D: It reduces the licensing cost of the hypervisor software itself, since most hypervisor vendors charge per physical host rather than per VM, independent of any actual hardware consolidation benefit achieved

questions.explanation_es: Un mayor ratio de consolidación (más VMs por host físico) mejora el retorno de la inversión (ROI), ya que se necesitan menos servidores físicos para correr la misma carga de trabajo total, reduciendo gasto de capital y espacio de datacenter.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid way to manage a VMware ESXi host or vCenter Server environment?

options.A: vCenter Server (a centralized management server for multiple ESXi hosts)
options.B: Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) client
options.C: The VMware Host Client (an HTML5-based client for managing a single ESXi host directly)
options.D: The vSphere HTML5 Web Client

questions.explanation_es: El cliente RDP de Microsoft no es un método de administración de un entorno VMware ESXi/vCenter. Se usa el VMware Host Client (para un solo host) o vCenter Server con sus distintos clientes web (para administración centralizada de múltiples hosts).

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: How does the Cisco Nexus 1000VE virtual switch improve on its predecessor, the Nexus 1000V?

options.A: It removes support for VMware vSphere environments entirely, targeting only KVM and Hyper-V instead
options.B: It can only be deployed with Open vSwitch as its underlying data plane, unlike the original Nexus 1000V which ran independently
options.C: It no longer depends on in-kernel hypervisor platform APIs (such as VMware's own APIs), unlike the original Nexus 1000V
options.D: It drops NX-OS CLI support entirely in favor of a GUI-only management model

questions.explanation_es: El Nexus 1000VE es la evolución del Nexus 1000V, y su mejora clave es que ya no depende de las APIs internas del hipervisor (como las APIs propias de VMware) para operar, a diferencia de su predecesor.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Which Cisco virtual switch is specifically used to provide switching and policy enforcement within a Cisco ACI environment?

options.A: vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS)
options.B: Cisco Nexus 1000V
options.C: Open vSwitch
options.D: Cisco ACI Virtual Edge

questions.explanation_es: Cisco ACI Virtual Edge es el virtual switch hypervisor-agnostic diseñado específicamente para manejar el switching y la aplicación de políticas dentro de un entorno Cisco ACI, a diferencia del Nexus 1000V (NX-OS genérico), Open vSwitch (multiplataforma general) o el vDS de VMware (nativo de vSphere, sin integración ACI).

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Is Cisco NFV (Network Functions Virtualization) infrastructure restricted to specialized, vendor-proprietary hardware?

options.A: Yes, NFV strictly requires Cisco-proprietary ASICs and cannot run on generic hardware
options.B: No, NFV infrastructure can be deployed on any general-purpose x86 platform, and can mix virtual and physical, Cisco and third-party devices and network services
options.C: No, but only ARM-based server platforms are supported, not x86
options.D: Yes, NFV requires SR-IOV-capable network interface cards in every host to achieve line-rate packet forwarding, since a purely software-based virtual switch data path is not considered viable for production NFV deployments

questions.explanation_es: La infraestructura NFV puede desplegarse sobre cualquier plataforma x86 de propósito general, permitiendo una mezcla de dispositivos virtuales y físicos, tanto de Cisco como de terceros, dentro del mismo entorno de servicios de red.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What distinguishes Cisco FlexVPN from a single specific VPN topology like DMVPN or a site-to-site VPN?

options.A: FlexVPN replaces IPsec entirely with a proprietary Cisco encryption scheme incompatible with standard IKE
options.B: FlexVPN is a unified solution/framework that simplifies deploying multiple different VPN types (site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, remote access) using a common IKEv2-based configuration model
options.C: FlexVPN is strictly limited to remote-access VPNs and cannot be used for any site-to-site topology
options.D: FlexVPN only operates over GRE tunnels and has no direct IPsec-only mode

questions.explanation_es: Cisco FlexVPN es un framework unificado, basado en IKEv2, que simplifica el despliegue de distintos tipos de VPN (site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, acceso remoto) bajo un mismo modelo de configuración, en vez de requerir enfoques separados para cada topología.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which IKE version introduced native support for NAT traversal (NAT-T)?

options.A: NAT-T is unrelated to IKE and is instead a function of ESP alone, independent of which IKE version negotiates the security association
options.B: IKEv1, with IKEv2 later dropping the feature for security reasons
options.C: Neither version supports NAT-T; it is implemented entirely outside of IKE
options.D: IKEv2

questions.explanation_es: El soporte de NAT traversal (NAT-T) fue incorporado en IKEv2, facilitando el establecimiento de túneles IPsec/IKE cuando uno de los extremos está detrás de un dispositivo NAT.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: What command activates Guest Shell so a Python interpreter can run directly on a Cisco IOS XE platform?

options.A: iox enable
options.B: guestshell run
options.C: guestshell run python
options.D: guestshell enable

questions.explanation_es: Guest Shell se activa con el comando 'guestshell enable', habilitando un contenedor Linux en la plataforma IOS XE donde se puede correr un intérprete de Python, entre otras herramientas.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: What does 'native' or 'onboard' Python refer to, in the context of Cisco switching platforms?

options.A: A Python interpreter that only understands Cisco-proprietary syntax extensions, incompatible with standard Python code
options.B: Python scripts that must always run from an external management server, never on the device itself
options.C: Python installed natively on the switching platform itself (e.g., a Cisco Catalyst 9300), rather than run through a separate container or external host
options.D: A cloud-hosted Python runtime that Cisco DNA Center exposes on the administrator's behalf

questions.explanation_es: 'Native' u 'onboard' Python se refiere a tener Python instalado directamente en la plataforma de switching (por ejemplo, un Catalyst 9300), en vez de depender de un contenedor separado (como Guest Shell) o de un host externo.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: When handling exceptions in Python with a try/except/else block, when does the code inside the 'else' clause execute?

options.A: Every single time, unconditionally, regardless of whether an exception occurred or not, exactly like code placed after the whole try/except block
options.B: Only when an exception was raised and successfully caught by the 'except' clause
options.C: Never — 'else' is not a valid keyword in Python's exception-handling syntax
options.D: Only when no exception was raised in the 'try' block

questions.explanation_es: El bloque 'else' en una construcción try/except se ejecuta únicamente cuando el bloque 'try' terminó sin lanzar ninguna excepción — es decir, cuando todo salió bien y no se entró a ningún 'except'.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which three protocols make up the model-driven programmability stack commonly referenced for network automation?

options.A: BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP
options.B: SNMP, Syslog, and NTP
options.C: Telnet, SSH, and HTTP
options.D: NETCONF, RESTCONF, and gRPC

questions.explanation_es: El stack de programabilidad basado en modelos referenciado habitualmente está compuesto por NETCONF, RESTCONF y gRPC — los tres protocolos de transporte/gestión usados junto con modelos de datos (como YANG) para configurar y operar dispositivos de forma programática.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What does the first line of a well-formed XML document typically indicate?

options.A: The first child element of the document, since XML has no concept of a distinct declaration line at all
options.B: The root element's name, which must always appear as the literal first line before any other content
options.C: The XML declaration, specifying the XML version and the character encoding used (e.g., version 1.0, ISO-8859-1)
options.D: A comment block documenting the schema author, required by the XML 1.0 specification

questions.explanation_es: La primera línea de un documento XML bien formado es la declaración XML, que especifica la versión de XML (por ejemplo 1.0) y la codificación de caracteres usada (por ejemplo ISO-8859-1), antes de que aparezca el elemento raíz.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: In a JSON object, what is the distinct role of the comma character, as opposed to the colon character?

options.A: The comma is only used inside JSON arrays and never appears inside a JSON object at all
options.B: Comma and colon are fully interchangeable in JSON syntax, and a parser accepts either one in either position
options.C: The comma separates one key/value pair from the next; the colon separates a key from its own value within a pair
options.D: The comma separates each key from its own value within a single pair; the colon separates one complete key/value pair from the next

questions.explanation_es: En JSON, la coma separa un par clave/valor del siguiente dentro de un objeto; los dos puntos (colon) separan la clave de su propio valor dentro de un mismo par. Omitir una coma entre pares es un error de sintaxis común.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Why is SNMP generally considered a poor fit as a 'data model' for modern network programmability, motivating the move toward YANG-based models instead?

options.A: SNMP does not distinguish between configuration data and operational (state) data, unlike YANG-based models which model them separately and explicitly
options.B: SNMP cannot run over UDP, requiring a costly protocol translation layer for every request
options.C: SNMP represents its managed objects strictly as flat, unstructured scalar values with no hierarchical organization at all, unlike the hierarchical, tree-structured data models that YANG defines
options.D: SNMP requires a dedicated hardware appliance per managed device, unlike YANG-based management

questions.explanation_es: Una limitación clave de SNMP frente a los modelos basados en YANG es que no distingue entre datos de configuración y datos operativos/de estado; los modelos YANG modelan ambos tipos de datos de forma separada y explícita, lo cual es una de las motivaciones para adoptar NETCONF/YANG en vez de depender solo de SNMP.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid SNMPv3 security level?

options.A: privNoAuth
options.B: authPriv
options.C: authNoPriv
options.D: noAuthNoPriv

questions.explanation_es: Los niveles de seguridad válidos de SNMPv3 son noAuthNoPriv (sin autenticación ni cifrado), authNoPriv (con autenticación, sin cifrado) y authPriv (con autenticación y cifrado). 'privNoAuth' no es un nivel real — el cifrado (priv) en SNMPv3 siempre requiere autenticación.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: In Cisco IOS traceroute output, what does an 'A' character next to a hop indicate?

options.A: The probe timed out waiting for a reply from that hop
options.B: The destination network is unreachable from that hop
options.C: The hop is administratively prohibited from responding, typically because an ACL is filtering the probe
options.D: The hop successfully forwarded the probe with no issues at all

questions.explanation_es: En la salida de traceroute de Cisco IOS, el carácter 'A' indica que el salto está administrativamente prohibido de responder, típicamente porque una ACL está filtrando el paquete de prueba.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What advantage does the SNMP 'Get Bulk' operation offer over repeatedly issuing 'Get Next'?

options.A: Get Bulk retrieves a large amount of object variable data in a single request/response exchange, instead of requiring many repeated Get Next round-trips
options.B: Get Bulk can only retrieve a single specific object, making it more limited than Get Next
options.C: Get Bulk works by internally issuing a sequence of Get Next requests in the background and returning their combined results as a single response, so its round-trip savings depend on the agent's own implementation rather than on the protocol itself
options.D: Get Bulk retrieves values only for scalar objects and cannot walk a table's repeating rows the way repeated Get Next requests can, limiting its usefulness for retrieving tabular MIB data

questions.explanation_es: La operación 'Get Bulk' de SNMP permite recuperar una gran cantidad de variables de objeto en un solo intercambio de solicitud/respuesta, evitando tener que hacer muchas rondas repetidas de 'Get Next' para recorrer la misma cantidad de datos.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's four main dashboard sections aligned to IT workflow?

options.A: Provision
options.B: Automation
options.C: Assurance
options.D: Design

questions.explanation_es: Las cuatro secciones principales del dashboard de DNA/Catalyst Center son Design, Policy, Provision y Assurance. 'Automation' no es una de esas cuatro secciones (aunque muchas de ellas habilitan tareas de automatización).

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: In Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's Assurance section, what does the Device 360 / Client 360 view specifically provide?

options.A: The ability to push a new configuration template directly to the selected device or client
options.B: Historical topology, throughput, and latency information for a specific device or client across different time windows and applications
options.C: Machine-learning-driven context-aware baselining that models the relationship between metrics as network conditions change
options.D: A list of every ACL currently applied network-wide, unrelated to any single device

questions.explanation_es: La vista Device 360 / Client 360 de Catalyst Center Assurance muestra información histórica de topología, throughput y latencia para un dispositivo o cliente específico, a través de distintas ventanas de tiempo y aplicaciones — a diferencia del baselining por machine learning, que es otra capacidad distinta dentro de Assurance.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of the following routing protocols is classified as an Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) rather than an IGP?

options.A: EIGRP
options.B: BGP
options.C: IS-IS
options.D: OSPF

questions.explanation_es: BGP es el único protocolo de la lista clasificado como EGP, ya que se usa para enrutar entre sistemas autónomos distintos; OSPF, EIGRP e IS-IS son IGPs que operan dentro de un mismo sistema autónomo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which three of the following routing protocols are classified as Interior Gateway Protocols (IGPs)? (Choose three.)

options.A: OSPF
options.B: RIPv2
options.C: BGP
options.D: EIGRP

questions.explanation_es: RIPv2, EIGRP y OSPF operan dentro de un mismo sistema autónomo y por eso se clasifican como IGPs; BGP, en cambio, es un protocolo de puerta de enlace exterior (EGP) usado entre sistemas autónomos distintos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A path-vector routing protocol such as BGP selects the best loop-free path primarily by evaluating which of the following?

options.A: Interface cost
options.B: Hop count
options.C: Total accumulated delay
options.D: Path attributes (such as AS_Path)

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de vector de ruta, como BGP, no usan métricas tradicionales de distancia; en su lugar evalúan atributos de ruta como el AS_Path para determinar el mejor camino libre de bucles.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A classic distance-vector routing protocol determines the best loop-free path mainly by comparing which metric?

options.A: Hop count
options.B: AS path length
options.C: Combined bandwidth and delay
options.D: Interface cost

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de vector de distancia clásicos, como RIP, seleccionan la mejor ruta basándose principalmente en el número de saltos hasta el destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A link-state routing protocol such as OSPF determines the best loop-free path mainly by using which value?

options.A: Hop count
options.B: AS path attributes
options.C: Interface cost (link metric)
options.D: Administrative distance

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de estado de enlace, como OSPF, calculan la mejor ruta ejecutando el algoritmo SPF sobre el costo (métrica) de cada enlace, no sobre el número de saltos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which IP protocol number does EIGRP use to identify its packets at Layer 3?
questions.explanation_es: EIGRP utiliza el número de protocolo IP 88, mientras que OSPF usa el 89.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How many distinct packet types does EIGRP use for communication between routers?

options.A: Three
options.B: Six
options.C: Four
options.D: Five

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP define cinco tipos de paquetes: hello, update, query, reply y ack.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In EIGRP terminology, what is the successor for a given destination network?

options.A: A backup route that satisfies the feasibility condition
options.B: The router responsible for maintaining adjacencies on a broadcast segment
options.C: Any neighbor that has advertised the destination prefix, regardless of metric
options.D: The next-hop router associated with the lowest-metric (feasible distance) path to that destination

questions.explanation_es: El sucesor es el router del siguiente salto que se usa para reenviar tráfico porque ofrece la ruta con la distancia factible (FD) más baja hacia el destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which three of the following are pieces of information stored in an EIGRP topology table entry for a prefix? (Choose three.)

options.A: The total path delay reported for the route
options.B: The destination network prefix
options.C: The list of neighbors that advertised that prefix
options.D: The maximum bandwidth available along the path

questions.explanation_es: La tabla de topología de EIGRP guarda el prefijo de destino, el retraso total y los vecinos que anunciaron esa ruta; en realidad se registra el ancho de banda mínimo del trayecto, no el máximo, así que esa opción es incorrecta.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which two of the following destination addresses does EIGRP use, when possible, to communicate with neighbors? (Choose two.)

options.A: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:05
options.B: IP multicast address 224.0.0.10
options.C: IP multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.D: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:0A

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP usa la dirección multicast 224.0.0.10 y su correspondiente dirección MAC multicast 01:00:5E:00:00:0A; 224.0.0.5 y su MAC asociada pertenecen a OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which interface-level value can be tuned to influence EIGRP's path selection without affecting the metric calculations of other protocols such as OSPF?

options.A: Interface MTU
options.B: Interface bandwidth
options.C: Interface delay
options.D: Interface priority

questions.explanation_es: El retraso de interfaz (delay) es un valor propio del cálculo de métrica de EIGRP; modificarlo no afecta a OSPF, mientras que cambiar el ancho de banda de la interfaz sí impactaría a ambos protocolos, ya que OSPF también usa el ancho de banda para su costo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the classic EIGRP metric formula, the bandwidth component is scaled relative to a reference link speed of how much?

options.A: 40 Gbps
options.B: 10 Gbps
options.C: 100 Mbps
options.D: 1 Gbps

questions.explanation_es: La fórmula clásica de EIGRP escala el ancho de banda mínimo del trayecto respecto a un enlace de referencia de 10 Gbps (10^7 kbps).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the default EIGRP hello interval on high-speed interfaces (above T1 speed)?

options.A: 1 second
options.B: 5 seconds
options.C: 30 seconds
options.D: 10 seconds

questions.explanation_es: En interfaces de alta velocidad, EIGRP envía paquetes hello cada 5 segundos por defecto.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When an EIGRP route has a stable path with no ongoing recomputation, what state is that route considered to be in?

options.A: Held-down
options.B: Dead
options.C: Passive
options.D: Active

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta EIGRP estable se encuentra en estado pasivo (P); pasa a estado activo (A) solo cuando DUAL necesita recalcular el camino tras perder el sucesor.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When an EIGRP router loses its successor route and has no feasible successor available, how does it signal that a path recomputation is needed?

options.A: It sends an update packet with a topology-change notification flag.
options.B: It marks the route as unreachable and sends query packets to its neighbors asking for alternate paths.
options.C: It sends a withdrawal message instructing neighbors to purge the route from their topology tables.
options.D: It sends an update packet advertising the route with a metric of zero.

questions.explanation_es: Sin sucesor factible, el router marca la ruta con métrica infinita (inalcanzable), pasa a estado activo y envía paquetes query a sus vecinos para buscar un camino alternativo, como parte del algoritmo DUAL.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When you manually configure EIGRP route summarization on a specific interface, out of which interfaces is the resulting summary route advertised?

options.A: Only toward the neighbor holding the feasible successor
options.B: Out every interface belonging to the same VRF
options.C: Out every EIGRP-enabled interface on the router
options.D: Only out the interface where the summarization command was applied

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización manual de EIGRP se aplica por interfaz; el resumen solo se anuncia por la interfaz donde se configuró, no automáticamente por todas las interfaces del router.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which two of the following routing protocols rely on a link-state (SPF-based) algorithm to compute the best path? (Choose two.)

options.A: IS-IS
options.B: EIGRP
options.C: OSPF
options.D: RIP

questions.explanation_es: OSPF e IS-IS son protocolos de estado de enlace que ejecutan el algoritmo SPF de Dijkstra; RIP es vector de distancia y EIGRP es un vector de distancia avanzado (DUAL).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What IP protocol number is carried in the header of EIGRP packets?
questions.explanation_es: EIGRP se identifica con el número de protocolo IP 88.
