questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: On a high-speed EIGRP-enabled interface, how often does the router send hello packets by default?

options.A: Every 15 seconds
options.B: Every 5 seconds
options.C: Every 3 seconds
options.D: Every 10 seconds

questions.explanation_es: El temporizador hello por defecto de EIGRP en interfaces de alta velocidad es de 5 segundos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of the following is considered a pure distance-vector routing protocol, without link-state or hybrid characteristics?

options.A: RIP
options.B: IS-IS
options.C: EIGRP
options.D: OSPF

questions.explanation_es: RIP es un protocolo de vector de distancia puro (algoritmo Bellman-Ford); EIGRP es un vector de distancia avanzado con rasgos de estado de enlace, y OSPF/IS-IS son protocolos de estado de enlace.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the default EIGRP hello interval on slower interfaces, such as those below T1 speed?

options.A: 60 seconds
options.B: 10 seconds
options.C: 15 seconds
options.D: 180 seconds

questions.explanation_es: En interfaces lentas (por debajo de T1), EIGRP usa un temporizador hello por defecto de 60 segundos, en lugar de los 5 segundos usados en interfaces rápidas.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Besides per-route metric details, what does the EIGRP topology table contain overall?

options.A: Every network prefix advertised within the EIGRP autonomous system, along with the neighbors that advertised each one
options.B: The complete OSPF link-state database learned via redistribution
options.C: Only the routes currently installed in the IP routing table (RIB)
options.D: A historical audit log of every past successor change

questions.explanation_es: La tabla de topología de EIGRP contiene todos los prefijos anunciados dentro del sistema autónomo EIGRP, junto con los vecinos que los anunciaron, no solo las rutas activas instaladas en la RIB.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What IP protocol number does OSPF use in its packet header?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF utiliza el número de protocolo IP 89; EIGRP usa el 88.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many distinct OSPF packet types are used for inter-router communication?

options.A: Four
options.B: Five
options.C: Three
options.D: Six

questions.explanation_es: OSPF define cinco tipos de paquetes: hello, DBD, LSR, LSU y LSAck.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which two of the following destination addresses does OSPF use, when possible, for its packets? (Choose two.)

options.A: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:0A
options.B: IP multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.C: IP multicast address 224.0.0.10
options.D: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:05

questions.explanation_es: OSPF usa la dirección multicast AllSPFRouters 224.0.0.5 y su MAC multicast asociada 01:00:5E:00:00:05; 224.0.0.10 y su MAC son de EIGRP.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which statement about enabling OSPF on a router interface is accurate?

options.A: A wildcard mask can only be applied at the interface level, not within the OSPF process.
options.B: OSPF activates itself automatically on every interface with an IP address once the process starts.
options.C: OSPF can be enabled either through the network command under the process or through an interface-level command.
options.D: OSPF can only be enabled through the network command under the OSPF process.

questions.explanation_es: OSPF admite dos métodos de habilitación: el comando network bajo el proceso, o el comando de interfaz ip ospf process-id area area-id; no está limitado a un único método.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of the following must match between two directly connected routers for an OSPF neighbor adjacency to form?

options.A: The router ID configured on each router
options.B: The OSPF process number combined with the area name
options.C: The hello and dead interval timers configured on the shared interfaces
options.D: The OSPF process ID configured on each router

questions.explanation_es: El process ID de OSPF es de significado local y no necesita coincidir entre routers; en cambio, los temporizadores hello y dead sí deben coincidir para que la adyacencia se establezca correctamente.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When a default route is injected into OSPF using the default-information originate command, how does it typically appear in the routing table of other OSPF routers?

options.A: As an OSPF inter-area route (O IA)
options.B: As an OSPF intra-area route (O)
options.C: As an OSPF external route (O*E1 or O*E2)
options.D: As a directly connected route

questions.explanation_es: Un default route inyectado con default-information originate se anuncia como una ruta externa de OSPF (tipo E1 o E2), no como una ruta intra-área ni inter-área.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On an OSPF point-to-point network type, such as a serial link between two routers, what happens regarding the designated router (DR) role?

options.A: No DR or BDR election occurs on that network type.
options.B: The router with the highest interface IP address becomes the DR.
options.C: The router with the highest router ID becomes the DR.
options.D: Both routers alternate holding the DR role periodically.

questions.explanation_es: En redes punto a punto no existe el concepto de DR/BDR, ya que solo hay dos routers y una adyacencia completa se forma directamente entre ellos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: By default, OSPF calculates an interface's cost using a reference bandwidth of how much?

options.A: 1 Gbps
options.B: 100 Mbps
options.C: 10 Gbps
options.D: 40 Gbps

questions.explanation_es: El ancho de banda de referencia por defecto de OSPF es 100 Mbps, lo cual hace que interfaces de mayor velocidad compartan el mismo costo mínimo de 1 si no se ajusta el valor de referencia.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which interface command prevents a router from ever being elected as the designated router (DR) on that segment?

options.A: ip ospf priority 0
options.B: ip ospf priority 255
options.C: ip ospf network point-to-point
options.D: passive-interface (configured under the OSPF process)

questions.explanation_es: Configurar ip ospf priority 0 en la interfaz excluye al router de la elección de DR/BDR; priority 255 en cambio lo haría más propenso a ganar la elección.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: By default, what network does OSPF advertise for a loopback interface configured with IP address 10.123.4.1/30?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF anuncia las interfaces de loopback como rutas host /32 por defecto, sin importar la máscara configurada en la interfaz.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an OSPF ABR advertises reachability for a route between two areas, what actually happens to the original intra-area route information?

options.A: The ABR originates a new Type 3 summary LSA representing that reachability into the other area.
options.B: The ABR bundles the entire source-area LSDB into a single LSA and floods it.
options.C: The ABR forwards the route only if both areas use the same area ID.
options.D: The ABR forwards the original Type 1 router LSA unchanged into the other area.

questions.explanation_es: El ABR no reenvía las LSA de tipo 1 originales entre áreas; en su lugar genera una nueva LSA de tipo 3 (resumen) que representa la alcanzabilidad de esa red en la otra área.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which statement best describes the scope of a single OSPF router's link-state database (LSDB) in a multi-area design?

options.A: Only ABRs maintain any LSDB; internal routers keep none.
options.B: Every router in the domain keeps an identical LSDB covering all areas.
options.C: A router maintains LSDB entries only for the areas in which it has at least one active interface.
options.D: The LSDB is synchronized identically across every router in the OSPF domain because Type 5 LSAs are understood to carry a complete copy of every area's internal topology information, not just external route summaries

questions.explanation_es: Cada router OSPF solo mantiene la base de datos de estado de enlace de las áreas a las que está directamente conectado, no de todo el dominio.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many OSPF LSA types are used for routing traditional IPv4 traffic?

options.A: Six
options.B: Four
options.C: Seven
options.D: Five

questions.explanation_es: OSPF utiliza seis tipos de LSA para IPv4: tipo 1 (router), 2 (network), 3 (summary), 4 (ASBR summary), 5 (AS external) y 7 (NSSA external).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the purpose of the age field carried in each entry of the OSPF link-state database?

options.A: To count upward so the LSA is removed from the LSDB once it reaches its maximum age (3600 seconds)
options.B: To provide version control so the most recently originated LSA is preferred
options.C: To count down from an initial value and purge the LSA once it reaches zero
options.D: To record, for troubleshooting purposes, the exact time the LSA was first advertised

questions.explanation_es: El campo age de una LSA se incrementa con el tiempo, y cuando alcanza el valor MaxAge (3600 segundos), la LSA se elimina de la base de datos y se fuerza un nuevo cálculo SPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which LSA type is present in every OSPF area, including the backbone and every non-backbone area?

options.A: Router LSA (Type 1)
options.B: Summary LSA (Type 3)
options.C: AS external LSA (Type 5)
options.D: Network LSA (Type 2)

questions.explanation_es: La LSA de tipo 1 (router LSA) la origina cada router en cada área a la que pertenece, por lo que existe en todas las áreas del dominio OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an ABR receives a Type 2 (network) LSA from a multi-access segment inside one of its attached areas, what does it do with that LSA?

options.A: It floods the Type 2 LSA unchanged into the other attached areas.
options.B: It keeps the Type 2 LSA scoped to the area where it was received and does not forward it into other areas.
options.C: It converts the Type 2 LSA into a Type 1 router LSA before forwarding it.
options.D: It forwards the Type 2 LSA only into the backbone area.

questions.explanation_es: Las LSA de tipo 2 (network) tienen alcance de área única; el ABR no las reenvía a otras áreas, sino que representa esa red mediante una LSA de tipo 3 si es necesario.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an ABR receives a Type 3 summary LSA inside one of its non-backbone areas, what does it do with that information?

options.A: It installs the route for the area where it was received but does not directly re-advertise that LSA into another non-backbone area.
options.B: It discards the Type 3 LSA without processing it.
options.C: It advertises the Type 3 LSA into the backbone area and flags it as an error.
options.D: It always re-advertises the same Type 3 LSA into every other attached area.

questions.explanation_es: Un ABR instala la información de la LSA tipo 3 recibida en un área no backbone, pero no la reenvía directamente a otra área no backbone; el tránsito entre áreas no troncales debe pasar por el área 0.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Is it accurate to say that OSPF always selects the mathematically shortest end-to-end path for both intra-area and inter-area destinations?

options.A: Yes, because SPF guarantees a globally optimal path for every route type.
options.B: No, because OSPF never uses SPF for inter-area routes, only for intra-area routes.
options.C: Yes, but only when all areas use the same reference bandwidth.
options.D: No, because inter-area path selection can be suboptimal since a Type 3 LSA only advertises a cost value, hiding the detailed topology beyond the originating ABR.

questions.explanation_es: Dentro de un área, OSPF sí garantiza la ruta más corta real mediante SPF; pero para rutas inter-área, el ABR solo anuncia un costo agregado sin el detalle topológico completo, por lo que la selección puede no ser la óptima global cuando existen múltiples ABR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why is segmenting a large OSPF domain into multiple areas considered a form of summarization?

options.A: Because it reduces the total IP address space required by the network
options.B: Because it removes the need for a designated router on multi-access segments
options.C: Because it compresses the LSA headers exchanged over slow WAN links
options.D: Because it hides the detailed topology of one area from routers in other areas, exposing only aggregated reachability information via Type 3 LSAs

questions.explanation_es: Dividir en áreas oculta los detalles topológicos internos de un área frente a las demás, ya que solo se propaga información agregada mediante LSA de resumen, lo cual es conceptualmente una forma de sumarización.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which command, configured under the OSPF process on an ABR, summarizes routes learned from one area before advertising them into another area?

options.A: The OSPF process command summary-address network prefix-length
options.B: The interface command area area-id summary-address network subnet-mask
options.C: The OSPF process command area area-id range network subnet-mask
options.D: The interface command summary-address network prefix-length

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización entre áreas en un ABR se configura con el comando de proceso area area-id range network subnet-mask; el comando summary-address se usa en el ASBR para sumarizar rutas externas redistribuidas.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many distinct OSPFv3 packet types exist for inter-router communication?

options.A: Six
options.B: Four
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 conserva la misma lógica y los mismos cinco tipos de paquete que OSPFv2: hello, DBD, LSR, LSU y LSAck.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What destination address does an OSPFv3 hello packet typically use?

options.A: IPv6 multicast address FF02::6
options.B: IPv6 multicast address FF02::5
options.C: IPv4 multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.D: IPv4 multicast address 224.0.0.10

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 usa la dirección multicast de enlace local FF02::5 (AllSPFRouters) para los paquetes hello, equivalente conceptual de 224.0.0.5 en OSPFv2.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How is OSPFv3 enabled on a router interface?

options.A: Automatically on every IPv6-enabled interface once the OSPF process initializes
options.B: With the command network interface-id under the OSPF process
options.C: With the interface command ospfv3 process-id ipv6 area area-id
options.D: With the command network prefix/prefix-length under the OSPF process

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de OSPFv2, OSPFv3 no usa network statements; se habilita directamente en la interfaz con el comando ospfv3 process-id ipv6 area area-id.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On a router with no IPv4 address configured anywhere, what happens if you configure only an IPv6 link-local address and enable OSPFv3 on that interface?

options.A: OSPFv3 fails to form an adjacency because the router ID defaults to 0.0.0.0 unless one is manually configured.
options.B: OSPFv3 automatically derives its router ID from the interface's MAC address.
options.C: The OSPFv3 process refuses to start at all without an IPv4 address present somewhere on the router.
options.D: OSPFv3 forms the neighbor adjacency normally, since a router ID is optional.

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 sigue necesitando un router ID de 32 bits; si no hay direcciones IPv4 disponibles ni se configura manualmente, el router ID queda en 0.0.0.0 y no se forman adyacencias.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Besides an IPv4 address and enabling the IPv4 address-family, what else is required to run OSPFv3 for IPv4 on a Cisco interface?

options.A: The interface must be configured as a passive interface for IPv4 traffic.
options.B: A separate OSPFv2 process must run in parallel on the same interface.
options.C: IPv6 unicast routing must be enabled and the interface still needs an IPv6 link-local address, because OSPFv3 always uses IPv6 for transport.
options.D: Nothing else; the IPv4 address and address-family are sufficient by themselves.

questions.explanation_es: Aunque OSPFv3 pueda transportar prefijos IPv4 mediante address-family ipv4, el protocolo sigue usando IPv6 como transporte subyacente, por lo que se requiere ipv6 unicast-routing y una dirección link-local IPv6 en la interfaz.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the default administrative distance assigned to routes learned via OSPF on a Cisco router?
questions.explanation_es: La distancia administrativa por defecto de OSPF es 110, comparada con 90 para EIGRP interno y 120 para RIP.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What problem does an OSPF virtual link solve?

options.A: It creates a redundant physical adjacency between two ABRs located in the same area.
options.B: It provides a logical connection joining a disconnected non-backbone area to the backbone (Area 0).
options.C: It allows two OSPF routers configured with different process IDs to form an adjacency.
options.D: It removes the need for a designated router on a multi-access network.

questions.explanation_es: Un enlace virtual conecta lógicamente, a través de un área de tránsito, a un área que no tiene conexión física con el área 0, cumpliendo así el requisito de que todas las áreas lleguen al backbone.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the AllSPFRouters multicast destination address used by OSPFv2?
questions.explanation_es: 224.0.0.5 es la dirección multicast AllSPFRouters usada por todos los routers OSPFv2 para el descubrimiento de vecinos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the AllDRouters multicast destination address used by OSPFv3?
questions.explanation_es: FF02::6 es la dirección multicast AllDRouters de OSPFv3, usada por routers no DR/BDR para enviar actualizaciones al DR y al BDR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How does OSPFv3 differ from OSPFv2 regarding the number of protocol instances that can run on a single link?

options.A: Multiple instances per link are supported only when the link carries IPv4 traffic.
options.B: Both versions restrict a link to a single OSPF process with no distinguishing field.
options.C: OSPFv3 allows multiple independent OSPFv3 instances on the same link, distinguished by an instance ID field; OSPFv2 has no equivalent mechanism.
options.D: OSPFv2 supports multiple instances per link, while OSPFv3 restricts a link to a single instance.

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 incorpora un campo de Instance ID que permite ejecutar varias instancias independientes de OSPFv3 sobre el mismo enlace, una capacidad que OSPFv2 no ofrece.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: On an Ethernet (multi-access) exit interface, which type of static route best avoids unintended forwarding behavior if the link fails?

options.A: A directly attached static route (specifying only the exit interface)
options.B: A fully specified static route (specifying both the exit interface and the next-hop IP address)
options.C: A static route to the null interface
options.D: A recursive static route (specifying only a next-hop IP address)

questions.explanation_es: En un enlace Ethernet, una ruta estática completamente especificada (interfaz de salida más next-hop) evita el comportamiento indeseado que puede ocurrir con rutas solo por interfaz (uso de ARP proxy) o rutas recursivas que podrían seguir resolviéndose por una ruta alterna tras una falla.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What is a floating static route primarily used for?

options.A: As a static route that keeps recursing until it resolves to a directly connected interface
options.B: As a route that is automatically installed once the primary route ages out after 180 seconds
options.C: As a static route configured with an administrative distance lower than the routing protocol it is meant to back up, so it takes over immediately once configured rather than waiting for the primary route to fail
options.D: As a backup route to a primary or dynamically learned route, made less preferred by configuring a higher administrative distance

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta estática flotante se configura con una distancia administrativa mayor que la de la ruta primaria (estática o dinámica), de modo que solo se instala en la RIB si la ruta primaria desaparece.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What defines a recursive static route?

options.A: A static route whose next hop is directly connected, requiring no further lookup
options.B: A static route where the exit interface and next-hop IP are both explicitly specified
options.C: A static route that points only to a null interface for traffic filtering
options.D: A static route whose next hop must itself be resolved by looking up another route already present in the RIB

questions.explanation_es: En una ruta estática recursiva, el router solo especifica una IP de next-hop, y debe hacer una búsqueda adicional en la tabla de enrutamiento para determinar la interfaz de salida hacia ese next-hop.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) can be used to segment routing tables for which type(s) of addressing?

options.A: IPv4 addresses only
options.B: IPv6 addresses only
options.C: Both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
options.D: MAC addresses only

questions.explanation_es: VRF-lite permite mantener tablas de enrutamiento separadas e independientes tanto para IPv4 como para IPv6 dentro del mismo router físico.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which two ranges represent private-use autonomous system numbers reserved by IANA? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation_es: El rango de 2 bytes reservado para ASN privados es 64.512–65.534, y el rango de 4 bytes reservado para ASN privados es 4.200.000.000–4.294.967.294 (según RFC 6996). Los otros rangos mostrados no corresponden a los bloques oficiales de ASN privados.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which category of BGP path attribute must be understood by every BGP implementation and must be included in every route advertisement sent to peers?

options.A: Optional non-transitive
options.B: Optional transitive
options.C: Well-known mandatory
options.D: Well-known discretionary

questions.explanation_es: Un atributo well-known mandatory (obligatorio y reconocido) debe ser entendido por todas las implementaciones de BGP y debe incluirse en cada actualización enviada a los vecinos (por ejemplo, AS_PATH, ORIGIN y NEXT_HOP). Los atributos discrecionales u opcionales no tienen ese requisito.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how BGP routers normally identify their peers?

options.A: BGP relies on DHCP option 43 to learn the IP addresses of potential peers.
options.B: BGP neighbors are discovered automatically by sending ARP requests to every directly connected subnet.
options.C: BGP routers automatically discover neighbors using multicast hello packets, similar to OSPF.
options.D: BGP peers are explicitly configured with neighbor statements; BGP does not use multicast hello discovery like IGPs do.

questions.explanation_es: BGP no utiliza mecanismos de descubrimiento dinámico basados en multidifusión como los IGP; los vecinos se configuran explícitamente mediante sentencias neighbor en cada extremo de la sesión.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the number of hops that can separate two BGP peers?

options.A: BGP requires an IGP to already be running between two peers before any session can form, regardless of hop count.
options.B: BGP peers must always be directly connected, one hop away from each other.
options.C: Only iBGP sessions can span multiple hops; eBGP sessions can never be configured to do so.
options.D: Because BGP runs over TCP, both iBGP and eBGP sessions can be established between routers that are multiple hops apart, given appropriate underlying reachability.

questions.explanation_es: Una sesión BGP no está limitada a un solo salto: como BGP funciona sobre TCP, tanto sesiones iBGP como eBGP (esta última usando ebgp-multihop) pueden establecerse entre routers separados por varios saltos, siempre que exista alcanzabilidad de capa 3 subyacente.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement about IPv4 unicast BGP sessions is accurate?

options.A: IPv4 unicast reachability must be explicitly activated with neighbor activate before the underlying TCP session can even be established.
options.B: BGP cannot form a TCP session with a peer until the IPv4 unicast address family has been manually enabled.
options.C: The IPv4 unicast address family must be created under address-family ipv4 unicast before any neighbor statement can be applied.
options.D: The IPv4 unicast address family is enabled by default for a newly configured neighbor, so no extra activation step is needed to form a basic session.

questions.explanation_es: La familia de direcciones IPv4 unicast se activa de forma predeterminada para cualquier vecino recién configurado, por lo que no es necesario activarla manualmente para establecer una sesión BGP básica sobre IPv4.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which command displays detailed BGP neighbor information, including the negotiated hello and hold timers, for a specific address family?

options.A: show bgp <afi> <safi> neighbors
options.B: show bgp neighbors
options.C: show ip bgp interface brief
options.D: show bgp <afi> <safi> summary

questions.explanation_es: El comando show bgp <afi> <safi> neighbors muestra información detallada de cada vecino, incluidos los temporizadores de hello y hold negociados para esa familia de direcciones específica.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: According to the BGP RIB model defined in RFC 4271, how many distinct routing information bases does a BGP speaker conceptually maintain?

options.A: Two
options.B: Three (Adj-RIB-In, Loc-RIB, and Adj-RIB-Out)
options.C: One
options.D: Four

questions.explanation_es: Según la RFC 4271, un router BGP mantiene conceptualmente tres bases de información de enrutamiento: Adj-RIB-In (rutas recibidas de los vecinos), Loc-RIB (la tabla BGP local con las mejores rutas seleccionadas) y Adj-RIB-Out (rutas que se anunciarán a cada vecino).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement best describes what a BGP router advertises to its neighbors for a given prefix, by default?

options.A: It advertises every path it has learned for that prefix so each neighbor can build a full topology map.
options.B: It advertises only the single best path it selected for that prefix, unless the BGP Additional Paths (Add-Path) capability has been negotiated.
options.C: It advertises all iBGP-learned paths but withholds every eBGP-learned path.
options.D: It advertises whichever path has the shortest AS_Path, even if that path was not selected as the overall best path.

questions.explanation_es: De forma predeterminada, un router BGP anuncia a sus vecinos únicamente la mejor ruta que ha seleccionado para un prefijo determinado, no todas las rutas candidatas; para anunciar múltiples caminos es necesario negociar la funcionalidad BGP Additional Paths (Add-Path).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which BGP command creates a summarized route while suppressing advertisement of its more-specific component routes, shielding downstream routers from flaps of those individual prefixes?

options.A: aggregate-address <network> <subnet-mask> summary-only
options.B: summary-address <network> <subnet-mask>
options.C: aggregate-address <network> <subnet-mask> as-set
options.D: summary-address <network> <mask> <subnet-mask>

questions.explanation_es: El comando aggregate-address <red> <máscara> summary-only crea una ruta resumen y suprime el anuncio de las rutas más específicas que la componen, evitando que los routers en sentido descendente procesen las fluctuaciones (flaps) de cada prefijo individual.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement about establishing a BGP session that carries IPv6 prefixes is accurate?

options.A: IPv6 unicast is enabled by default for every neighbor, exactly like IPv4 unicast, so no additional activation is required.
options.B: BGP cannot exchange IPv6 prefixes under any circumstances; only IPv4 transport and prefixes are supported.
options.C: The address-family ipv6 configuration only changes the output of show commands and has no effect on which routes are actually exchanged.
options.D: The IPv6 unicast address family must be explicitly configured and activated for the neighbor before IPv6 prefixes can be exchanged, unlike the default IPv4 unicast address family.

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de IPv4 unicast, la familia de direcciones IPv6 unicast no se activa de forma predeterminada: es necesario configurarla explícitamente con address-family ipv6 y activar al vecino con neighbor activate para poder intercambiar prefijos IPv6.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In which scenarios is it generally considered poor practice to let a multihomed site provide transit routing for traffic belonging to other sites? (Choose three.)

options.A: MPLS-based connections at a data center that has been sized for transit traffic
options.B: Internet-facing connections at a data center
options.C: MPLS-based connections at a branch location
options.D: Internet-facing connections at a branch location

questions.explanation_es: El enrutamiento de tránsito suele evitarse en las conexiones a Internet, tanto en centros de datos como en sucursales, y en las conexiones MPLS de las sucursales, ya que esos enlaces normalmente no están dimensionados para cursar tráfico ajeno. En cambio, un centro de datos conectado por MPLS sí puede actuar como punto de tránsito planificado porque su ancho de banda puede dimensionarse para ello.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes using an extended ACL to conditionally match routes (network prefixes) rather than packets?

options.A: The way the source and destination fields are interpreted when matching a route can differ depending on whether the ACL is applied to an IGP or to BGP.
options.B: Extended ACLs cannot be used at all to filter routing protocol prefixes, only to filter packets.
options.C: Extended ACLs behave identically whether they are filtering packets, IGP routes, or BGP routes.
options.D: Extended ACLs can only be used to filter BGP routes; IGPs must always rely on standard ACLs instead.

questions.explanation_es: Cuando una ACL extendida se utiliza para hacer coincidir prefijos de enrutamiento en lugar de paquetes, la forma en que se interpretan los campos de origen y destino puede variar según se aplique a un IGP o a BGP, por lo que la misma ACL no necesariamente produce el mismo resultado en ambos casos.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Given the prefix-list entry "permit 10.168.0.0/13 ge 24", which two prefixes does it match? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation_es: La entrada permit 10.168.0.0/13 ge 24 exige que el prefijo esté contenido dentro del rango 10.168.0.0/13 (10.168.0.0–10.175.255.255) y que su longitud de máscara sea de 24 bits o más. El prefijo base /13 queda excluido porque su longitud (13) es menor que el mínimo exigido (24), y 10.104.0.0/24 queda excluido porque no pertenece al rango de red indicado.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which regular expression correctly matches a BGP route whose AS_Path shows that it originated in AS 300 (that is, AS 300 is the last, originating ASN in the path)?
questions.explanation_es: En las expresiones regulares de BGP, el símbolo $ representa el final de la cadena AS_Path, es decir, el AS de origen (el primero en originar el prefijo). Por lo tanto, _300$ coincide con rutas cuyo AS de origen es el 300. El símbolo ^, en cambio, representa el inicio de la cadena, es decir, el AS más reciente en el trayecto.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: If a permit clause in a route map contains no match statements at all, what happens to routes evaluated against that clause?

options.A: All routes reaching that clause are accepted, since a permit clause with no match conditions matches everything.
options.B: The router raises a configuration error and refuses to link the route map to the BGP neighbor.
options.C: All routes reaching that clause are discarded.
options.D: The routes are discarded and a syslog message is generated.

questions.explanation_es: Una cláusula permit de un route-map que no contiene ninguna sentencia match se considera una coincidencia universal: todas las rutas que llegan a esa cláusula se aceptan, aplicando además cualquier sentencia set que incluya.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question:
Consider the following route map:
route-map QUESTION deny 10
 match ip address prefix-list PrefixRFC1918
route-map QUESTION permit 20
 set metric 200
What happens to a prefix that does NOT match the PrefixRFC1918 prefix list?

options.A: The prefix is denied because it failed to match sequence 10.
options.B: The prefix is permitted, and Cisco IOS resets its metric to a default value of 100.
options.C: The prefix is permitted and has its metric set to 200, because it falls through to sequence 20, which matches everything.
options.D: The prefix is permitted, but its metric is left unchanged.

questions.explanation_es: La ruta que no coincide con la lista de prefijos PrefixRFC1918 no coincide con la secuencia 10 (deny), por lo que la evaluación continúa con la secuencia 20. Como esa secuencia es un permit sin condiciones de coincidencia, la ruta se permite y se le aplica la sentencia set metric 200.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding combining a BGP AS_Path filter (filter-list) with a prefix-list filter on the same neighbor?

options.A: A prefix-list always overrides and disables any AS_Path filter-list configured on the same neighbor.
options.B: An AS_Path filter-list and a prefix-list can both be applied to the same neighbor and direction at the same time; a route must pass both to be accepted.
options.C: Cisco IOS allows only one type of inbound filter per neighbor, so an AS_Path filter-list and a prefix-list cannot both be configured on it.
options.D: AS_Path filter-lists can only be applied globally to a BGP process and never to an individual neighbor.

questions.explanation_es: Un filtro de AS_Path (filter-list) y una lista de prefijos (prefix-list) son mecanismos de filtrado independientes y pueden aplicarse simultáneamente al mismo vecino y en la misma dirección; para que una ruta sea aceptada debe superar ambos filtros.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which of the following is not an actual well-known BGP community?

options.A: Private_Route
options.B: Internet
options.C: No_Advertise
options.D: No_Export

questions.explanation_es: No_Advertise, No_Export e Internet son comunidades BGP well-known reconocidas y estandarizadas. Private_Route no es una comunidad well-known definida; es un nombre inventado que no existe en la especificación de BGP.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In the Cisco BGP best-path selection process, which attribute is evaluated second, right after weight?

options.A: Weight
options.B: Origin
options.C: Local preference
options.D: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED)

questions.explanation_es: En el algoritmo de selección de mejor ruta de BGP en Cisco, tras comparar el weight (el primer criterio, local al router), el segundo criterio evaluado es la preferencia local (local preference), que se comparte entre los routers del mismo AS.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: By default, under what condition does a Cisco BGP router compare the MED (Multi-Exit Discriminator) attribute between candidate paths?

options.A: MED is never used unless BGP confederations are configured.
options.B: MED is compared for every path by default, regardless of the originating AS.
options.C: Only when the paths were received from neighbors in the same neighboring AS, unless bgp always-compare-med is configured.
options.D: Only when the paths were received from different autonomous systems.

questions.explanation_es: De forma predeterminada, Cisco IOS solo compara el atributo MED entre rutas recibidas del mismo AS vecino; para comparar el MED de rutas provenientes de AS vecinos distintos es necesario habilitar el comando bgp always-compare-med.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which BGP message type is used both to advertise newly reachable routes and to withdraw previously advertised routes?

options.A: Keepalive
options.B: Open
options.C: Notification
options.D: Update

questions.explanation_es: El mensaje BGP Update se utiliza tanto para anunciar rutas nuevas y alcanzables como para retirar (withdraw) rutas previamente anunciadas que ya no son válidas.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In which BGP finite-state-machine state do peers begin exchanging routing information using Update messages?

options.A: Connect
options.B: OpenConfirm
options.C: Active
options.D: Established

questions.explanation_es: En el estado Established de la máquina de estados de BGP, la sesión ya está completamente establecida y los vecinos comienzan a intercambiar información de enrutamiento mediante mensajes Update.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which traffic delivery model most accurately characterizes IP multicast forwarding?

options.A: One sender exchanging data with a single specific receiver
options.B: One sender flooding data to every host on the network
options.C: One sender delivering data to a defined set of interested receivers
options.D: Every host exchanging data with every other host simultaneously

questions.explanation_es: El multicast IP se describe como un modelo "uno-a-muchos" (one-to-many), donde una fuente envía tráfico solo a los receptores que han manifestado interés en unirse al grupo, a diferencia del broadcast que llega a todos los hosts.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which two protocols form the core building blocks that make IP multicast routing and group membership possible? (Choose two.)

options.A: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF)
options.B: Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM)
options.C: Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD)
options.D: Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP)

questions.explanation_es: PIM construye y mantiene los árboles de distribución multicast entre routers, mientras que IGMP permite que los hosts informen a su router local sobre su interés en unirse a un grupo multicast; ambos son indispensables para el funcionamiento básico de multicast.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: According to RFC 2365, which multicast address block is reserved for administratively (organization-local) scoped use and is never assigned globally by IANA?
questions.explanation_es: El bloque 239.0.0.0/8 está reservado por la RFC 2365 para uso local u organizacional, de forma similar a las direcciones privadas de la RFC 1918; no se asigna globalmente, por lo que los administradores pueden reutilizarlo libremente dentro de su propio dominio.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What are the fixed first 24 bits of every Ethernet multicast MAC address derived from an IPv4 multicast group address?
questions.explanation_es: Los primeros 24 bits de toda dirección MAC multicast IPv4 están fijados en 01:00:5E; los 23 bits restantes se copian directamente de los 23 bits de orden inferior de la dirección IP multicast del grupo.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: How can a host begin receiving traffic for a multicast group without waiting for the next periodic query from its router?

options.A: By sending a gratuitous ARP reply for the group's mapped MAC address
options.B: By sending an ICMP router solicitation message
options.C: By sending an unsolicited IGMP membership report for the group
options.D: By waiting passively for a PIM join to arrive from the RP

questions.explanation_es: A partir de IGMPv2, un host puede enviar un reporte de membresía IGMP no solicitado (unsolicited report) hacia la dirección del grupo en cuanto desea unirse, sin necesidad de esperar la consulta periódica del router.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What functional capability did IGMPv3 add that IGMPv2 lacks?

options.A: The ability for the router to send periodic membership queries
options.B: A shorter default query interval of 60 seconds
options.C: Support for source-filtered membership reports (include/exclude source lists)
options.D: The ability to snoop multicast traffic at Layer 2

questions.explanation_es: IGMPv3 introdujo reportes de membresía con filtrado por fuente (listas include/exclude), lo que permite a un host especificar de qué fuentes desea o no recibir tráfico, una capacidad necesaria para SSM que IGMPv2 no posee.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes IGMPv3's relationship to earlier IGMP versions and multicast service models?

options.A: IGMPv3 replaced PIM as the multicast routing protocol
options.B: IGMPv3 works only with SSM and cannot interoperate with IGMPv1/v2 hosts
options.C: IGMPv3 routers can still support IGMPv1 and IGMPv2 hosts, and IGMPv3 can also be used with ASM
options.D: IGMPv3 requires every host to be manually configured with the RP address

questions.explanation_es: IGMPv3 es retrocompatible: un router con IGMPv3 puede seguir interoperando con hosts que usan IGMPv1 o IGMPv2, y aunque IGMPv3 es imprescindible para SSM, también puede emplearse en el modelo ASM tradicional.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which feature prevents a Layer 2 switch from flooding multicast frames out every port in a VLAN?

options.A: IGMP snooping
options.B: Storm control on broadcast traffic
options.C: Spanning Tree PortFast
options.D: Unicast MAC flooding protection

questions.explanation_es: El IGMP snooping permite que el switch examine los mensajes IGMP y construya una tabla de puertos con hosts interesados, reenviando el tráfico multicast solo a esos puertos en lugar de inundar toda la VLAN.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which two statements accurately describe the shortest path tree (SPT) and rendezvous point tree (RPT) used by PIM-SM? (Choose two.)

options.A: The SPT is rooted at the multicast source
options.B: The RPT is rooted at the multicast source
options.C: The RPT is a shared tree rooted at the rendezvous point
options.D: The SPT is a shared tree rooted at the rendezvous point

questions.explanation_es: El SPT (shortest path tree) tiene como raíz a la propia fuente multicast y ofrece la ruta más corta hacia los receptores, mientras que el RPT (rendezvous point tree) es un árbol compartido cuya raíz es el rendezvous point (RP), usado por múltiples fuentes hacia el mismo grupo.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: After the last-hop router (LHR) receives an IGMP membership report from a directly connected receiver, what does it do next?

options.A: It floods the join request out all PIM-enabled interfaces
options.B: It sends a PIM join message directly toward the source
options.C: It sends a PIM register message toward the source
options.D: It sends a PIM join message toward the rendezvous point

questions.explanation_es: El LHR, al recibir un join IGMP de un receptor, genera un PIM join (*,G) que envía hacia el RP para engancharse al árbol compartido (RPT) y comenzar a recibir el tráfico del grupo.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: When a multicast source connected to the first-hop router (FHR) starts sending traffic but no receivers have joined yet, what does the FHR do?

options.A: It floods the encapsulated data as multicast register messages to all PIM neighbors
options.B: It drops the traffic until a PIM join is received from a downstream router
options.C: It encapsulates the multicast data inside PIM register messages and unicasts them to the RP until it gets a register-stop
options.D: It waits for the RP to unicast a register message confirming interested receivers exist

questions.explanation_es: El FHR encapsula el tráfico multicast dentro de mensajes PIM register y los envía en unicast al RP; este proceso continúa hasta que el RP responde con un register-stop, momento en el que el FHR deja de encapsular y unicastear el tráfico.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which group-to-RP mapping mechanism was originally developed by Cisco, prior to the standardized Bootstrap Router mechanism?

options.A: Bootstrap Router (BSR)
options.B: Anycast-RP
options.C: Auto-RP
options.D: Static RP configuration

questions.explanation_es: Auto-RP es un mecanismo propietario de Cisco creado antes de que se estandarizara BSR (definido en la RFC 5059) para automatizar el descubrimiento y la distribución de la información de mapeo grupo-a-RP entre los routers PIM-SM.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which statement about rendezvous points (RPs) in PIM dense mode (PIM-DM) is correct?

options.A: PIM-DM requires at least one RP to build the initial flood-and-prune tree
options.B: PIM-DM requires two RPs configured in an active/standby pair
options.C: PIM-DM uses a single RP elected dynamically via BSR
options.D: PIM-DM does not use RPs at all, since it floods traffic and then prunes unwanted branches

questions.explanation_es: PIM en modo denso (PIM-DM) no utiliza rendezvous points; en su lugar, inunda el tráfico multicast a toda la red y luego poda (prune) las ramas hacia donde no hay receptores interesados. El concepto de RP es exclusivo de PIM-SM.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which three of the following are commonly cited as leading causes of QoS problems on a network? (Choose three.)

options.A: Packet loss
options.B: Excessive latency and jitter
options.C: Insufficient available bandwidth
options.D: Use of copper cabling instead of fiber

questions.explanation_es: Los problemas de calidad de servicio se atribuyen principalmente a la falta de ancho de banda suficiente, a la latencia y variación de retardo (jitter) excesivas, y a la pérdida de paquetes. El tipo de medio físico, como el uso de cableado de cobre en lugar de fibra, no es en sí mismo una de las causas típicas que motivan la implementación de QoS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which three of the following are classified as fixed (constant) components of end-to-end network delay? (Choose three.)

options.A: Queuing delay
options.B: Propagation delay
options.C: Processing delay
options.D: Serialization delay

questions.explanation_es: El retardo de propagación, el retardo de serialización y el retardo de procesamiento se consideran componentes fijos del retardo total, ya que dependen de factores constantes como la distancia, la velocidad del enlace y la arquitectura del dispositivo. El retardo de encolamiento, en cambio, es variable porque depende del nivel de congestión en un momento dado, y es precisamente esa variabilidad la que produce el jitter.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the three QoS implementation models?

options.A: Differentiated Services (DiffServ)
options.B: Integrated Services (IntServ)
options.C: Expedited Forwarding
options.D: Best effort

questions.explanation_es: Los tres modelos de implementación de QoS son mejor esfuerzo (best effort), servicios integrados (IntServ) y servicios diferenciados (DiffServ). Expedited Forwarding no es un modelo de QoS, sino un comportamiento por salto (per-hop behavior, PHB) definido dentro del modelo DiffServ.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which QoS implementation model requires end hosts and network devices to use a signaling protocol to reserve resources for a flow before transmitting?

options.A: RSVP
options.B: Differentiated Services (DiffServ)
options.C: Integrated Services (IntServ)
options.D: Best effort

questions.explanation_es: El modelo de Servicios Integrados (IntServ) exige que las aplicaciones señalicen sus requisitos a la red y reserven recursos extremo a extremo antes de enviar tráfico, utilizando el protocolo RSVP (Resource Reservation Protocol) para dicha señalización. RSVP es el protocolo que se emplea para lograrlo, pero no es en sí mismo un modelo de QoS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which QoS implementation model is the most widely deployed in modern enterprise networks?

options.A: Differentiated Services (DiffServ)
options.B: Integrated Services (IntServ)
options.C: RSVP-based reservation
options.D: Best effort

questions.explanation_es: El modelo de Servicios Diferenciados (DiffServ) es el más utilizado en las redes actuales porque clasifica el tráfico en un número reducido de clases y aplica un tratamiento por salto (PHB) a cada una, sin requerir señalización de extremo a extremo ni el mantenimiento de estado por flujo, lo que lo hace mucho más escalable que IntServ.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In the Modular QoS CLI (MQC), which command is used, while inside policy-map configuration mode, to reference a previously defined class map?

options.A: class class-map-name
options.B: class-map match-any class-map-name
options.C: policy-map class-map-name
options.D: match class class-map-name

questions.explanation_es: Dentro del modo de configuración de policy-map, el comando class class-map-name se utiliza para hacer referencia a un class-map ya creado y así aplicarle acciones de calidad de servicio, como marcado, policiamiento o asignación de ancho de banda. El comando class-map se usa en un contexto distinto, en el modo de configuración global, para definir los criterios de clasificación.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which command attaches a policy map to an interface within the Modular QoS CLI framework?

options.A: apply-policy output policy-map-name
options.B: class-map input policy-map-name
options.C: service-policy {input | output} policy-map-name
options.D: policy-map input policy-map-name

questions.explanation_es: El comando service-policy, seguido de la palabra clave input u output y el nombre del policy-map, es el que se aplica en modo de configuración de interfaz para asociar una política de QoS ya definida al tráfico entrante o saliente de esa interfaz.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: True or false: Traffic classification for QoS purposes should ideally be performed in the core of the network.

options.A: True
options.B: Only when trust boundaries are disabled
options.C: Only on core routers with hardware-based CEF
options.D: False

questions.explanation_es: La clasificación del tráfico debe realizarse lo más cerca posible del origen del tráfico, es decir, en el borde de la red (por ejemplo, en el switch de acceso o en el propio endpoint), y no en el núcleo. Clasificar en el borde permite que todos los dispositivos posteriores del trayecto puedan aplicar el tratamiento adecuado basándose en la marca ya asignada, sin tener que reexaminar el paquete completo en cada salto.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: True or false: The Differentiated Services (DS) field in the IP header is an 8-bit DSCP field that provides 64 possible classification values (0 through 63).

options.A: True, but only in IPv6 headers
options.B: True
options.C: True, but only the 4 most significant bits are used
options.D: False

questions.explanation_es: El campo DS (Differentiated Services) ocupa 8 bits del encabezado IP, pero el propio DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) solo utiliza los 6 bits más significativos de ese campo, lo cual sí produce 64 valores posibles (0 a 63); los 2 bits restantes se reservan para ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification). Por lo tanto, es incorrecto describir el campo completo de 8 bits como si fuera únicamente el DSCP.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which two MQC configuration snippets correctly mark traffic matched by class VOIP-TELEPHONY with DSCP EF? (Choose two.)

options.A: policy-map INBOUND-MARKING-POLICY / class VOIP-TELEPHONY / set ip dscp ef
options.B: policy-map INBOUND-MARKING-POLICY / class VOIP-TELEPHONY / set ip precedence ef
options.C: policy-map INBOUND-MARKING-POLICY / class VOIP-TELEPHONY / set dscp ef
options.D: policy-map INBOUND-MARKING-POLICY / class VOIP-TELEPHONY / mark dscp ef

questions.explanation_es: Tanto set ip dscp ef como set dscp ef son sintaxis válidas de la Modular QoS CLI para marcar el tráfico coincidente con el valor DSCP EF (Expedited Forwarding). El comando mark dscp no existe en la MQC, y el comando set ip precedence no acepta la palabra clave ef, ya que la precedencia IP usa una escala numérica de 0 a 7, no las etiquetas de nombre que emplea DSCP.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which traffic-conditioning mechanism drops or re-marks packets that exceed a configured traffic rate?

options.A: Policers
options.B: Weighted round robin (WRR)
options.C: Class-based weighted fair queuing (CBWFQ)
options.D: Shapers

questions.explanation_es: Los policiadores (policers) miden el tráfico contra una tasa configurada y, cuando el tráfico excede esa tasa, lo descartan o lo remarcan con un valor de menor prioridad. Los conformadores (shapers), en cambio, retrasan el tráfico excedente almacenándolo en una cola en lugar de descartarlo.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In traffic-policing terminology, what does the variable Tc represent?

options.A: The committed time interval used to measure the committed burst
options.B: The number of unused token credits carried over from the previous interval
options.C: A counter used strictly for traffic-control accounting
options.D: The size, in bytes, of the committed burst (Bc) bucket

questions.explanation_es: Tc representa el intervalo de tiempo comprometido (committed time interval) que se utiliza en los algoritmos de policiamiento de tráfico, y se calcula típicamente como Bc dividido entre el CIR (tasa de información comprometida). Es el periodo sobre el cual se mide si el tráfico respeta la tasa comprometida.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which two congestion-management (queuing) mechanisms are recommended for modern networks carrying converged voice, video, and data traffic? (Choose two.)

options.A: Low-latency queuing (LLQ)
options.B: Class-based weighted fair queuing (CBWFQ)
options.C: Weighted random early detection (WRED)
options.D: Legacy priority queuing (PQ)

questions.explanation_es: CBWFQ y LLQ son los mecanismos de gestión de congestión recomendados para redes convergentes modernas, ya que combinan un reparto justo del ancho de banda entre clases con una cola de prioridad estricta para el tráfico sensible a la latencia. La cola de prioridad clásica (PQ) no se recomienda porque puede dejar sin servicio a las colas de menor prioridad, y WRED es en realidad un mecanismo de prevención de congestión, no de gestión de colas.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which congestion-avoidance mechanism is recommended for modern rich-media networks?

options.A: First-in, first-out (FIFO) queuing
options.B: Tail drop
options.C: Plain random early detection (RED)
options.D: Weighted random early detection (WRED)

questions.explanation_es: WRED es el mecanismo de prevención de congestión recomendado porque descarta paquetes de forma selectiva según su prioridad (por ejemplo, según el valor DSCP) antes de que la cola se llene por completo, evitando así la sincronización global de TCP. El descarte por cola llena (tail drop) y el RED simple no diferencian entre clases de tráfico, y FIFO ni siquiera implementa gestión de colas por clase.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question:
Given the configuration below, which two statements correctly describe the effect of "percent 30"? (Choose two.)
policy-map QUEUING
 class VOIP
  priority level 1 percent 30

options.A: Priority traffic is allowed to exceed 30 percent whenever additional bandwidth is available
options.B: The priority class can never consume more than 30 percent of the interface bandwidth, even when spare capacity exists
options.C: The priority queue is policed to 30 percent of interface bandwidth at all times, regardless of congestion
options.D: The priority queue is capped at 30 percent only while the interface is congested

questions.explanation_es: El comando priority configura una cola de prioridad estricta que Cisco siempre policía a la tasa configurada (en este caso, el 30 por ciento del ancho de banda de la interfaz), tanto si hay congestión como si no la hay. Este policiamiento constante existe precisamente para evitar que el tráfico de la cola de prioridad monopolice el enlace y deje sin ancho de banda a las demás clases, por lo que dicho tráfico nunca puede superar el 30 por ciento configurado, incluso si sobra capacidad disponible.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which type of network delay accounts for the time a router or switch takes to move a packet from an input interface to the output queue of the outbound interface?

options.A: Serialization delay
options.B: Queuing delay
options.C: Processing delay
options.D: Propagation delay

questions.explanation_es: El retardo de procesamiento es el tiempo fijo que le toma a un dispositivo de red tomar un paquete de una interfaz de entrada y colocarlo en la cola de salida de la interfaz correspondiente, y depende de factores como la velocidad de la CPU, el modo de conmutación de paquetes y la carga del dispositivo.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which QoS process examines fields within a packet to distinguish one type of traffic from another so it can be treated differently downstream?

options.A: Shaping
options.B: Policing
options.C: Marking
options.D: Classification

questions.explanation_es: La clasificación es el proceso de QoS encargado de examinar campos del paquete, como direcciones, puertos o valores existentes de DSCP, para distinguir un tipo de tráfico de otro y determinar qué tratamiento diferenciado debe recibir. El marcado, el policiamiento y el conformado son acciones posteriores que se aplican una vez que el tráfico ya ha sido clasificado.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: In NTP, what term describes the numeric value indicating how many hops a device is from an authoritative reference clock, used to gauge how trustworthy that time source is?

options.A: Root dispersion
options.B: Administrative distance
options.C: Poll interval
options.D: Stratum

questions.explanation_es: El estrato (stratum) indica la distancia jerárquica de un dispositivo respecto a la fuente de tiempo autorizada, como un reloj atómico. Un número de estrato más bajo implica una fuente más confiable y cercana a la referencia original.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: An NTP client has been configured to reference three different NTP servers at the same time. Which statement best describes how the client actually uses these servers to set its clock?

options.A: It always uses the first server listed in the configuration and ignores the others unless that one fails
options.B: It averages the time reported by all configured servers into a single value
options.C: It synchronizes to only one selected server at a time, chosen using criteria such as stratum and clock stability
options.D: It alternates between the servers on a fixed round-robin schedule

questions.explanation_es: Aunque un cliente NTP puede consultar varios servidores, el algoritmo de selección de NTP elige un único servidor de sistema (system peer) para sincronizar el reloj, basándose en el estrato, la estabilidad y otros criterios; no promedia ni alterna entre todos ellos por turnos.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What is the main benefit of configuring a peer association between two NTP servers, instead of a simple client-server relationship?

options.A: It lets both devices stay synchronized with each other and provides redundancy if one of them loses contact with its higher-stratum source
options.B: It allows both devices to share a single IP address for all NTP queries
options.C: It forces both devices to become stratum 1 references regardless of their actual hardware clock
options.D: It removes the need for a stratum hierarchy between the two devices

questions.explanation_es: Cuando dos servidores NTP se configuran como peers, ambos pueden mantenerse sincronizados entre sí y ofrecer redundancia: si uno pierde el acceso a su fuente de estrato superior, todavía puede obtener una referencia de tiempo razonable a través del otro peer.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Which command should be used on a Cisco IOS router to display the currently active NAT translation entries?

options.A: show xlate
options.B: show ip nat translations
options.C: show ip translations
options.D: show nat table

questions.explanation_es: El comando show ip nat translations muestra la tabla de traducciones NAT activas en un router con Cisco IOS. El comando show xlate corresponde a dispositivos de seguridad como ASA, no a routers IOS.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: A company uses the private range 10.0.0.0/8 internally. A workstation with address 10.1.1.1 sends traffic to the Internet through a NAT-enabled edge router. From the router's NAT perspective, this original 10.1.1.1 address is classified as which type of address?

options.A: Inside global
options.B: Inside local
options.C: Outside local
options.D: Outside global

questions.explanation_es: La dirección inside local es la dirección IP asignada al host dentro de la red privada, tal como aparece antes de aplicar la traducción NAT. La dirección inside global es la que representa a ese mismo host una vez traducida para salir a Internet.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: By default, how long does a Cisco router keep a dynamic NAT translation entry for a TCP connection before removing it from the translation table due to inactivity?

options.A: 1 hour
options.B: 12 hours
options.C: 4 hours
options.D: 24 hours

questions.explanation_es: El temporizador de expiración predeterminado para las traducciones NAT dinámicas de conexiones TCP es de 24 horas; transcurrido ese tiempo sin actividad, la entrada se elimina de la tabla de traducciones.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Which global configuration command changes the default idle timeout applied to dynamic NAT translation entries?

options.A: ip nat pool timeout seconds
options.B: nat translation-timeout seconds
options.C: ip nat translation timeout seconds
options.D: ip nat inside timeout seconds

questions.explanation_es: El comando ip nat translation timeout seconds permite modificar el valor predeterminado de 24 horas que se usa para expirar las entradas dinámicas de traducción NAT.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which two limitations of a typical host's default-gateway setup are addressed by first-hop redundancy protocols (FHRPs) such as HSRP, VRRP, and GLBP? (Choose two.)

options.A: Hosts typically reach their default gateway through a static route entry that does not react automatically to a gateway outage
options.B: Hosts must run a distance-vector routing protocol to pick the best gateway
options.C: Hosts are usually configured with only a single default gateway and have no built-in way to fail over to a backup
options.D: Hosts must run a link-state routing protocol to learn about every available gateway on the segment

questions.explanation_es: Los hosts normalmente se configuran con una única puerta de enlace predeterminada, a menudo mediante una ruta estática, sin ningún mecanismo propio para detectar una falla y cambiar a otra puerta de enlace. Los FHRP resuelven esto presentando una IP virtual respaldada por varios routers que se turnan el reenvío del tráfico.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which two first-hop redundancy protocols are Cisco-proprietary rather than open industry standards? (Choose two.)

options.A: VRRP
options.B: HSRP
options.C: ODR
options.D: GLBP

questions.explanation_es: HSRP y GLBP son protocolos propietarios de Cisco. VRRP es un estándar abierto definido por el IETF, y ODR (On-Demand Routing) ni siquiera es un protocolo de redundancia de primer salto.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which interface configuration command assigns 10.1.1.1 as the virtual IP address for HSRP group 1?

options.A: hsrp 1 vip 10.1.1.1
options.B: standby 1 ip 10.1.1.1
options.C: hsrp 1 ip 10.1.1.1
options.D: standby ip 1 10.1.1.1

questions.explanation_es: El comando standby 1 ip 10.1.1.1 configura la dirección IP virtual del grupo HSRP 1 en la interfaz. La sintaxis de HSRP usa la palabra clave standby, no hsrp.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Which first-hop redundancy protocol natively provides load balancing of outbound traffic across multiple gateway routers while presenting a single virtual IP address to hosts?

options.A: HSRP
options.B: VRRP
options.C: ODR
options.D: GLBP

questions.explanation_es: GLBP ofrece balanceo de carga nativo: asigna distintas direcciones MAC virtuales a los distintos routers miembros de un mismo grupo, de modo que los hosts distribuyen su tráfico entre varios gateways activos simultáneamente. HSRP y VRRP mantienen un solo router activo/maestro por grupo a la vez.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In VRRP terminology, which router role performs the same function as the active router in an HSRP group?

options.A: Backup
options.B: Master
options.C: Standby
options.D: Primary

questions.explanation_es: El router master de VRRP cumple la misma función que el router activo en HSRP: es el que reenvía el tráfico destinado a la IP virtual en condiciones normales de operación.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: When you deploy path isolation with VRF-based virtualization on a network device, which two planes of operation are being virtualized? (Choose two.)

options.A: Management plane
options.B: Control plane
options.C: Physical plane
options.D: Data plane

questions.explanation_es: VRF virtualiza tanto el plano de control (tablas de enrutamiento independientes) como el plano de datos (tablas de reenvío independientes) para cada instancia; el plano de gestión normalmente permanece compartido en VRF-Lite.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core components that make up a VRF instance?

options.A: A derived forwarding table
options.B: An access control list bound to the instance
options.C: An IP routing table
options.D: The interface(s) assigned to the instance

questions.explanation_es: Una instancia VRF se compone de una tabla de enrutamiento IP, una tabla de reenvío derivada y las interfaces asignadas; una ACL no es un componente intrínseco de la instancia VRF, aunque se pueda aplicar por separado.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Which plane of operation is responsible for the protocols, databases, and tables used to compute loop-free paths and make forwarding decisions?

options.A: Management plane
options.B: Services plane
options.C: Control plane
options.D: Data plane

questions.explanation_es: El plano de control incluye los protocolos, bases de datos y tablas (como las de enrutamiento) que se usan para calcular rutas libres de bucles y tomar decisiones de reenvío.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: True or false: VRF-Lite provides genuine separation of the control and data planes between virtual networks on the same device.

options.A: Only the data plane is separated, not the control plane
options.B: False
options.C: True
options.D: This is true only when combined with MPLS

questions.explanation_es: VRF-Lite crea planos de control y de datos independientes para cada instancia, de modo que no hay comunicación entre VRFs distintos a menos que se permita explícitamente, por ejemplo mediante route leaking.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: When configuring a point-to-point GRE tunnel interface, which two of the following configuration items are optional rather than mandatory?

options.A: keepalive
options.B: tunnel source
options.C: tunnel mode
options.D: tunnel destination

questions.explanation_es: El modo del túnel (tunnel mode) tiene GRE sobre IP como valor por defecto, y los keepalives son opcionales; en cambio, tunnel source y tunnel destination son obligatorios para que el túnel se levante.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: True or false: GRE was originally developed to let networks carry protocols that could not be natively routed across an IP backbone.

options.A: True, but only for IPv6 traffic
options.B: True
options.C: False
options.D: False, GRE was originally created specifically to encapsulate IPX and AppleTalk traffic between Cisco routers, not as a general-purpose, protocol-agnostic tunneling mechanism for arbitrary payloads

questions.explanation_es: GRE se creó originalmente para permitir el transporte de protocolos heredados y no enrutables de forma nativa, como SNA, encapsulándolos dentro de paquetes IP para cruzar una red troncal IP.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which of the following should generally NOT be advertised dynamically via an IGP running inside a GRE tunnel?

options.A: Connected LAN interfaces
options.B: The tunnel source interface or its underlying IP address
options.C: The IP address assigned to the GRE tunnel interface itself
options.D: Loopback interfaces used by internal networks

questions.explanation_es: Si la dirección o interfaz de origen del túnel se anuncia dinámicamente por el mismo protocolo que corre dentro del túnel, se puede generar un problema de enrutamiento recursivo que tumba el túnel.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which two packet transport modes are defined for IPsec?

options.A: Tunnel mode
options.B: Transparent mode
options.C: Crypto mode
options.D: Transport mode

questions.explanation_es: IPsec define el modo túnel, que encapsula el paquete IP completo, y el modo transporte, que cifra solo la carga útil manteniendo la cabecera IP original.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which two encryption algorithms are now considered weak and should be avoided in modern IPsec deployments?

options.A: DES
options.B: 3DES
options.C: AES-GCM
options.D: AES

questions.explanation_es: DES y 3DES tienen longitudes de clave o diseños que ya se consideran débiles frente a ataques modernos; AES y AES-GCM son los algoritmos recomendados actualmente.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: In IKEv1, which exchange negotiates the actual IPsec data-plane security association after the ISAKMP SA has already been established?

options.A: Quick mode
options.B: Main mode
options.C: CREATE_CHILD_SA
options.D: Aggressive mode

questions.explanation_es: Quick mode es el intercambio de la fase 2 de IKEv1 que negocia la SA de IPsec real de datos, apoyándose en la SA ISAKMP ya creada en la fase 1 mediante main mode o aggressive mode.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Because GRE adds extra header overhead to every encapsulated packet, which interface parameter often needs adjustment to avoid fragmentation issues along the tunnel path?

options.A: The bandwidth
options.B: The tunnel checksum
options.C: The keepalive interval
options.D: The MTU

questions.explanation_es: GRE agrega al menos 24 bytes de sobrecarga, así que a menudo hay que ajustar la MTU, o la MSS de TCP, en la interfaz de túnel para evitar fragmentación.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which IPsec security service ensures that data was not altered or tampered with while in transit?

options.A: Anti-replay protection
options.B: Peer authentication
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Data integrity

questions.explanation_es: La integridad de datos garantiza, mediante un hash, que la información no fue modificada en tránsito; la confidencialidad se logra con cifrado y es un servicio distinto.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which of the following statements about GRE tunnels is NOT actually true?

options.A: GRE has weak native security features
options.B: GRE can carry routing protocol traffic across the tunnel
options.C: GRE can encapsulate virtually any Layer 3 protocol
options.D: GRE tunnels are stateful and track the remote peer's status

questions.explanation_es: Los túneles GRE son sin estado, stateless: el extremo del túnel no mantiene información sobre la disponibilidad del extremo remoto, al contrario de lo que afirma la opcion C.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required to bring up a basic GRE tunnel?

options.A: A configured tunnel source
options.B: An IP address on the tunnel interface
options.C: A configured tunnel destination
options.D: A dynamic routing protocol running over the tunnel

questions.explanation_es: Un túnel GRE básico solo necesita dirección IP, origen y destino configurados; ejecutar un protocolo de enrutamiento dinámico sobre el túnel es opcional.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What do the transit (intermediate) routers along the underlay path between two GRE tunnel endpoints do with the tunneled traffic?

options.A: They forward the packet based only on the outer IP header
options.B: They inspect and route based on the encapsulated payload
options.C: They decapsulate the GRE header before forwarding
options.D: They re-encapsulate the packet with a new GRE header

questions.explanation_es: Los routers de tránsito solo examinan la cabecera IP exterior para reenviar el paquete hacia el destino del túnel; no procesan ni decapsulan la carga GRE interna.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which VPN technology dynamically builds IPsec tunnels between spoke sites on demand, without requiring a permanently configured tunnel to every peer?

options.A: DMVPN
options.B: A static IPsec VTI
options.C: A dedicated point-to-point GRE tunnel over IPsec
options.D: Cisco FlexVPN with only static crypto maps

questions.explanation_es: DMVPN utiliza NHRP para descubrir dinámicamente a los pares y levantar túneles IPsec spoke-to-spoke o spoke-to-hub bajo demanda, sin necesidad de túneles permanentes preconfigurados hacia cada sitio.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which Cisco VPN solution acts as a unifying framework capable of implementing site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, and remote-access VPNs under a common IKEv2-based configuration model?

options.A: GRE tunnels secured with static crypto maps
options.B: Cisco FlexVPN
options.C: Classic crypto maps
options.D: Static VTI deployments only

questions.explanation_es: Cisco FlexVPN es una solución unificada basada en IKEv2 que simplifica y consolida el despliegue de distintos tipos de VPN bajo un mismo modelo de configuración.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Built-in support for NAT traversal (NAT-T) was introduced as a native capability of which key management protocol version?

options.A: ESP
options.B: IKEv2
options.C: AH
options.D: IKEv1

questions.explanation_es: IKEv2 incorporó de forma nativa el soporte de NAT traversal, simplificando el establecimiento de túneles IPsec cuando hay dispositivos NAT en el camino.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which technology provides multi-hop path isolation, as opposed to hop-by-hop isolation, for extending virtual networks across an IP infrastructure?

options.A: Static routing between VRF instances
options.B: Per-hop VRF-Lite with subinterfaces
options.C: 802.1Q trunking
options.D: Multipoint GRE (mGRE)

questions.explanation_es: El GRE multipunto, mGRE, permite el aislamiento de rutas de múltiples saltos, a diferencia de 802.1Q, que se limita al aislamiento salto a salto entre dispositivos Capa 3 adyacentes.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which IP protocol number is used to identify GRE-encapsulated packets?

options.A: IP protocol 43
options.B: IP protocol 51
options.C: IP protocol 47
options.D: IP protocol 50

questions.explanation_es: GRE se identifica en la cabecera IP con el número de protocolo 47, distinto de ESP, que usa 50, o AH, que usa 51.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core protocols that make up the IPsec suite?

options.A: Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP)
options.B: Internet Key Exchange (IKE)
options.C: Authentication Header (AH)
options.D: Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP)

questions.explanation_es: AH, ESP e IKE son los tres protocolos principales que conforman IPsec; EAP es un marco de autenticación usado en otros contextos, como 802.1X, y no un protocolo central de IPsec.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: LISP's core design principle splits an endpoint's IP addressing into which two distinct namespaces?

options.A: Routing locators (RLOCs)
options.B: Subnet and host portions
options.C: Endpoint identifiers (EIDs)
options.D: LISP site identifiers

questions.explanation_es: LISP separa la identidad del dispositivo, EID, de su ubicación en la red, RLOC, en lugar de usar una única dirección IP para ambos propósitos.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What destination UDP port does the LISP data plane use for encapsulated traffic?

options.A: UDP 4342
options.B: UDP 4143
options.C: UDP 4341
options.D: UDP 4142

questions.explanation_es: El plano de datos de LISP encapsula el tráfico hacia el puerto UDP 4341, mientras que el plano de control, los mensajes de mapeo, usa el puerto UDP 4342.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: True or false: an ETR is the only type of device that can ever be involved in responding to a map request originated by an ITR.

options.A: True, only the authoritative ETR ever replies
options.B: False, only the Map Resolver itself replies directly with the mapping
options.C: True, because Map Servers never communicate with ITRs
options.D: False, other elements such as a Map Resolver forwarding to an ETR or a Proxy ETR can be involved in the reply path

questions.explanation_es: Aunque el ETR autoritativo suele responder, un Map Resolver puede reenviar la solicitud y un Proxy ETR puede responder en nombre de sitios no LISP, por lo que el ETR no es el único elemento involucrado en la respuesta.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In Cisco's SD-Access fabric architecture, which technology serves as the control plane for tracking endpoint location?

options.A: EIGRP
options.B: VXLAN
options.C: LISP
options.D: Multiprotocol BGP

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access usa LISP como plano de control para registrar y resolver la ubicación, RLOC, de cada endpoint, EID, dentro del fabric.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
questions.question: Which UDP port has IANA officially assigned for VXLAN traffic?

options.A: UDP 4789
options.B: UDP 4987
options.C: UDP 8472
options.D: UDP 8947

questions.explanation_es: IANA asignó oficialmente el puerto UDP 4789 para VXLAN; el puerto 8472 fue el usado inicialmente por la implementacion de Linux antes de esa asignacion oficial.

questions.name: VXLAN EVPN/BUM
